title: Take a boat across the turquoise water of Attabad Lake
description: A 2010 landslide dammed the Hunza River and drowned a stretch of the Karakoram Highway under water this shade of blue. Speedboats now cross where the old road used to run, past the submerged tops of buildings in low-water years.

title: Trace the high-altitude route towards Khunjerab Pass
description: The route from Sost climbs through Khunjerab National Park towards the China border. Australia advises reconsidering travel to Pakistan and flying, rather than driving, into Gilgit-Baltistan. Check current security advice, movement permits, road conditions and border opening before planning; this listing does not establish permission to cross.

title: Trek to K2 Base Camp through the Karakoram
description: Roughly two weeks on foot from Askole to Concordia, where four of the world's fourteen eight-thousand-metre peaks stand around you at once. Porters and permits need arranging in Skardu well ahead, this is not a walk-up trek.

title: Camp on the high plateau of Deosai National Park
description: Locals call it the Land of Giants: one of the highest plateaus on earth, carpeted in wildflowers for a few weeks each summer and home to the Himalayan brown bear. Snow closes the only access road from October to May.

title: Cross the Hussaini suspension bridge below the Passu Cones
description: Missing planks and a serious sway make this one of the more nerve-testing footbridges anyone crosses on purpose, strung over the Hunza River under a ridge of jagged rock spires. Go early morning for the light on the cones and a bridge to yourself.

title: Watch the call to prayer echo across Badshahi Mosque's courtyard
description: Built in 1673 by Aurangzeb, the courtyard alone holds around a hundred thousand worshippers and still fills for Friday prayers. Climb one of the minarets, when it's open, for a view straight down into the fort across the square.

title: See the flag lowering ceremony at the Wagah border
description: The ceremonial flag lowering is a border tradition. Australia currently advises reconsidering travel to Pakistan, avoiding crowds and remaining alert near Wagah; the Attari-Wagah crossing is closed. Crossing closure does not establish whether a ceremony operates. Confirm official spectator access and security conditions before considering a visit.

title: Eat under the fort walls on Lahore's Food Street
description: Restaurant rooftops along this pedestrianised strip face the floodlit Badshahi Mosque and fort walls, which makes it worth the markup tourists get charged over the food halls elsewhere in the old city.

title: Walk the streets of the 4,500-year-old city of Mohenjo-daro
description: One of the best-preserved cities of the Indus Valley Civilisation, laid out on a grid with covered drains centuries before Rome existed. Go in winter — Sindh's summer heat on the exposed brick site is brutal by mid-morning.

title: Stand beneath Faisal Mosque's tent-shaped roof
description: Pakistan's largest mosque skips the usual dome for a Bedouin-tent silhouette by a Turkish architect, set against the Margalla Hills. It can hold over a hundred thousand people and still feels empty on a weekday morning.

title: Drive the green switchbacks of the Swat Valley
description: Called Pakistan's Switzerland for its pine forests and river valleys, and once the heart of the Buddhist Gandhara civilisation — ruined stupas still sit above the orchards. Check the current security situation before planning a route beyond Mingora.

title: Ride a wooden launch on the Buriganga through Old Dhaka
description: Sadarghat terminal moves more river traffic than almost anywhere on earth — hire a small wooden boat for twenty minutes and watch the chaos from the water instead of the ghat. The colour and the smell both hit hardest before 9am.

title: Count the pillars inside the Sixty Dome Mosque
description: Built in the 1450s by a Turkish general, it actually has seventy-seven domes; the name comes from the sixty stone pillars holding the roof up, not a mistranslation anyone bothered to fix. Bagerhat is a long side trip from Khulna, not a Dhaka day trip.

title: Explore the unfinished Mughal fort of Lalbagh
description: Started in 1678 and never finished after the governor's daughter died here and the project was abandoned as ill-omened. Her tomb, the Pari Bibi mausoleum, is still the best-preserved building on site.

title: Climb the pyramid-shaped ruins of Paharpur monastery
description: The largest Buddhist monastery south of the Himalayas, an eighth-century complex that housed thousands of monks and now looks like a stepped brick pyramid from a distance. It's a full day's travel from Dhaka, so pair it with Bogura or stay overnight in Naogaon.

title: Snorkel the coral reef off Saint Martin's Island
description: Bangladesh's only coral island, three hours by boat from Teknaf and closed to boat traffic outside the winter season. The reef is thin compared to its neighbours but the coconut-lined beaches and the sea turtle nesting sites are the real draw.

title: Paddle through the flooded trees of Ratargul Swamp Forest
description: One of very few freshwater swamp forests left anywhere, nicknamed the Amazon of Bangladesh, only fully navigable by boat when the monsoon floods the forest floor. Come dry season and you'll mostly be looking at tree trunks in mud.

title: Cross the Shibuya scramble at rush hour
description: Up to three thousand people cross at once when the lights change. The Starbucks window above it is the free viewing gallery.

title: Get to Senso-ji before the shutters go up
description: Tokyo's oldest temple, founded in 628. At six in the morning the approach is empty and the smoke from the incense cauldron is yours alone.

title: Eat sushi for breakfast at Toyosu
description: The tuna auction moved here from Tsukiji in 2018. Viewing from the deck is free; the sushi counters upstairs open at five.

title: Walk the Meiji Jingu forest in the middle of the city
description: A hundred thousand trees donated from across Japan in 1920 and planted to become a forest. It worked.

title: Drink in a Golden Gai bar the size of a cupboard
description: Two hundred bars in six alleys, most seating five or six people. Many charge a cover; the ones that welcome visitors say so on the door.

title: Look down on Tokyo for free from the Metropolitan Building
description: Two hundred and two metres up, no charge, and on a clear winter morning Mount Fuji is visible from the north tower.

title: See the Ghibli Museum in Mitaka
description: Tickets go on sale on the tenth of the month before and sell out the same day. No photography inside, deliberately.

title: Watch a sumo morning practice
description: Stables allow a small number of visitors to sit silently at the edge of morning training. Tournaments are only six times a year; this is not.

title: Walk from Yanaka cemetery through old Shitamachi
description: One of the few districts to survive both the 1923 earthquake and the firebombing, so the wooden houses and shopping street are original.

title: Walk up through the Fushimi Inari gates at dawn
description: Ten thousand vermilion torii up a mountain, each donated by a business. Open all night; go at five and you will meet almost no one.

title: Stand under the Arashiyama bamboo before seven
description: The sound of the stalks knocking together is on Japan's official list of soundscapes to preserve, and you can only hear it early.

title: See Kinkaku-ji reflected in its pond
description: Two floors covered in gold leaf, burned down by a monk in 1950 and rebuilt. Best after snow, which Kyoto gets a few days a year.

title: Sit in front of the rock garden at Ryoan-ji
description: Fifteen stones in raked gravel, arranged so you can never see all fifteen at once from the veranda. Nobody agrees what it means.

title: Walk the Philosopher's Path in cherry blossom
description: Two kilometres of canal lined with cherry trees, named for a philosopher who walked it daily to Kyoto University.

title: Eat kaiseki in a Kyoto machiya
description: A multi-course seasonal meal that is the formal end of Japanese cooking. Book weeks ahead; many places take no walk-ins.

title: Take part in a tea ceremony properly
description: Uji has grown the country's best matcha since the twelfth century. A full ceremony runs to a script and takes real time.

title: Bow to the deer at Nara Park
description: Twelve hundred wild sika deer that will bow back if you bow first. They are wild animals and will also take your map.

title: Stand under the Great Buddha at Todai-ji
description: Fifteen metres of bronze in what was the largest wooden building in the world until 1998, and is still enormous.

title: Eat takoyaki and kushikatsu in Dotonbori
description: Osaka's word for eating yourself broke is kuidaore, and this is where it happens. Never double-dip the kushikatsu sauce.

title: Cross the floating garden at Umeda Sky Building
description: Two towers joined by a doughnut-shaped roof deck 170 metres up, reached by an escalator through open air.

title: Climb the keep at Himeji Castle
description: The finest surviving Japanese castle, never burned or bombed, with six storeys of steep wooden stairs to the top.

title: Walk the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage route
description: A thousand-year-old pilgrimage through cedar forest, and one of only two pilgrim routes in the world with world heritage status.

title: Stay overnight in a temple on Koyasan
description: Sleep in a working monastery, eat shojin ryori and attend the dawn service. Okunoin cemetery at night is the reason to stay.

title: Climb Mount Fuji overnight for the sunrise
description: The official season is barely two months. Huts must be booked, and altitude catches out people who treated it as a walk.

title: See Fuji from Lake Kawaguchi in the morning
description: The mountain hides behind cloud most summer days. Winter mornings are clear, and the reflection in the lake is why people come.

title: Watch the snow monkeys bathe at Jigokudani
description: Japanese macaques that learned to sit in a hot spring. A 1.6-kilometre walk in through snow, and the monkeys ignore you entirely.

title: Walk the Azusa river at Kamikochi
description: A closed valley in the Northern Alps with no private cars, clear water and the Hotaka range standing over it.

title: See the thatched gassho houses at Shirakawa-go
description: Steep-roofed farmhouses built to shed four metres of snow, some three hundred years old and still lived in.

title: Walk the old merchant streets of Takayama
description: Dark timber sake breweries and morning markets in a mountain town that the modern railway reached late and lightly.

title: Walk Kenroku-en in winter, when the pines hang in rope cones
description: One of Japan's three great gardens. In winter the pines are hung with rope cones to stop the snow breaking them.

title: Walk the snow corridor on the Alpine Route
description: Snow walls up to twenty metres high, cut through each spring by ploughs, on a route crossed by cable car, bus and trolley.

title: See the lavender fields of Furano
description: Hokkaido's brief summer turns these hills purple for about four weeks. The Farm Tomita fields are the ones in the photographs.

title: Ski the powder at Niseko
description: Siberian air crossing the Sea of Japan dumps fifteen metres of dry snow a season here. It is why Australians learned to ski in Japan.

title: Look for brown bears in Shiretoko
description: A peninsula at the far north-east with one of the densest brown bear populations on earth, reached mostly by boat.

title: Walk the Sapporo Snow Festival sculptures
description: Two hundred snow and ice sculptures along Odori Park each February, some of them the size of buildings.

title: Walk the beech forest of Shirakami-Sanchi
description: The last large virgin beech forest in East Asia, world heritage listed, with almost no trails through the core.

title: See the gold hall at Chuson-ji
description: A twelfth-century hall covered inside and out in gold leaf, protected within a concrete shell, in the far north.

title: Take the boat through the pines of Matsushima bay
description: Two hundred and sixty pine-covered islets, ranked one of Japan's three great views since the seventeenth century.

title: Climb the thousand steps at Yamadera
description: A temple complex up a cliff, reached by 1,015 stone steps through cedar. Basho wrote a famous haiku here about the silence.

title: Stand in the Peace Memorial Park
description: The dome was left standing as it was on 6 August 1945. The museum next to it is unsparing and should be done slowly.

title: See the Itsukushima torii at high tide
description: The gate appears to float when the tide is in and you can walk out to it when it is out. Check the tide table before the ferry.

title: Cycle the art islands of Naoshima
description: A former industrial island turned over to Tadao Ando museums and a Yayoi Kusama pumpkin on the jetty.

title: Walk the Tottori sand dunes
description: Sixteen kilometres of coastal dunes up to fifty metres high, the largest in Japan, with camels for hire at the edge.

title: Visit Izumo Taisha, where the gods gather
description: The oldest shrine in Japan, where all eight million gods are said to meet each October. You clap four times here, not two.

title: Walk part of the 88-temple Shikoku pilgrimage
description: Twelve hundred kilometres around an island, walked in white with a staff. Most people do it in sections over years.

title: Eat tonkotsu ramen at a Fukuoka yatai
description: Open-air food stalls that set up on the riverbank each evening. Fukuoka is where the pork bone broth comes from.

title: Bathe in a Beppu onsen
description: More hot spring water comes out of the ground here than anywhere on earth except Yellowstone. Tattoo rules vary; ask first.

title: Walk to the ancient cedars on Yakushima
description: Cedars up to seven thousand years old in a moss forest that rains most days. The island Princess Mononoke was drawn from.

title: Look into the Mount Aso caldera
description: One of the largest calderas in the world with a live crater at the centre. Access closes without notice on gas readings.

title: Dive the Kerama islands
description: Water clarity here has its own name, Kerama blue, and humpbacks calve in the channel between January and March.

title: Snorkel with manta rays at Ishigaki
description: Manta Scramble is a cleaning station where mantas queue up. One of the most reliable manta sites in the world.

title: Ride a water buffalo cart on Taketomi
description: A coral-walled village of red-tiled roofs and sand streets, where the whole island is under a preservation order.

title: See the Emerald Buddha at Wat Phra Kaew
description: The most sacred image in Thailand, carved from a single block of jade and dressed by the king three times a year. Cover knees and shoulders.

title: Watch the sunset from Wat Arun
description: A seventy-metre prang encrusted with broken Chinese porcelain, best seen from the far bank as the light goes.

title: Eat your way along a Bangkok street
description: Chinatown after dark, where the woks come out onto the pavement. Follow the queues of locals rather than the signs in English.

title: Take a longtail through the Thonburi canals
description: The city was built on canals before it was built on roads, and on the west bank most of them are still there.

title: Cycle the ruins of Ayutthaya
description: The capital sacked by the Burmese in 1767, left as brick stupas and a Buddha head grown into a fig tree.

title: Climb to Doi Suthep above Chiang Mai
description: Three hundred and six steps flanked by naga serpents, to a gold chedi that has been there since 1383.

title: Spend a day at an ethical elephant sanctuary
description: Rescued working elephants, no riding and no bathing shows. The distinction between sanctuaries here matters; check before booking.

title: See the white temple at Chiang Rai
description: A privately built temple in white and mirrored glass, still unfinished, with a bridge over a pit of reaching hands.

title: Ride the 762 curves to Pai
description: A mountain road with a counted number of bends, to a valley town of hot springs and canyon ridges in the far north-west.

title: Climb the limestone at Railay
description: Seven hundred bolted routes on overhanging limestone, on a peninsula reachable only by longtail boat.

title: Kayak the mangroves at Ao Thalane
description: Limestone karst rising straight out of mangrove channels, with the tide carrying you in and out. Quieter than Phang Nga.

title: Paddle into the hongs of Phang Nga Bay
description: Collapsed cave systems that form hidden lagoons inside the islands, entered lying flat in a kayak at low tide.

title: Sleep on a raft house at Cheow Lan Lake
description: Limestone towers out of an emerald reservoir, in a rainforest older than the Amazon. Hornbills at dawn, gibbons calling across the water.

title: Swim the Emerald Cave to Koh Muk
description: Eighty metres of swimming through a dark sea cave to a hidden beach inside a collapsed karst, with a rope to follow.

title: Cycle the Sukhothai historical park at dawn
description: The first Thai kingdom's capital, quieter and better preserved than Ayutthaya, with walking Buddhas in the lotus ponds.

title: Walk the old quarter's thirty-six streets
description: Each street was once a single guild's trade, and many still are. Crossing the road means walking slowly and not stopping.

title: Drink egg coffee in Hanoi
description: Invented in 1946 when milk was scarce: egg yolk whipped with condensed milk over strong coffee, served hot in a bowl of water.

title: Sleep on a boat in Bai Tu Long bay
description: The quieter half of Ha Long, with the same limestone towers and a fraction of the boats. Overnight is worth the extra day.

title: Be rowed through the caves at Trang An
description: Karst towers in flooded rice country, on a two-hour row through nine caves. The boatwomen row with their feet.

title: Ride the Ha Giang loop
description: Three hundred and fifty kilometres of mountain road along the Chinese border, through Hmong villages and the Ma Pi Leng pass.

title: Trek between the villages around Sapa
description: Rice terraces cut into the Hoang Lien Son mountains. Going with a local homestay host rather than a town agency changes the trip.

title: Go into the caves at Phong Nha
description: Home to Son Doong, the largest cave passage on earth. Paradise and Dark Cave are the accessible ones and are still vast.

title: Cycle the imperial citadel and tombs at Hue
description: The Nguyen capital, badly damaged in 1968 and slowly being restored, with emperors' tombs scattered along the Perfume River.

title: Ride the Hai Van Pass
description: Twenty-one kilometres over a spur of the Annamite range, with the weather often different on each side.

title: Have clothes made in Hoi An
description: A preserved trading port of Japanese, Chinese and French buildings, and several hundred tailors who will fit you in a day.

title: Canyon down the waterfalls at Da Lat
description: Abseiling into falls in the cool highlands the French built as a hill station. Choose the operator carefully; this one has a safety record.

title: Eat banh mi and pho on a Saigon street
description: The French left the baguette and the Vietnamese improved it. Pho in the south comes with a plate of herbs to add yourself.

title: Go down into the Cu Chi tunnels
description: Two hundred and fifty kilometres of hand-dug tunnel. A widened section is open to visitors and is still a tight squeeze.

title: Reach Cai Rang floating market at six
description: Wholesalers hang a sample of what they sell from a pole. By eight it is over, so the early boat is the only boat worth taking.

title: Watch the sun come up over Angkor Wat
description: The largest religious monument in the world. Buy the three-day pass; one day is not enough and the crowds thin after the first morning.

title: Find the faces at the Bayon
description: Two hundred and sixteen serene stone faces on fifty-four towers, at the centre of the walled city of Angkor Thom.

title: See the trees growing through Ta Prohm
description: Deliberately left partly unrestored, with silk-cotton roots prising the galleries apart. Go early; it is small and fills fast.

title: See the pink sandstone carving at Banteay Srei
description: Small, rose-coloured, and carved so finely it was long assumed to be the work of women. The best stonework at Angkor.

title: Visit Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek
description: A school turned interrogation centre, and the field where its prisoners were killed. Take the audio guide and take your time.

title: Stay in the Cardamom Mountains
description: One of the largest intact rainforests in Southeast Asia, with community-run camps funding the rangers who patrol it.

title: Taste Kampot pepper at a plantation
description: Protected by origin, nearly wiped out under the Khmer Rouge, and now grown again on the same red soil by the same families.

title: Watch the alms round at dawn in Luang Prabang
description: Hundreds of monks collect rice at first light. Watch from a distance and quietly, or do not watch at all.

title: Swim in the Kuang Si pools
description: Turquoise limestone terraces below a fifty-metre fall, with a bear rescue centre on the walk in.

title: Balloon over the Vang Vieng karsts
description: The tubing-and-buckets era is over; the town now sells sunrise balloon flights over limestone towers and rice fields.

title: Look for Irrawaddy dolphins at Si Phan Don
description: The Four Thousand Islands where the Mekong braids out, with a handful of critically endangered dolphins in one deep pool.

title: Walk the Plain of Jars
description: Thousands of stone jars two thousand years old, in a province that was the most heavily bombed place on earth. Stay on the marked paths.

title: Cross the Petronas skybridge
description: The tallest twin towers in the world, joined at the forty-first floor. Tickets are capped daily and released online.

title: Climb the steps at Batu Caves
description: Two hundred and seventy-two rainbow steps to a limestone cave temple, guarded by a forty-three metre gold statue and rude macaques.

title: Eat char kway teow in George Town
description: Malaysia's food capital, where Chinese, Malay and Indian cooking have been arguing productively for two centuries.

title: Walk the mossy forest in the Cameron Highlands
description: Tea plantations the British planted, and above them a cloud forest where everything is covered in moss and pitcher plants.

title: Climb Mount Kinabalu
description: Four thousand and ninety-five metres, climbed overnight to reach the granite summit plateau at sunrise. Permits are capped and book out.

title: Watch orphaned orangutans come in to feed at Sepilok
description: A rehabilitation centre for orphaned orangutans in Borneo, with a nursery viewing platform and feeding twice a day.

title: Dive Sipadan's wall
description: An oceanic island dropping six hundred metres, with barracuda tornadoes and turtles everywhere. Only 176 permits a day.

title: See the bat exodus at Mulu
description: Three million wrinkle-lipped bats spiral out of Deer Cave each evening in a ribbon that takes an hour to pass.

title: Snorkel with turtles at the Perhentians
description: White sand and green turtles an hour off the east coast, closed by the monsoon from November to February.

title: Walk the Supertrees at Gardens by the Bay
description: Vertical gardens up to fifty metres tall that vent the conservatories and light up twice a night. The skywalk between two of them is the view.

title: Eat at a hawker centre with a Michelin star
description: Hawker culture is UNESCO listed. Chicken rice for a few dollars, and the queue tells you which stall to join.

title: Walk the Southern Ridges tree-top bridge
description: Ten kilometres of connected parks and elevated walkways across the south of the island, with the wave bridge at the high point.

title: Look for otters along the Singapore River
description: Smooth-coated otters recolonised the city after the water was cleaned up, and now have their own celebrity families.

title: Take a water taxi through Kampong Ayer
description: A village of thirteen thousand people on stilts over the river, six hundred years old and still occupied.

title: Walk the canopy at Ulu Temburong
description: Untouched Borneo rainforest reached by longboat, with an aluminium tower taking you above the canopy.

title: Island-hop the Bacuit archipelago
description: Limestone islands with hidden lagoons you swim or kayak into. Tours are lettered A to D; C has the best lagoons.

title: Dive the Japanese wrecks at Coron
description: A dozen ships sunk by a US air raid in September 1944, most of them shallow enough to see without technical gear.

title: Paddle the underground river at Puerto Princesa
description: Eight kilometres of navigable river inside a mountain. Permits are capped daily and must be arranged in advance.

title: Walk the rice terraces at Batad
description: Two thousand years of terracing carved into the Cordillera by hand, in an amphitheatre you walk down into and back out of.

title: See the Chocolate Hills and the tarsiers
description: Over a thousand grass-covered limestone mounds that go brown in the dry season, with a tarsier sanctuary nearby.

title: Canyoneer down to Kawasan Falls
description: Three hours of jumping, sliding and swimming down a limestone canyon to a turquoise waterfall.

title: Surf Cloud 9 at Siargao
description: A hollow right-hand reef break over shallow coral, with a boardwalk out to a viewing tower above it.

title: Swim with whale sharks at Donsol
description: The interaction here is regulated and the animals are wild and unfed, which is not true of every whale shark site in the country.

title: Watch the sun rise over the Bagan plain
description: More than two thousand temples across forty square kilometres, built between the eleventh and thirteenth centuries.

title: See the leg-rowing fishermen on Inle Lake
description: Intha fishermen row standing with one leg wrapped round the oar, above floating gardens anchored to the lake bed.

title: Walk the platform at Shwedagon Pagoda
description: Ninety-nine metres of gold plate and several thousand diamonds, walked barefoot, best at dusk when the lamps come on.

title: See the Golden Rock at Kyaiktiyo
description: A gilded boulder balanced on the edge of a cliff, said to be held by a single hair of the Buddha.

title: See the Taj Mahal at sunrise
description: Twenty-two years and twenty thousand workers for one man's wife. The marble changes colour through the morning, which is the reason to be early.

title: Walk the red sandstone of Agra Fort
description: Where Shah Jahan was imprisoned by his son and spent eight years looking downriver at the tomb he had built.

title: Watch the Ganga Aarti at Varanasi
description: Fire, brass lamps and bells at dusk on the river, in one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities on earth.

title: Take a rowing boat along the ghats at dawn
description: Eighty-four ghats along the west bank, with bathing, laundry, cremation and prayer all happening within a few hundred metres.

title: Climb to Amber Fort above Jaipur
description: A hilltop fort of mirrored halls and stepped courtyards. Walk up rather than taking an elephant.

title: Look over the blue city from Mehrangarh
description: One of the largest forts in India on a 120-metre cliff, with the indigo-washed old town spread out beneath it.

title: Sleep in the dunes outside Jaisalmer
description: A living fort of yellow sandstone at the edge of the Thar, with camel treks out to the dunes for the night.

title: Row on Lake Pichola at Udaipur
description: Palaces on islands, hills behind, and the whole city built to be looked at from the water.

title: Find the stepwells of Bundi
description: Fifty ornate stepwells in a small blue town, almost none of them visited, and a palace Kipling wrote about.

title: Walk Old Delhi from the Jama Masjid
description: The largest mosque in India, then down into Chandni Chowk, which is the most concentrated street in the country.

title: See the Qutb Minar and the iron pillar
description: A 73-metre victory tower from 1193, beside an iron pillar sixteen centuries old that has never rusted.

title: Eat in the langar at the Golden Temple
description: A hundred thousand people are fed free every day by volunteers. Cover your head, remove your shoes, and take a turn washing up.

title: Drive over the Khardung La
description: One of the highest motorable passes in the world at over 5,300 metres. Acclimatise in Leh for two days before you attempt it.

title: Camp beside Pangong Tso
description: A saltwater lake at 4,350 metres that changes colour hour by hour and runs sixty per cent into Tibet.

title: Cross the Spiti valley
description: A cold desert of thousand-year-old monasteries between the Himalaya and Tibet, on roads that wash out most summers.

title: Raft the Ganges at Rishikesh
description: Grade three and four water where the river leaves the mountains, in the town the Beatles made famous in 1968.

title: Walk the Valley of Flowers in monsoon
description: Three hundred alpine species flowering at once, only during the rains, seventeen kilometres up from the road head.

title: Sleep on a Kerala backwater houseboat
description: Converted rice barges on nine hundred kilometres of lagoon and canal. The smaller canoes reach the channels the boats cannot.

title: Walk the tea estates at Munnar
description: Hills carpeted in tea to the horizon, and once every twelve years the neelakurinji flowers turn them blue. Next in 2030.

title: Watch the Chinese fishing nets at Fort Kochi
description: Cantilevered shore nets worked by teams of four, brought here by traders from Kublai Khan's court.

title: See the gopurams at Meenakshi Temple
description: Fourteen gate towers covered in thirty-three thousand painted figures, in a temple complex the size of a small town.

title: See the rock-cut caves at Ajanta and Ellora
description: Thirty-four temples cut down into solid basalt at Ellora, and Buddhist paintings at Ajanta lost in the jungle until 1819.

title: Walk to a living root bridge in Meghalaya
description: Bridges grown from rubber fig roots over decades by Khasi villagers, reached by three and a half thousand steps down.

title: Look for tigers at Bandhavgarh
description: One of the highest densities of Bengal tigers anywhere. Book the core zone and go on consecutive mornings.

title: Find the quiet beaches in south Goa
description: The north is developed; the south still has palm-backed crescents with fishing boats on them.

title: Walk the Kathmandu durbar squares
description: Three royal squares of pagoda temples across the valley, much of it rebuilt since the 2015 earthquake.

title: Walk the kora at Boudhanath
description: One of the largest stupas in the world, circled clockwise at dusk by Tibetan pilgrims turning the prayer wheels.

title: Trek to Annapurna Base Camp
description: Ten to twelve days into a glacial amphitheatre ringed by seven-thousanders, sleeping in teahouses the whole way.

title: Trek to Everest Base Camp
description: Twelve days up the Khumbu to 5,364 metres. The flight into Lukla is the part people talk about afterwards.

title: Paraglide over Phewa Lake at Pokhara
description: Thermals off the Sarangkot ridge with the Annapurnas behind, and one of the best places in the world to learn.

title: Look for rhinos in Chitwan
description: Greater one-horned rhino, gharial and occasionally tiger, in grassland and sal forest on the Indian border.

title: Climb to the Tiger's Nest
description: A monastery on a cliff ledge nine hundred metres above the valley, reached by a steep two-hour walk each way.

title: Watch a masked cham dance at a tsechu
description: Days of masked religious dance in a courtyard, attended by the whole town in their best kira and gho.

title: Walk the Bumthang valley temples
description: The spiritual heart of Bhutan, with the country's oldest temples and a daily fee that keeps visitor numbers low.

title: Climb Sigiriya rock at first light
description: Twelve hundred steps up a granite plug to a fifth-century palace, past frescoes and a gateway of giant lion's paws.

title: See the Temple of the Tooth at Kandy
description: A relic of the Buddha kept in a gold casket, shown only during the evening puja. The August perahera is the big one.

title: Ride the train from Kandy to Ella
description: Seven hours through tea country on a British-built line, with the doors open and everyone hanging out of them.

title: Climb Adam's Peak overnight
description: Five thousand steps by torchlight to a footprint claimed by four religions, and a shadow the mountain casts at sunrise.

title: Look for leopards at Yala
description: The highest density of leopards in the world, in scrub jungle where they sleep on the rocks in plain view.

title: Watch blue whales off Mirissa
description: The continental shelf comes close to shore here, so the largest animal that has ever lived passes within a few kilometres.

title: Walk the ramparts of Galle Fort at sunset
description: A Dutch colonial fort on a headland, still lived in, with the sea on three sides and cricket on the green.

title: Snorkel a house reef in the Maldives
description: Twenty-six atolls of coral rings. A resort with a good house reef gives you more time in the water than any boat trip.

title: Swim with manta rays at Hanifaru Bay
description: Currents funnel plankton into a small bay and up to two hundred mantas come to feed. Snorkelling only, and numbers are capped.

title: Stay on a local island rather than a resort
description: Guesthouses on inhabited islands have been legal since 2009, and cost a fraction of a resort. Local rules on dress apply.

title: Take a boat into the Sundarbans
description: The largest mangrove forest on earth, shared with India, and home to tigers that swim between the islands.

title: Walk the Bay of Bengal shore at Cox's Bazar
description: One hundred and twenty kilometres of unbroken sand on the Bay of Bengal, and almost entirely domestic tourism.

title: Walk the tea gardens at Srimangal
description: Bangladesh's tea capital, where they serve a seven-layer tea that stays separated in the glass.

title: See the Hunza valley in autumn
description: Apricot and poplar turning gold under seven-thousand-metre peaks, on the Karakoram Highway near the Chinese border.

title: Walk to Fairy Meadows below Nanga Parbat
description: A grass shelf facing the eight-thousand-metre Rupal face, reached by a jeep road with a reputation and then a walk.

title: See the Badshahi Mosque and Lahore Fort
description: Mughal building at its height, with a mosque courtyard that holds a hundred thousand people, facing the fort across a square.

title: Walk an unrestored stretch of the Great Wall
description: Jinshanling and Gubeikou are steep, crumbling and nearly empty, which Badaling is not.

title: Cross the Forbidden City north to south
description: Nine hundred and eighty buildings over seventy-two hectares. Tickets are capped daily and sold online with a passport number.

title: Walk the Temple of Heaven park in the morning
description: The park fills at seven with tai chi, ballroom dancing, choirs and card games. The temple is the excuse.

title: Stand in front of the Terracotta Army
description: Eight thousand figures, each with a different face, found by farmers digging a well in 1974. Pit one first, then three.

title: Cycle the Xi'an city wall
description: Fourteen kilometres of Ming wall, complete all the way round, wide enough to ride four abreast.

title: Be at the Chengdu panda base at opening, before they sleep
description: Arrive at opening; pandas are active in the cool of the morning and asleep by ten.

title: Walk the blue lakes of Jiuzhaigou
description: Travertine-dammed lakes so clear you can count the fallen trunks on the bottom, ringed by autumn forest.

title: Walk Tiger Leaping Gorge
description: Two days along a high trail above the Jinsha river, between two mountains over five thousand metres.

title: See the Yuanyang rice terraces flooded
description: Thirteen hundred years of Hani terracing, at its best when flooded in winter and reflecting the sky.

title: Walk the sandstone pillars at Zhangjiajie
description: Three thousand quartz sandstone columns in the mist, and the glass bridge over the Grand Canyon nearby if you can face it.

title: Cycle the karst country around Yangshuo
description: The limestone towers on the back of the twenty yuan note, best seen from a bike on the Yulong river road.

title: See the Mogao caves at Dunhuang
description: Four hundred and ninety-two painted grottoes on the Silk Road, a thousand years of Buddhist art sealed up until 1900.

title: Walk the Bund at night
description: Colonial banking houses on one side of the river and the Pudong skyline on the other, floodlit until eleven.

title: Walk Bukchon Hanok Village
description: Six hundred years of tiled-roof houses between two palaces, still lived in, so keep your voice down.

title: Watch the changing of the guard at Gyeongbokgung
description: Entry is free if you wear hanbok, which you can hire on the street outside, and most people do.

title: Eat at Gwangjang night market
description: Mung bean pancakes and raw beef tartare at counters that have been in the same families for generations.

title: Look into North Korea from the DMZ
description: The Joint Security Area opens and closes with the political weather. Book a licensed tour; independent access is not possible.

title: Cycle the royal tombs of Gyeongju
description: A thousand years of Silla capital, described as a museum without walls, with grass burial mounds in the middle of town.

title: Climb Hallasan on Jeju
description: South Korea's highest peak at 1,947 metres, a shield volcano with a crater lake, on an island of lava tubes and haenyeo divers.

title: Ride to the top of Taipei 101
description: The fastest lift in the world when it opened, and a 660-tonne steel damper ball you can walk around near the top.

title: Walk Jiufen old street in the rain
description: A gold-mining town of red lanterns and tea houses on a steep hillside above the sea. Better wet and out of season.

title: Walk the marble gorge at Taroko
description: Nineteen kilometres of marble canyon cut by the Liwu river. Check for closures; typhoons and quakes shut trails regularly.

title: Cycle the East Rift Valley
description: A hundred and eighty kilometres between two mountain ranges, through rice and indigenous villages on Taiwan's quiet side.

title: Ride the Alishan forest railway to the sunrise
description: A narrow-gauge line built by the Japanese for cypress logging, now climbing through three climate zones to a sea of cloud.

title: Ride the Star Ferry across the harbour
description: Running since 1888 and still the cheapest and best way to see the skyline. Sit on the lower deck.

title: Walk the Dragon's Back ridge
description: Forty minutes from Central to a ridge trail over the south coast. Three quarters of Hong Kong is countryside.

title: Eat dim sum from a trolley
description: Old-style tea houses where you flag down the trolley and stamp your own card. Go before eleven and share a table.

title: Take the tram to Victoria Peak early
description: The Peak Tram has run since 1888. The free circular walk around the summit is better than the paid viewing deck.

title: Walk from the ruins of St Paul's to Senado Square
description: A Portuguese church facade standing alone after an 1835 fire, and a world heritage old town behind it.

title: Eat a Macanese egg tart and pork chop bun
description: Four centuries of Portuguese and Cantonese cooking crossed into a cuisine that exists nowhere else.

title: See the Gandan monastery in Ulaanbaatar
description: A twenty-six metre gold Buddha rebuilt in 1996, in the one monastery Stalin's purges left standing.

title: Stay in a ger with a herding family
description: The valley where Genghis Khan's capital stood. Staying with herders is the normal way to travel here, not a novelty.

title: Ride a camel over the Khongoryn Els
description: Singing sand dunes up to three hundred metres high in the Gobi, near the cliffs where the first dinosaur eggs were found.

title: See the eagle hunters of Bayan-Olgii
description: Kazakh hunters flying golden eagles from horseback in the far west, with a festival each October.

title: Skate at Medeu above Almaty
description: The highest Olympic-size ice rink in the world at 1,691 metres, where dozens of world records were set.

title: Walk the Charyn canyon
description: Eighty kilometres of red rock canyon, often compared to Arizona, three hours from Almaty on the Chinese border road.

title: Look down on the drowned spruce forest of Lake Kaindy
description: Spruce trunks standing dead and upright out of a lake formed by a 1911 earthquake, preserved by the cold water.

title: Stand in the Registan at Samarkand
description: Three madrasas facing a square, tiled in blue, and the single most impressive thing on the Silk Road.

title: Walk the Shah-i-Zinda avenue of tombs
description: A narrow street of eleven mausoleums, each tiled differently, built over eight centuries.

title: Walk the old town of Bukhara
description: A working Silk Road city rather than a monument: trading domes, a minaret Genghis Khan spared, and a pool in the centre.

title: Sleep inside the walls of Khiva
description: A walled desert town preserved almost whole, small enough to walk around the ramparts in an hour.

title: Drink tea and have your ears cleaned at Heming Teahouse
description: A bamboo-chair teahouse inside People's Park, where the park costs nothing and a cup is topped up from a long-spouted kettle all afternoon. The ear cleaners with their tuning-fork tools are part of the scene - agree the price first.

title: Set foot in all eight states and territories together
description: The big one. Six states and two territories - tick it off properly, with a photo in each.

title: Drive across the Nullarbor
description: 1,200km between Ceduna and Norseman, including the longest straight stretch of road in Australia at 146.6km. Carry water and watch the fuel gaps.

title: Drive the Explorer's Way from Adelaide to Darwin
description: 3,000km from the Southern Ocean to the Timor Sea, through the Flinders, Coober Pedy, the Red Centre and the Top End.

title: Ride The Ghan from end to end
description: Adelaide to Darwin over about 54 hours, named for the Afghan cameleers who ran the inland routes before the railway.

title: Ride the Indian Pacific coast to coast
description: Sydney to Perth across four days, including the 478km dead-straight Nullarbor section - the longest stretch of straight railway on earth.

title: See sunrise on the east coast and sunset on the west, same day
description: The time difference makes it just possible - dawn at Cape Byron, a flight west, and the sun going down over the Indian Ocean the same evening.

title: Swim in the Pacific, the Indian and the Southern Ocean
description: Three different oceans touch this continent. Bondi, Cottesloe and anywhere along the South Australian or Victorian coast will do it.

title: See a platypus in the wild
description: Harder than it sounds - they are shy, mostly crepuscular, and easy to mistake for a ripple. Eungella and Tidbinbilla are the best odds.

title: Find a wild echidna in the bush
description: Australia's most widespread native mammal and still a genuine thrill to stumble across. Watch the roadsides on warm days after rain.

title: Watch whales on the east coast and the west coast
description: Humpbacks run up both sides of the continent every winter - Hervey Bay on one side, Exmouth or Albany on the other.

title: Stand in falling snow in Australia
description: Australia has more alpine snow country than Switzerland in a good year. Thredbo, Falls Creek or kunanyi will all deliver it.

title: Spend a night somewhere with no phone reception
description: Not difficult in this country, and worth doing deliberately at least once. Tell someone where you are going first.

title: See the core of the Milky Way with no light pollution
description: The galactic core sits high in southern skies from about April to September. Warrumbungle, Arkaroola or anywhere in the Centre.

title: Photograph a Big Thing in every state
description: There are more than 150 of them - Banana, Koala, Merino, Lobster, Pineapple. A genuinely stupid and genuinely great national tradition.

title: Visit a World Heritage site in every state and territory
description: Australia has twenty World Heritage properties, and at least one in every state and territory - Uluru, Kakadu, the Reef, Naracoorte, Port Arthur, Purnululu.

title: Stand on the highest point of a state or territory
description: Kosciuszko is the easy one at 2,228m. Bimberi, Ossa, Bogong, Zeil, Bartle Frere and Meharry get progressively harder.

title: Watch a footy game in a state that isn't yours
description: AFL at the MCG or Adelaide Oval, NRL in Brisbane or Sydney - the code changes at the border and so does the entire atmosphere.

title: Canoe on Moraine Lake in Banff
description: Rock flour suspended in glacial meltwater gives that colour. Private vehicles are now banned on the Moraine Lake road - shuttle only.

title: Drive the Icefields Parkway to Jasper
description: 232km past more than 100 glaciers between Lake Louise and Jasper - routinely called one of the great drives anywhere.

title: Stargaze in Jasper's Dark Sky Preserve
description: One of the largest accessible dark sky preserves in the world, with a decent chance of aurora on clear winter nights.

title: Walk the sea floor at Hopewell Rocks
description: The highest tides on earth, up to 16m. You walk on the ocean floor at low tide and kayak over the same spot six hours later.

title: Drive the Cabot Trail in autumn
description: 298km around Cape Breton's highlands, through Acadian and Gaelic communities, at its best when the maples turn in early October.

title: Ride a tundra buggy among the polar bears at Churchill
description: Bears gather here waiting for Hudson Bay to freeze. There is no road in - you arrive by train or plane, and go out in a tundra buggy.

title: Visit the Watchmen sites on Haida Gwaii
description: Standing mortuary poles at SGang Gwaay, guarded by Haida Watchmen and deliberately left to return to the earth. Access is permitted and limited.

title: Take the boat under Horseshoe Falls
description: Around 2,800 cubic metres a second go over the Horseshoe. The Canadian side has the view; the boat gets you into the spray.

title: Walk the walled old town of Quebec City
description: The only walled city north of Mexico, founded 1608, and the most convincingly European place in North America.

title: Drive the Dempster Highway to the Arctic Ocean
description: Around 900km of gravel from Dawson City to Tuktoyaktuk on the Arctic Ocean. Carry two spare tyres - this is not an exaggeration.

title: Cycle the Stanley Park seawall
description: A 9km flat loop around a 400-hectare forest on a downtown peninsula, past totem poles and under the Lions Gate Bridge.

title: Cross the Capilano Suspension Bridge
description: 137m of swaying cedar plank 70m above a river gorge, first strung across in 1889. The free Lynn Canyon bridge nearby does much the same job.

title: Eat your way around Granville Island Public Market
description: An industrial sandbar turned market and artist quarter under a bridge, reached by tiny rainbow-coloured ferries that hold about twelve people.

title: Drive the Sea to Sky Highway to Whistler
description: 120km along Howe Sound with the water on one side and granite on the other, past Shannon Falls and the Stawamus Chief.

title: Climb the Stawamus Chief at Squamish
description: One of the largest granite monoliths in the world, climbed by chains and ladders to three summits above Howe Sound.

title: Hike to the Joffre Lakes
description: Three stacked glacial lakes in improbable turquoise. Day passes are required, and the park now closes for periods so Lil'wat and N'Quatqua Nations can harvest.

title: Ride the Peak 2 Peak gondola at Whistler
description: The largest ski resort in North America, linked by a gondola with the longest unsupported span in the world at over 3km between towers.

title: Storm-watch at Tofino in winter
description: People book rooms specifically to watch Pacific storms hit Long Beach. Surfing here happens year-round in a thick wetsuit.

title: Walk the rainforest trails in Pacific Rim National Park
description: Old-growth Sitka spruce and western red cedar on boardwalks over bog, with the West Coast Trail running south for 75 gruelling kilometres.

title: See the Butchart Gardens near Victoria
description: Built inside an exhausted limestone quarry from 1904 onward by the cement magnate's wife, and now a national historic site.

title: Look for the spirit bear in the Great Bear Rainforest
description: The Kermode bear is a white-coated black bear found almost nowhere else - maybe 400 exist. Access is through First Nations-led operators only.

title: Taste ice wine in the Okanagan Valley
description: Canada's warmest wine region, on a desert lake, and the source of most of the world's ice wine - pressed from grapes frozen on the vine.

title: Paddle to Emerald Lake in Yoho
description: Takakkaw Falls drops 254m in the same park, and the Burgess Shale here holds the best-preserved Cambrian fossils found anywhere.

title: Canoe on Lake Louise beneath the Victoria Glacier
description: Get there before seven or the car park is full by eight. In winter the lake freezes hard enough to skate and they carve an ice castle on it.

title: Walk on the Athabasca Glacier at the Columbia Icefield
description: The largest icefield in the Rockies, feeding three oceans. Markers along the approach road show where the glacier stood each decade - it is a sobering walk.

title: Ride the gondola at Banff for the Bow Valley view
description: Up Sulphur Mountain to a boardwalk along the summit ridge, with hot springs at the bottom that started the whole national park system in 1885.

title: See the dinosaur collection at the Royal Tyrrell Museum
description: One of the largest dinosaur collections in the world, in Drumheller, because the badlands around it are among the richest fossil beds anywhere.

title: Walk the hoodoos at Dinosaur Provincial Park
description: World Heritage listed, and more than 400 dinosaur skeletons have come out of it - many still lie exposed where they eroded out.

title: Stand at the cliff of Head-Smashed-In Buffalo Jump
description: Blackfoot peoples drove bison off this cliff for nearly 6,000 years. The interpretive centre is built into the hillside and told from their perspective.

title: Walk the Red Rock Canyon in Waterton Lakes
description: Joined to Montana's Glacier as the world's first International Peace Park, where prairie runs straight into mountain with no foothills between.

title: Go to the Calgary Stampede
description: Ten days of rodeo, chuckwagon racing and pancake breakfasts every July, with the whole city in boots. Running since 1912.

title: Hear the silence in Grasslands National Park
description: A Dark Sky Preserve of mixed-grass prairie with reintroduced bison and black-tailed prairie dogs, and almost no light or noise for a hundred kilometres.

title: Snorkel with beluga whales at Churchill
description: Around 57,000 belugas move into the Churchill River estuary each summer. They are curious enough to come and inspect a snorkeller.

title: Do the EdgeWalk on the CN Tower
description: A hands-free walk on a 1.5m ledge around the outside of the tower at 356m, tethered to an overhead rail. The tallest such walk in the world.

title: Swim at the Grotto on the Bruce Peninsula
description: A limestone sea cave on Georgian Bay with water clear enough to be mistaken for the Caribbean, and roughly ten degrees colder than it looks.

title: Canoe and portage through Algonquin Park
description: 2,400 lakes linked by portage, with wolf howls answered on organised August nights and maples that turn the whole park red in late September.

title: Skate the Rideau Canal in Ottawa
description: 7.8km of frozen canal used as a commuter route, with beavertail pastry stands on the ice. Warming winters mean some years it barely opens at all.

title: Cruise the Thousand Islands
description: Actually 1,864 islands in the St Lawrence, split between Canada and the US - one holds the shortest international bridge in the world.

title: Eat a smoked meat sandwich and a bagel in Montreal
description: Boiled in honey water and baked in a wood oven, the Montreal bagel is a genuinely different thing from the New York version - and locals will explain why.

title: Walk up Mont Royal for the city view
description: Designed by Frederick Law Olmsted, who also did Central Park. Sunday afternoons in summer bring the tam-tams - an open drum circle on the east slope.

title: Stand at the foot of Montmorency Falls
description: 83m, higher than Niagara, with a suspension bridge across the lip and a via ferrata up the cliff beside it.

title: Watch belugas in the Saguenay Fjord
description: One of the longest fjords in the world outside Scandinavia, with a resident and endangered beluga population, plus blue whales at the confluence.

title: Walk to Perce Rock at low tide
description: A 400m limestone wall with an arch through it, walkable from shore at low tide, with the world's most accessible gannet colony on the island beyond.

title: Photograph the lighthouse at Peggy's Cove
description: A working fishing village on granite scoured bare by glaciers. People are swept off the black rocks near the water most years - stay on the light-coloured stone.

title: Walk the painted waterfront at Lunenburg
description: A World Heritage town laid out on a 1753 British grid, still in its original wooden buildings, and home port of the schooner on the Canadian dime.

title: Visit Green Gables on Prince Edward Island
description: The farmhouse that inspired Anne of Green Gables, on an island of red sand cliffs where the book still drives a good part of the economy.

title: Walk on the earth's mantle at the Tablelands
description: Peridotite from the earth's mantle, forced to the surface by continental collision. So toxic to plants that it looks like Mars - and it helped prove plate tectonics.

title: Boat into Western Brook Pond
description: A landlocked fjord with 600m walls, reached by a 3km bog walk before the boat. The water is so pure it barely conducts electricity.

title: Watch icebergs drift past Iceberg Alley
description: Ice calved off Greenland glaciers 10,000 years ago, drifting down the Labrador Current. Locals chip it out for gin, and there is a public tracking map.

title: Stand among the puffins at Elliston
description: One of the closest land-based puffin viewing sites in North America - the birds nest on a stack a few metres from where you stand.

title: See the Norse settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows
description: The only confirmed Norse site in North America, occupied around 1021 CE - five hundred years before Columbus, and dated precisely by a solar storm.

title: Climb Signal Hill above St John's
description: Where Marconi received the first transatlantic wireless signal in 1901, above a harbour entrance called the Narrows and a street of painted row houses.

title: Drink the Sourtoe cocktail in Dawson City
description: A gold rush town with wooden boardwalks and a bar that drops a mummified human toe into your drink. The rule is your lips must touch it.

title: Fly over the Kluane icefields
description: Canada's highest peak and the largest non-polar icefield on earth, almost none of it reachable on foot. The flightseeing run is the only realistic way in.

title: Raft past Virginia Falls in Nahanni
description: One of the first four sites ever added to the World Heritage list, in 1978. Virginia Falls is twice the height of Niagara, and access is by float plane only.

title: Watch the aurora from Yellowknife
description: Directly under the auroral oval with a flat horizon and very dry winter air - statistically among the most reliable aurora viewing anywhere on earth.

title: Reach the floe edge on Baffin Island
description: The line where sea ice meets open water, travelled by snowmobile and qamutik sled with Inuit guides - narwhal, bowhead and polar bear all use it.

title: Walk out onto the sea ice from Iqaluit
description: Frobisher Bay freezes solid enough to drive on, and spring is when the light comes back and the town goes out onto it.

title: Watch narwhal at the floe edge
description: Where the fast ice meets open water, narwhal and bowhead gather. You camp on the ice with Inuit guides who read it for you.

title: Walk into Auyuittuq and Mount Thor
description: Mount Thor has the greatest vertical drop on earth at 1,250 metres, most of it overhanging. Registration with Parks Canada is compulsory.

title: See Kinngait printmaking where it began
description: The co-operative here has produced Inuit prints since 1959 and is the reason the art is known worldwide.

title: Fly into Virginia Falls on the Nahanni
description: Twice the height of Niagara, in a canyon system reachable only by float plane. The first natural site ever added to the world heritage list.

title: Look for whooping cranes in Wood Buffalo
description: The largest national park in Canada and the only nesting ground of the whooping crane, which was down to 21 birds in 1941.

title: Ice road across Great Slave Lake
description: Public roads ploughed onto metre-thick lake ice each winter, with a posted weight limit and a speed limit set to stop the ice waving.

title: Walk the red cliffs of PEI National Park
description: Iron in the sandstone turns the cliffs and the sand red, against water warmer than anywhere else north of the Carolinas.

title: Eat oysters and mussels where they are farmed
description: Malpeque oysters come from a bay twenty minutes away, and PEI grows about eighty per cent of North America's cultivated mussels.

title: See Green Gables and the surrounding shore
description: The farmhouse that gave Montgomery the setting, with the Haunted Wood and Lover's Lane walks she used by name.

title: Drive to North Cape and the reef
description: The longest natural rock reef in North America runs out from the tip, walkable at low tide, with a wind test site above it.

title: Kayak among the Hopewell stacks at high tide
description: Six hours after walking the sea floor you can paddle sixteen metres above the same ground. Nowhere else changes that much twice a day.

title: Walk the Fundy Footpath
description: Forty-one kilometres of coastal wilderness with river crossings timed to the tide, and a reputation as the hardest trail in the Maritimes.

title: Watch the Reversing Falls change direction
description: The tide is strong enough to push the Saint John River backwards through a gorge. Published times tell you when it turns.

title: Eat and dance at an Acadian kitchen party
description: The Acadians were deported in 1755 and came back. The Tintamarre each August is thousands of people making noise about it.

title: Stargaze at Cypress Hills dark sky preserve
description: Hills the ice sheets went round rather than over, so the ecology is unlike the prairie below, and the sky is protected.

title: Paddle to Grey Owl's cabin
description: Twenty kilometres of paddling and portage to the cabin where an Englishman who claimed to be Ojibwe wrote about conservation in the 1930s.

title: Walk the Meewasin Valley along the river
description: Sixty kilometres of free trail along the South Saskatchewan, with seven bridges and the Bessborough hotel on the bank.

title: Fly in by float plane to the Athabasca sand dunes
description: The most northerly major dune field in the world, a hundred kilometres of sand on a lake shore reachable only by float plane.

title: Walk the Forks and the human rights museum
description: Six thousand years of meeting at the junction of two rivers, with a museum built to argue rather than to reassure.

title: Watch bison at Riding Mountain
description: An escarpment island of forest above the farmland, with an enclosed plains bison herd and a lake town in the middle of the park.

title: Look for whales off Brier Island
description: Fundy tides push nutrients up where the bay meets the Gulf of Maine, and humpbacks and right whales feed on the result.

title: Soak at Takhini hot springs under the aurora
description: Forty-two degree water outdoors at minus thirty, with a hair-freezing contest each winter that people take seriously.

title: Ride a 1950s American car through Havana
description: Kept running for seventy years on improvised parts after the 1962 embargo cut off imports. Habana Vieja around them is World Heritage listed.

title: Ride through the tobacco fields of Vinales
description: Limestone mogotes rising straight out of a valley farmed by ox and plough, producing the tobacco that goes into Cuba's best cigars.

title: Walk the cobbled streets of Trinidad
description: A sugar-boom town frozen since the 1850s, with pastel houses, a live-music staircase every night, and steam trains into the Valle de los Ingenios.

title: Climb Dunn's River Falls
description: 180m of travertine terraces climbed hand-in-hand in a human chain, with the sea right at the bottom of them.

title: Walk the Blue Mountain Peak trail for sunrise
description: A 2am start to 2,256m, where on a clear morning you can see Cuba. The coffee grown on these slopes is among the most expensive in the world.

title: Visit the Bob Marley Museum in Kingston
description: His home and studio at 56 Hope Road, kept as it was, with the bullet holes from the 1976 assassination attempt still in the wall.

title: Swim with the pigs at Big Major Cay
description: Feral pigs that swim out to meet boats on an uninhabited cay. Nobody agrees how they got there, and overfeeding has killed several - follow the guides.

title: Dive the blue holes of Andros
description: The largest concentration of blue holes on earth, inland and offshore, beside the third-longest barrier reef in the world.

title: Watch humpbacks in Samana Bay
description: Thousands of North Atlantic humpbacks come here to breed each winter - one of the largest and most reliable gatherings anywhere.

title: Swim at Bahia de las Aguilas
description: 8km of undeveloped white sand inside a national park, reached by boat or a rough track - and protected from resort building so far.

title: Kayak the bioluminescent bay at Mosquito Bay
description: The brightest recorded bioluminescent bay in the world - dinoflagellates light up around the paddle. Go on a new moon, and never with sunscreen on.

title: Walk to La Mina Falls in El Yunque
description: The only tropical rainforest in the US national forest system, full of coqui frogs whose call is on every Puerto Rican recording ever made.

title: Walk the walls of Old San Juan
description: Blue cobblestones cast from iron ballast, and El Morro - a six-level fortress that held off Drake and stood for four centuries.

title: Swim with turtles off Carlisle Bay
description: A marine park with six shipwrecks in shallow water and a resident hawksbill turtle population, right off the capital.

title: Go down into Harrison's Cave
description: A limestone cavern toured by electric tram, with a 12m waterfall inside it and stalactites still actively forming.

title: Play mas at Trinidad Carnival
description: The carnival that soca and steelpan came from, and the template most Caribbean carnivals copy. J'ouvert starts at 4am covered in mud and paint.

title: Snorkel the Buccoo Reef and Nylon Pool
description: A protected reef with a waist-deep sandbar pool a kilometre offshore, named by Princess Margaret for water she said was clear as nylon.

title: Climb Gros Piton
description: 770m of volcanic plug straight up out of the sea, guided only. The two Pitons together are the most recognisable silhouette in the Caribbean.

title: Bathe in the sulphur springs at Soufriere
description: Billed as the world's only drive-in volcano - a collapsed caldera you drive into, with mud baths people coat themselves in.

title: Walk to the Boiling Lake in Dominica
description: The second largest hot lake on earth, at the end of six hours through the Valley of Desolation. The Nature Isle has 365 rivers and almost no beaches.

title: Swim with sperm whales off Dominica
description: Resident family groups live off this coast year-round, and Dominica is one of the only countries to license in-water encounters with them.

title: Stand in the shallows at Stingray City
description: Southern stingrays gather on a waist-deep sandbar in the North Sound, a habit that started when fishermen cleaned their catch there decades ago.

title: Snorkel the wall at Grace Bay
description: Repeatedly voted the best beach in the world, protected by a barrier reef so there is no seaweed and almost no swell.

title: Find the natural pool in Arikok National Park
description: A desert island of cacti and divi-divi trees bent permanently by the trade winds, with a rock-enclosed tidal pool reachable only by 4WD or on foot.

title: Walk Nelson's Dockyard at English Harbour
description: The only continuously working Georgian naval dockyard in the world, built by enslaved labour and now World Heritage listed.

title: Dive the underwater sculpture park off Grenada
description: The world's first underwater sculpture park, installed in 2006 to draw divers away from reefs damaged by Hurricane Ivan - and now a reef itself.

title: Squeeze through The Baths on Virgin Gorda
description: House-sized granite boulders forming tidal grottoes and passages you scramble and swim through between two beaches.

title: Follow the underwater trail at Trunk Bay
description: A marked snorkelling trail with underwater signs identifying the coral, in a national park covering roughly two thirds of St John.

title: Climb to the Citadelle Laferriere
description: The largest fortress in the Americas, built after independence by the world's first free Black republic to repel a French return that never came.

title: Peer into the crater lake at Poas Volcano
description: Entry is capped and must be booked online for a specific time slot - turn up without one and you're turned away at the gate. The lake is one of the most acidic on earth and the park closes within minutes if gas readings spike.

title: Swim beneath La Fortuna waterfall
description: 500 concrete steps down a cliff face to a 70m fall you can swim beneath, then the same 500 back up in tropical heat. The current at the base is stronger than it looks - stay inside the roped swimming area.

title: Hike to the turquoise water of Rio Celeste
description: The colour is pure chemistry, not paint or dye - an optical effect from particle size where two clear, colourless rivers of different mineral content meet. Swimming is banned to protect it, so bring a rain jacket instead of togs.

title: Stand in the moonscape crater of Irazu Volcano
description: The country's highest volcano, barren enough at the top to be nicknamed the moonscape. Arrive before 10am - cloud rolls in most days by late morning and the view of both oceans from the summit disappears.

title: Drive the Orosi Valley loop past coffee farms and colonial ruins
description: The country's oldest surviving church, coffee farms ringing a volcanic crater, and the Ujarras ruins half-swallowed by jungle since a flood destroyed the town in 1833 - an hour from the capital and largely ignored by it.

title: Raft the Pacuare River whitewater
description: Consistently rated one of the best whitewater runs on the planet, Class III-IV through a roadless gorge - some lodges along it can only be reached by raft, so the trip out is the only way home.

title: Glide above the canopy on the Braulio Carrillo aerial tram
description: A ski-lift-style gondola through primary rainforest canopy that no footpath could reach without cutting a scar through it - built by one of the biologists behind Iguazu's walkway system.

title: Follow cacao to chocolate at Tirimbina
description: Costa Rica exported cacao a century before coffee ever arrived. The tour crosses a hanging bridge over the Sarapiqui River and ends with a bar you helped roast - stains your hands and changes what you think chocolate is supposed to taste like.

title: Walk the mud pots and hot springs of Rincon de la Vieja
description: Bubbling sulphur pots, a hidden waterfall and natural hot springs inside an active volcano's national park. The summit trail closes for months at a stretch whenever activity rises - check before you build a trip around it.

title: Watch the olive ridley arribada at Ostional
description: Tens of thousands of turtles crawl ashore over two or three nights each lunar cycle, in numbers so dense that later arrivals dig up earlier nests. It's one of the few beaches on earth where locals are legally permitted to harvest a share of the eggs, which funds the patrols protecting the rest.

title: Surf Witch's Rock at Playa Naranjo
description: Reachable only by boat or a rough hour of 4WD track through Santa Rosa National Park, the wave that closed Endless Summer II is still one of the world's few great breaks with no beachfront development anywhere in sight.

title: Walk the crushed-shell sand of Playa Conchal
description: The sand here is crushed shell rather than quartz, which gives it a coarse sparkle underfoot and means it never gets uncomfortably hot at midday the way the beaches either side of it do.

title: Spot sloths on the trails of Manuel Antonio
description: The country's smallest national park and its most visited, packing sloths and squirrel monkeys onto trails that end at a beach once ranked among the best in the world by National Geographic. Book entry online - daily numbers are capped and it sells out in high season.

title: Dive Isla del Cano from Drake Bay
description: A biological reserve 20km offshore with the best visibility on the Pacific coast, and the usual jump-off point for exploring Corcovado without hiking in - Drake Bay itself still has no reliable road connection in wet season.

title: Walk the whale-tail sandbar at Marino Ballena
description: A sandbar shaped exactly like a whale's tail, walkable only at low tide, in a park that gets humpback whales from two different hemispheres migrating through in different halves of the year - one of the longest whale seasons anywhere on earth.

title: Learn to surf at Jaco
description: The closest real surf beach to San Jose, which makes it the easiest place in the country to learn - consistent beach breaks, boards for rent on every corner, and a two-hour drive instead of a flight.

title: Ride to the twin pools of Nauyaca Waterfalls
description: A two-tiered fall on private ranch land reached by horseback or 4WD, with a swimming pool at the base that locals still consider a well-kept alternative to the crowds at La Fortuna.

title: Walk the free reef trail at Cahuita
description: One of the only national parks in the country with no entry fee - it runs on donations instead. Sloths and howler monkeys hang over the beach trail, and the reef just offshore is the best snorkelling on the Caribbean side.

title: Watch the reef break at Salsa Brava
description: A wave that breaks hard over a shallow reef a few hundred metres offshore, named for how it 'slaps' surfers who misjudge it. Advanced only - the town's other breaks nearby are far more forgiving.

title: Explore the untouched coast of Gandoca-Manzanillo
description: The last stretch of undeveloped Caribbean coast in the country, where the road simply ends and a rainforest trail takes over - howler monkeys and sloths overhead, and manatees in the lagoons behind the beach.

title: Wander the balconies of Casco Viejo
description: Panama City's original quarter, built after pirates burned the first site to the ground in 1671. Restored blocks of French balconies and rooftop bars sit one street away from blocks still waiting their turn.

title: Tour a geisha coffee farm in Boquete
description: A cool-climate highland town growing some of the most expensive coffee on earth - geisha varietals from a single Boquete farm have sold at auction for over $100 a pound.

title: Climb Volcan Baru overnight for sunrise
description: Panama's only volcano and highest point, climbed through the night to crest 3,474m for sunrise - on a clear morning it's the one spot on earth where you can see both the Pacific and the Caribbean at once.

title: Canoe up the Chagres River to an Embera village
description: Reached by dugout canoe up the same river system that feeds the Panama Canal's fresh water, to a village that runs on solar power and still paints visitors with temporary jagua tattoos the way it always has.

title: Dive the sharks and rays of Coiba
description: A former penal colony left alone for decades because nobody but prisoners was allowed near it - now one of the last places in the eastern Pacific with real numbers of sharks and rays.

title: Walk the Spanish forts at Portobelo
description: Forts guarding the harbour where the silver of the entire Peruvian empire was loaded for Spain. Once a year a life-size Black Christ statue is carried through the streets by purple-robed devotees fulfilling vows.

title: Surf the point break at Santa Catalina
description: A fishing village with one of the best right-hand point breaks in Central America, and the usual launch point for boats into Coiba - most surfers only meant to stay a few days and are still there months later.

title: Island hop the Pearl Islands from Contadora
description: The pearl-fishing islands that reputedly supplied Spain's crown jewels, a 20-minute flight from the capital, with a swimmable beach on one side and whales passing close inshore on the other in season.

title: Wander the market inside the crater at El Valle de Anton
description: A town built inside the second-largest inhabited volcanic crater on earth, with a Sunday market and a golden frog now extinct in the wild almost everywhere else.

title: Get soaked at Las Tablas carnival
description: Panama's biggest carnival, split between two rival streets that douse each other and the crowd with water-cannon trucks every afternoon before the real parade starts at night.

title: Snorkel the Zapatillas Cays
description: Two uninhabited cays inside Bastimentos National Marine Park that look like a stock photo of a desert island, because they were used as one - a season of Survivor filmed here.

title: Bird Pipeline Road in Soberania
description: Held the world record for most bird species recorded in 24 hours for over three decades. A rutted track through old rainforest 40 minutes from a capital city, named for the historic pipeline it still runs alongside.

title: Enter the Darien wilderness with a Wounaan guide
description: One of the last true wildernesses in the Americas and the only gap in the Pan-American Highway, entered legally and safely only with an indigenous Wounaan or Embera guide arranged in advance - and unrelated to the migrant trail on the Colombian side.

title: Hike Indian Nose for sunrise over Lake Atitlan
description: Guides leave San Pedro by headlamp around 4am so you're on the ridge before first light - the profile the peak is named for only reads clearly from the water far below. Bring a jacket, it's genuinely cold at altitude before the sun clears the volcanoes.

title: Kayak the crater lake from San Pedro La Laguna
description: Lake Atitlan fills a volcanic caldera nearly 300 metres deep, and the water is glassy at dawn and choppy by early afternoon once the Xocomil wind picks up - paddle out before 11am or plan to fight a headwind home.

title: Watch natural dyes made at a San Juan weaving cooperative
description: Women's weaving cooperatives here still dye cotton with cochineal insects, indigo and avocado pits rather than synthetic dye, and demonstrate the whole process before you buy - a different pitch entirely to the market stalls in Panajachel.

title: Trek multiple days through jungle to El Mirador's pyramids
description: No road reaches it - the only ways in are a five-day round-trip hike or a helicopter charter, to a pyramid complex larger than anything at Tikal that almost nobody visiting Guatemala this year will ever see. Mule-supported camping trips need booking weeks ahead in dry season.

title: Watch sunset from Yaxha's temple over the lagoon
description: Smaller and far quieter than Tikal, with a temple platform looking over Laguna Yaxha where howler monkeys start calling right as the sun drops - a Survivor season filmed its closing scenes here, but most afternoons it's nearly empty.

title: Bargain the stalls at Chichicastenango market
description: One of the largest indigenous markets in the Americas, but it only reaches full size on Thursdays and Sundays - arrive on any other day and half the plaza is empty stalls. Photographing the syncretic rituals on the church steps out front without asking causes real offence.

title: Tour a working coffee finca outside Antigua
description: Guatemala's volcanic soil and altitude produce some of the world's most prized arabica, and the harvest tours run only from November through February - visit outside that window and there are no cherries left on the trees to see picked.

title: Roast marshmallows on hot lava rock at Pacaya
description: The most active and most climbed volcano in the country, close enough to the capital for a half-day trip - the hardened black rock near the summit stays warm enough underfoot to toast a marshmallow on a stick, no fire required.

title: Watch the bat exodus from Lanquin's caves at dusk
description: A river runs straight through the cave mouth, lit for a stretch by hanging bulbs before the path turns to candlelight only. Time it for dusk and hundreds of thousands of bats stream out overhead on their way to feed.

title: Hike to the perfectly round jungle lake at Laguna Lachua
description: A near-perfect circle of water inside dense rainforest, reached by a 4km trail from the ranger station with no road access and no development anywhere on the shore. Park-run cabins are the only place to stay and need booking directly with the reserve.

title: Boat through the limestone gorge of Rio Dulce
description: The river narrows into a canyon of hanging jungle and hot sulphur springs bubbling straight out of the cliff face at Aguas Calientes, on the same run boats take between Livingston and the Rio Dulce town bridge.

title: Eat tapado in the Garifuna town of Livingston
description: Reachable only by boat, never by road, with a Garifuna culture, language and coconut-milk seafood stew found nowhere else in the country. Punta drumming on the beach after dark is unannounced and just happens.

title: Swim beneath a hot waterfall at Finca El Paraiso
description: A thermal river drops straight into a cool jungle pool, so the temperature shifts by the metre depending on how close you swim to the falls. Go on a weekday morning - weekend tour buses from Rio Dulce crowd the pool by early afternoon.

title: Release baby turtles into the surf at Monterrico
