description: A narrow gorge cut through white rock an hour from Berat, run on small rubber dinghies since it's too shallow and technical for standard rafts. Almost unknown outside Albania until a few years ago.

title: See the church of Sveti Jovan at Kaneo
description: A 13th-century chapel on a cliff edge above the lake, painted on more Macedonian postcards than any other single building. Come near sunset when the tour buses have gone.

title: Walk the walls of Samuel's Fortress
description: A medieval Bulgarian tsar's stronghold above the old town, with ramparts you can walk the full circuit of for a view over both the lake and the terracotta roofs below.

title: Cross the Stone Bridge into the Old Bazaar
description: The Ottoman-era bazaar on the north bank, the largest outside Istanbul, sitting in contrast to the neoclassical statues and facades the government built across the river after 2010.

title: Ride the cable car up to the Millennium Cross
description: One of the tallest crosses in the world, on Mount Vodno above the city, lit up at night and visible from most of Skopje. The cable car up is faster than the hiking trail and runs most of the year.

title: Hike or ski Mavrovo National Park
description: North Macedonia's largest national park, with a lake, a ski resort, and one of the last wolf and bear populations in the southern Balkans. The submerged church tower of Sveti Nikola breaks the lake surface when levels drop.

title: Stand at the Kokino megalithic observatory
description: A Bronze Age astronomical site on a hilltop, ranked by NASA among the oldest solar observatories in the world. Markers on the rock align with sunrise on the solstices, and almost nobody visits to see it.

title: Taste Vranec at a Tikves winery
description: The Balkans' biggest wine region, producing the dark, tannic Vranec grape found on most Macedonian restaurant lists. Tastings at the larger estates are easy to arrange without a tour.

title: Wade the fifth season floods at Soomaa
description: Snowshoe-like bog shoes let you walk on ground that would otherwise swallow a boot, over pools 10,000 years in the making. Every spring the rivers flood the forest into a fifth season, when locals swap the shoes for canoes.

title: Wander the wooden streets of Kalamaja
description: A former fishermen's and factory-workers' district of wooden houses, now cafes and studios around the old Soviet submarine hall at Seaplane Harbour. Ten minutes' walk from the medieval old town, but nothing like it.

title: Spend a summer afternoon on Parnu beach
description: Estonia's self-declared summer capital, a white sand beach backed by pine trees and Soviet-era sanatoriums since rebuilt as spas. The water is shallow enough to wade out a long way.

title: Explore Estonia's university town of Tartu
description: Home to the country's oldest university since 1632, with a leaning bridge, a hilltop park of ruined cathedral walls, and a student culture that keeps the whole town young.

title: Cross the moat into Kuressaare's bishop's castle
description: The best-preserved medieval castle in the Baltics, a stone fortress with an intact moat on Estonia's largest island. Saaremaa spent centuries answering to Danish, Swedish, German and Russian rulers in turn, and the castle shows every layer.

title: Watch seals off Vilsandi National Park
description: Estonia's oldest protected area, a scatter of over a hundred islets off Saaremaa where grey seals haul out and migrating birds stop by the thousand. Boat trips leave from the western coast when the sea allows.

title: Climb St Peter's tower over Riga's old town
description: A UNESCO old town of guild halls and the House of the Blackheads, rebuilt after wartime bombing from old photographs. The lift up St Peter's spire gives the view the ground-level streets can't.

title: Walk the grounds of Turaida Castle
description: A rebuilt medieval red-brick castle in Gauja National Park, with a folk song hill and the grave of the 'Rose of Turaida' below it. Pair it with Gutmanis Cave, the biggest grotto in the Baltics, a short walk down the valley.

title: Tour the state rooms of Rundale Palace
description: A Baroque summer palace by the architect of St Petersburg's Winter Palace, built for a Duke of Courland and restored room by room since Soviet times. The French formal gardens behind it are worth the extra ticket.

title: Walk the beach promenade at Jurmala
description: Thirty kilometres of white sand backed by wooden Tsarist-era holiday villas, twenty minutes from Riga by train. A Soviet-era spa culture survives in the sanatoriums that still line the dunes.

title: Ride the Sigulda Olympic bobsled track
description: A real World Cup bobsled and luge track built in 1986, open to the public in a wheeled summer cart or a winter sled with a professional driver. Hits speeds of 80 km/h in under a minute.

title: Visit the Aglona Basilica on assumption day
description: The Baltics' biggest Catholic pilgrimage site, drawing over a hundred thousand people every August 15th to a basilica between two lakes in Latvia's most Polish-influenced region.

title: Cross the footbridge to Trakai island castle
description: A red-brick castle rebuilt on its own island in a lake chain, once the capital of a Grand Duchy that stretched to the Black Sea. Rent a kayak instead of just the footbridge and circle it from the water.

title: Ride the funicular up Gediminas' Tower
description: The last remnant of Vilnius' upper castle, on the hill where the city's founding is said to have been dreamed by a duke. Independence rallies gathered here in 1991 while Soviet tanks were still in the streets.

title: Walk the cells of the Vilnius KGB museum
description: Interrogation rooms and a padded execution chamber, preserved in the basement of the former KGB headquarters. Used continuously as a prison from 1940 until 1991, under three different occupying regimes.

title: Walk the pier at Palanga at sunset
description: Lithuania's biggest beach resort, with a wooden sea bridge built for sunset walks and an amber museum inside a count's old palace and rose garden.

title: Walk among the toppled statues at Grutas Park
description: Lenin, Stalin and dozens of other Soviet statues pulled off their pedestals after 1990 and gathered in a forest park, half museum and half theme park - it was pitched to a TV network as 'Stalin World' before opening.

title: Canoe the lakes of Aukstaitija
description: Lithuania's oldest national park, a hundred and twenty-six lakes linked by pine forest, best seen from a multi-day canoe route between villages that still smoke fish over alder wood.

title: Tour the fairytale rooms of Bojnice Castle
description: Slovakia's most visited castle, remodelled in the 1900s into a French-chateau fantasy by the industrialist who owned it. An international ghost festival takes over the halls every May.

title: Stand at the ruins of Devin Castle
description: A ruined clifftop fortress where the Morava river joins the Danube and the Iron Curtain once ran straight through the water. A short bus ride from central Bratislava.

title: Walk the ice formations of Demanovska cave
description: One of the few caves in Europe with ice that survives into summer, in a valley of the Low Tatras riddled with over forty kilometres of passages. Bring a jacket regardless of the weather outside.

title: See the painted houses of Cicmany
description: Log houses lime-washed white and hand-painted with lace-like geometric patterns, a tradition that started after a fire in 1921 and became the village's trademark. One of the first folk sites protected in Europe.

title: Climb the cliffside rooms of Orava Castle
description: A castle built up a rock outcrop in stages over five centuries, used as Count Orlok's home in the 1922 film Nosferatu. The uppermost tower is a genuine climb, not just a walk.

title: Walk the mining town of Banska Stiavnica
description: A silver and gold mining town that funded the Habsburg empire and hosted the world's first mining academy, now a hillside of baroque houses over flooded pit lakes called tajchy.

title: Hike the ridgeline above Vratna valley
description: A cable car up Snilovske sedlo saves half the climb to the ridge of the Mala Fatra, in the valley where the folk-hero outlaw Juraj Janosik is said to have hidden. Limestone crags called Tiesnavy pinch the trail to a rope-assisted scramble lower down.

title: Watch the singing fountain in Kosice's old town
description: Slovakia's second city and a former European Capital of Culture, built around the largest Gothic cathedral in the country. The fountain in the main square runs a light-and-music show most summer evenings.

title: Take a boat through the Blue Grotto sea caves
description: Traditional luzzu boats duck through a string of sea caves lit an electric blue by refracted sunlight. Go before 10am - the boats stop running in rough seas and the light is best in the morning.

title: Stand inside temples older than the pyramids
description: Two megalithic temple complexes on a clifftop, built from limestone slabs around 3600 BC - older than Stonehenge or the Giza pyramids. Tent-like canopies now protect the stone from the same weather that has eroded it for 5,000 years.

title: Watch the sunset from Gozo's Citadel
description: A walled hilltop fortress over Victoria that held the entire island's population during pirate raids, when residents had to sleep inside every night for safety. The restored ramparts give a 360-degree view of Gozo's whole coastline.

title: Swim in Comino's Blue Lagoon
description: Shallow turquoise water over white sand between Comino and a tiny islet, with almost no permanent population to share it with - except the day-tripper boats that fill it by 11am. An early or late ferry beats the crowd.

title: Wander the film set at Popeye Village
description: A wooden fishing village built for the 1980 Robin Williams film Popeye and kept standing ever since as a waterfront park. Sits on a genuinely striking bay, film set or not.

title: See the oldest free-standing structures on earth at Ggantija
description: Two temples on Gozo dated to around 3600 BC, predating the pyramids by a thousand years. Local legend credited them to a giantess who carried the stones on her head, which is roughly how heavy they look.

title: Browse the Sunday fish market at Marsaxlokk
description: A working fishing harbour of orange, yellow and blue luzzu boats, each painted with a pair of eyes on the bow to ward off misfortune. Sunday brings a market of fish, produce and tourist stalls along the whole waterfront.

title: Watch a play in the Greco-Roman theatre at Kourion
description: A cliff-edge theatre with the Mediterranean as its backdrop, still hosting performances in summer nearly two thousand years after it was built. The mosaic floors of the House of Eustolios, just below it, survived an earthquake that levelled most of the city in 365 AD.

title: Find the frescoes hidden in the Troodos painted churches
description: Ten Byzantine and post-Byzantine churches scattered through mountain villages, plain steep-roofed shells outside and wall-to-wall fresco inside. Most keep a caretaker's phone number pinned to the door rather than fixed opening hours.

title: Walk the underground Tombs of the Kings at Paphos
description: Rock-cut tombs from the 4th century BC carved to imitate the houses of the living, despite the name built for aristocrats rather than royalty. There's almost no shade, so a morning visit beats the afternoon sun.

title: Watch the sunset at Aphrodite's Rock
description: A sea stack off the coast road where legend says Aphrodite rose from the foam, with a pebble beach opposite for the view rather than easy swimming. Sunset lines the rock up with the road behind it, and the car park empties out fast after.

title: Walk the Green Line through central Nicosia
description: A UN-patrolled buffer zone has run through the last divided capital in Europe since 1974, and the Ledra Street crossing lets you walk from one side to the other on foot with a passport. Bring ID - the checkpoint is a working border post, not a photo opportunity.

title: See the mosaic floors of the House of Dionysus
description: Roman villa floors depicting the god Dionysus and scenes from Greek myth, preserved almost intact under later layers of soil until a farmer's plough struck them in 1962. Raised walkways cover most of the site so nothing underfoot is missed.

title: Walk the Neolithic village of Choirokoitia
description: Circular stone houses from one of the best-preserved Neolithic settlements in the eastern Mediterranean, inhabited from around 7000 BC. A handful have been rebuilt full-height to show how they actually looked.

title: Visit the gilded interior of Kykkos Monastery
description: Cyprus' wealthiest and most important monastery, its courtyards covered floor to ceiling in gold-backed mosaics telling its own founding story. It holds an icon of the Virgin Mary so sacred it stays permanently covered from view.

title: Watch the flamingos on Larnaca Salt Lake
description: Thousands of migrating flamingos winter on a lake bed that dries into a walkable salt crust by summer. The 16th-century Hala Sultan Tekke mosque sits right on its edge, one of Islam's most important pilgrimage sites outside the Middle East's main countries.

title: Hike the sea caves of Cape Greco
description: Cliff paths link natural arches, sea caves and a submerged sculpture park you can snorkel straight out to from the rocks. Far less built-up than the Ayia Napa strip it borders.

title: Explore Kyrenia's Venetian harbour castle
description: A Byzantine, then Venetian, fortress guarding a horseshoe harbour on the island's north coast, home to the wreck of a 4th-century BC Greek merchant ship raised nearly whole. This side of the island has used a different currency and administration since 1974, so check current entry requirements before planning a crossing.

title: Climb the Crusader keep at Kolossi Castle
description: A squat stone keep built by the Knights Hospitaller, who ran a sugar plantation and refinery here that once supplied crusader Europe. The roof gives a flat view over the vineyards that grow the local Commandaria dessert wine.

title: Hike the Madriu-Perafita-Claror valley
description: Andorra's only UNESCO World Heritage site, a glacial valley of stone shepherd huts and terraced fields that shows a thousand years of mountain farming. No road reaches it - every visitor arrives on foot.

title: Tour Andorra's old parliament at Casa de la Vall
description: A 16th-century stone manor that served as the seat of Andorra's government until 2011, with a council chamber that still locks its decisions in a cabinet with six keys, one per parish.

title: Ski Grandvalira, the Pyrenees' biggest resort
description: Over 200 kilometres of linked pistes across two valleys, built up because skiing and duty-free shopping are most of what keeps Andorra's economy running. Lift lines are shortest on weekday mornings outside French and Spanish school holidays.

title: Visit the sanctuary of Andorra's patron saint
description: A modernist basilica rebuilt after a 1972 fire destroyed the original chapel, holding the statue of the Virgin of Meritxell that Andorrans credit with the country's protection. September 8th is a national holiday built entirely around it.

title: Look inside the Belle Epoque halls of the Monte Carlo Casino
description: Gilded gaming rooms that funded the principality when Monaco abolished taxes for its own citizens in the 1860s. A general admission ticket gets you into the ornate public rooms even if you don't gamble.

title: Watch the changing of the guard at the Prince's Palace
description: An 11:55am ceremony outside the ruling Grimaldi family's home, on a clifftop rock the family has held since 1297 - Europe's longest-ruling dynasty. The palace's state rooms open to the public only when the Prince isn't in residence.

title: Climb into the cave below the Jardin Exotique
description: Thousands of cacti and succulents planted down a cliff face, above a limestone cave with stalactites reaching almost to the sea. The steep paths aren't stroller or wheelchair friendly - the drop is the whole point of the view.

title: Walk the superyacht docks of Port Hercules
description: The floating heart of the Grand Prix track and the Monaco Yacht Show, lined with vessels that can cost more than the apartments overlooking them. Free to walk, and free to feel underdressed.

title: Climb the second tower, Cesta, for the arms museum
description: The tallest of San Marino's three fortresses, now a museum of medieval and Renaissance weapons, reached by the ridge path from Guaita. Wind on the exposed walkway between the towers can be sharp even in summer.

title: See the private third tower, Montale, from the ridge trail
description: Never open to the public and rarely photographed as well as its two neighbours because fewer people walk this far along the ridge. The path here thins out and the crowds mostly stop at Cesta.

title: Watch the guard change in Piazza della Liberta
description: The ceremonial heart of the world's oldest republic, in front of a government palace still in active use. The guard change happens on the hour and draws a bigger crowd than its five-minute length suggests.

title: Ride the cable car down to Borgo Maggiore market
description: San Marino's real working town, below the tourist-facing City on the peak, with a Thursday market that's sold produce since the 1600s. The cable car ride down is worth doing for its own sake.

title: Photograph Vaduz Castle from the vineyard path
description: The reigning prince's actual home, on a wooded outcrop above the capital, and closed to the public because of it. A marked path through the vineyards below gives the best photo without trespassing on the family's front lawn.

title: Walk a stage of the Liechtenstein Trail
description: A 75-kilometre route opened in 2019 that strings together all eleven municipalities, walkable end to end in about five days or sampled in single afternoon stages by bus back to Vaduz.

title: Browse Vaduz's stamp and art museums
description: A capital small enough to see on foot in an afternoon, with a postage stamp museum that explains how stamp sales alone used to fund a meaningful share of the state budget.

title: Ski Liechtenstein's only resort at Malbun
description: A small, unglamorous resort at the end of a dead-end mountain road, with beginner-friendly slopes and none of the prices or crowds of its Austrian and Swiss neighbours.

title: Visit the cave monastery at Orheiul Vechi
description: A monastery carved into a limestone cliff above the Raut river, still used by a handful of monks, on a site occupied on and off since the Stone Age. The village of Butuceni below keeps traditional Moldovan houses along a single dirt lane.

title: Drive the wine cellars of Cricova
description: Over a hundred kilometres of former limestone quarry turned wine cellar, toured by golf cart because walking it all isn't practical. Heads of state and half of Europe's political class have wine bottled here under their own names.

title: Tour the world's largest wine collection at Milestii Mici
description: A Guinness World Record two million bottles held in underground streets long enough to need street names and traffic signs. Some of the reserve wines here predate Moldovan independence.

title: Walk the boulevards of Chisinau
description: Europe's least-visited capital, rebuilt in wide Soviet boulevards after the Second World War, with a triumphal arch, a yellow-stone cathedral, and a park culture that fills every bench on a warm evening.

title: Cross into Transnistria to see Tiraspol
description: A breakaway strip along the Ukrainian border that still flies a hammer-and-sickle flag and uses its own currency, unrecognised by any UN member including Moldova itself. Crossing is currently straightforward for most nationalities at the checkpoint, but confirm the latest advice before going - the region sits close to the war in Ukraine.

title: Taste Negru de Purcari at Chateau Purcari
description: A winery founded in 1827 whose Negru de Purcari red was reportedly a favourite of the British royal family, on the Dniester near the Ukrainian border. The estate's own microclimate is credited for grapes ripening further north than they should.

title: See the Byzantine mosaics of Saint Sophia Cathedral
description: An 11th-century cathedral with its original mosaics and frescoes largely intact, one of the few Kyivan Rus buildings to survive Mongol invasion, Soviet demolition plans and, so far, the current war. Ukraine is under an active do-not-travel advisory; this is a record of what the country holds, not a current itinerary.

title: Walk the underground caves of the Kyiv Pechersk Lavra
description: A monastery complex of gold domes above catacombs where mummified monks have lain in glass cases for centuries, candle in hand as you file past in the dark. Founded in 1051 and still an active monastery between the museum sections.

title: Wander the UNESCO old town of Lviv
description: A central European old town of Austro-Hungarian, Polish and Ukrainian layers that came through the Second World War largely undamaged, unlike almost every other major Ukrainian city. The furthest west and generally calmest part of the country, though still under wartime air alerts.

title: Walk the abandoned streets of Pripyat in the Chernobyl zone
description: Guided day trips from Kyiv ran routinely to the reactor and the ghost city of Pripyat until Russian forces occupied and dug trenches in the radioactive Red Forest in early 2022. Tours have not consistently resumed since; check current status before planning anything.

title: Cross the canyon bridge to Kamianets-Podilskyi fortress
description: An Old Town fortress that sits on an island formed by a river canyon looping almost back on itself, crossed by a single bridge. Rated among the most dramatic castle settings in Europe, and far enough from the front line to have stayed largely untouched by the war so far.

title: Walk down the Potemkin Stairs in Odesa
description: One hundred and ninety-two steps down to the Black Sea harbour, made famous by Eisenstein's 1925 film Battleship Potemkin. Odesa's historic centre earned UNESCO listing in 2023, the same year Russian strikes damaged part of it - a status meant to draw protection as much as visitors.

title: Hike to the summit of Hoverla, Ukraine's highest peak
description: A 2,061-metre summit in the Hutsul highlands, normally a straightforward day hike from Ukraine's most peaceful region. Trailhead access has varied through the war; local guides are the most reliable source on current conditions.

title: Stand in Maidan Nezalezhnosti, Independence Square
description: The square at the centre of two revolutions, in 2004 and 2014, now lined with flags planted for every soldier killed since 2022. Less a tourist sight than a place to understand what the country is currently living through.

title: Cross the moat into Mir Castle
description: A red-brick Gothic-Renaissance castle rebuilt from ruin across three centuries, UNESCO listed for the sheer range of architectural styles stitched into one building. Belarus currently carries a do-not-travel advisory for foreign nationals over detention risk; this is a record of the country's heritage, not a current recommendation.

title: Tour the Radziwill family seat at Nesvizh
description: A moated palace that housed one of Eastern Europe's most powerful noble families for four centuries, with a landscaped park and a chain of ponds dug by hand. Paired with Mir Castle on the same UNESCO listing, 100 kilometres apart.

title: Look for European bison in the Bialowieza Forest
description: The last major remnant of the primeval forest that once covered the European plain, and home to the continent's largest land animal, the European bison, reintroduced here after it went extinct in the wild. The forest straddles the Polish border; the two sides are separately managed and not connected without a formal crossing.

title: See the diamond-shaped National Library of Belarus
description: A capital almost entirely rebuilt in wide Stalinist boulevards after 1944, with a 2006 library shaped like a giant illuminated rhombicuboctahedron on its edge. Foreign nationals currently face real detention risk in Belarus; treat this as background on the country, not travel advice.

title: Stand in Red Square between the Kremlin and GUM
description: Cobblestones between the Kremlin wall, Lenin's mausoleum and a 19th-century department store now selling Western luxury brands under sanctions-era workarounds. Russia currently carries a do-not-travel advisory over the war, sanctions and closed airspace to most of the world; this reflects the country's landmarks, not present-day advice to go.

title: Walk the maze of chapels inside St Basil's Cathedral
description: Nine separate chapels under those onion domes, each a distinct, low-ceilinged space rather than one grand nave. Legend holds Ivan the Terrible blinded the architect afterward so he could never build anything to rival it - almost certainly untrue, but it's the story every guide tells.

title: Tour the armoury and cathedrals inside the Kremlin walls
description: A walled complex of onion-domed cathedrals and the tsars' treasury, still the working seat of the Russian government behind its public-facing half. The Armoury's ticket allocation sells out by mid-morning on a normal day.

title: Get lost in the Hermitage's three million objects
description: The Winter Palace of the tsars turned into one of the largest art museums on earth - walking every gallery for a minute each would take over a week. Western credit cards no longer work anywhere in the country, so budget cash brought in advance.

title: Ride a stretch of the Trans-Siberian Railway
description: Nine thousand two hundred and eighty-nine kilometres of track from Moscow to Vladivostok, the longest railway line in the world, crossing eight time zones over about a week end to end. Almost no direct flights connect Russia to Western Europe or North America now, so getting to the start line is its own undertaking.

title: Swim or dive in Lake Baikal
description: The deepest and oldest lake on the planet, holding roughly a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh water, so clear you can see twenty metres down from a boat. In winter the surface freezes into clear ice slabs people drive cars across.

title: See the all-wood church built without a single nail at Kizhi
description: A 22-dome wooden church built in 1714 using nothing but axes, notched logs and wooden pegs - no nails anywhere in the structure. Reachable only by boat, on an island that also holds a working open-air museum of relocated peasant houses and windmills.

title: Hike an active volcano in Kamchatka
description: Twenty-nine active volcanoes on a peninsula with no roads connecting it to the rest of Russia - every trip starts with a flight into Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky. Helicopter transfers to the more remote craters are standard, since most of the terrain has no trails at all.

title: Watch the fountains start at Peterhof without a single pump
description: Peter the Great's answer to Versailles, its 150-plus fountains run entirely on gravity from elevated springs, with no mechanical pumps at all since the 18th century. The Grand Cascade below the palace is switched on each morning to a recorded fanfare.

title: Cycle between the monasteries of Suzdal
description: A Golden Ring town frozen at village scale, with more churches and monasteries than modern buildings and no high-rises breaking the skyline of onion domes. Small enough to see entirely by rented bike in a day.

title: Climb to the Motherland Calls statue at Mamayev Kurgan
description: An 85-metre sword-wielding statue over the mass graves of the Battle of Stalingrad, once the tallest statue in the world, on a hill where the fighting was so intense that unexploded ordnance is still found in the ground each year.

title: See the mosque and cathedral share a skyline at the Kazan Kremlin
description: A walled citadel where the blue-domed Qol Sharif Mosque and the Orthodox Annunciation Cathedral stand a few hundred metres apart, reflecting Tatarstan's mixed Muslim-Christian history. Kazan itself keeps a distinct Tatar language and identity within Russia.

title: Go inside the Sagrada Familia in the afternoon
description: The western windows are the warm ones. Gaudi started in 1882 and the towers are only now being finished; book a timed entry.

title: Walk the roof terraces of Casa Mila
description: Gaudi's warrior chimneys on an undulating roof with no straight line in it. The night visit includes the rooftop lit up.

title: Find a seat in Park Guell's serpentine bench
description: A failed housing estate turned public park. The monumental zone is ticketed and capped; the woodland above it is free.

title: Eat standing up at the Boqueria before nine
description: The market bars at the back serve breakfast to the stallholders. By eleven it belongs to the tour groups.

title: Walk the ridge above Montserrat monastery
description: A saw-toothed conglomerate massif with a Benedictine monastery halfway up. Take the rack railway and walk down.

title: Follow the Cami de Ronda around the Costa Brava
description: An old coastguard footpath linking coves between Blanes and Portbou. Sant Feliu to Tossa is the stretch to walk.

title: See Dali's own museum at Figueres
description: He designed it, filled it, and is buried under the floor. Easily the strangest major museum in Spain.

title: Walk to the Estany de Sant Maurici
description: Catalonia's only national park: granite peaks, two hundred lakes and no private cars past the gate.

title: Stand in the forest of arches at the Mezquita
description: Eight hundred and fifty columns of a tenth-century mosque with a cathedral dropped into the middle of it. Free entry before nine thirty.

title: Climb the Giralda ramp instead of stairs
description: Thirty-five ramps rather than steps, built so the muezzin could ride a horse to the top of the minaret.

title: See flamenco in a Triana peña
description: The gitano quarter across the river where the form comes from. A peña is a members' club, and most will let you in.

title: Walk the walkways on top of the Setas
description: The largest timber structure in the world, over a Roman excavation. The rooftop walk at sunset costs very little.

title: Look down into the Tajo gorge at Ronda
description: A town split by a hundred-metre gorge and stitched together by an eighteenth-century bridge. Walk down to the bottom for the real view.

title: Walk the Caminito del Rey
description: A metre-wide walkway pinned to a gorge wall a hundred metres up. Rebuilt in 2015 after years as the most dangerous path in Spain.

title: See the sherry bodegas of Jerez
description: The solera system means a glass of fino contains wine from decades of vintages. Tours end in a tasting, as they should.

title: Walk the volcanic coast of Cabo de Gata
description: The driest place in Europe, a protected volcanic coastline of empty beaches and no development. Bring your own water.

title: Look for lynx in Donana
description: Marshland at the mouth of the Guadalquivir holding most of the world's remaining Iberian lynx and half a million wintering birds.

title: Walk up to the Mirador de San Nicolas at sunset
description: The Moorish quarter opposite the Alhambra, and the view across to it as the Sierra Nevada turns pink behind.

title: See Las Meninas in the Prado
description: Velazquez, Goya and Bosch in one building. Free for the last two hours every day, which is exactly when everyone goes.

title: Stand in front of Guernica
description: Picasso would not let it come to Spain until democracy returned. It arrived in 1981 and has not moved since.

title: Eat bocadillo de calamares on the Plaza Mayor
description: A fried squid sandwich in a landlocked city three hundred kilometres from the sea. Madrid does not explain itself.

title: Walk the Retiro at opening time
description: The old royal gardens, with a glasshouse of pure glass and iron and rowing boats on the lake.

title: Walk to La Pedriza above Manzanares
description: A granite badlands of rounded boulders an hour from the city, where Madrid goes climbing at the weekend.

title: Walk under the Segovia aqueduct
description: One hundred and sixty-seven arches of unmortared granite, built around 100 AD and carrying water until the 1970s.

title: Find the frog on the Salamanca facade
description: A small carved frog hidden in the plateresque stonework. Students say finding it unaided means you will pass your exams.

title: See the human fossils at Atapuerca
description: The richest early-human site in Europe, with remains going back 1.2 million years. The dig is open to guided visits.

title: Walk the three-faith quarters of Toledo
description: A synagogue, a mosque and a cathedral within a few hundred metres, in the city where all three coexisted for centuries.

title: See the hanging houses of Cuenca
description: Balconied houses built out over a gorge in the fifteenth century, best seen from the iron footbridge opposite.

title: Stargaze in the Monfrague dark sky reserve
description: A certified starlight reserve that is also the best raptor-watching site in Spain, with black vultures nesting on the Salto del Gitano.

title: Work through the pintxos bars of the Parte Vieja
description: One pintxo and one drink per bar, then move on. The old town has over a hundred and the good ones are standing room only.

title: See the Guggenheim from the river side
description: Gehry's titanium curves turned a dying industrial port around in a decade. The building outside is as much of the point as the art inside.

title: Climb the 241 steps to Gaztelugatxe
description: A hermitage on a rock island joined to the coast by a stone bridge. Free, but you must book a time slot.

title: See the bison at Altamira in the replica cave
description: The first cave art ever recognised as prehistoric, and dismissed as a forgery for twenty years. The neocave reproduces it exactly.

title: Drive up to the Lagos de Covadonga
description: Two glacial lakes at 1,100 metres in the Picos. In summer the road closes to private cars and a shuttle runs instead.

title: Pour Asturian cider from above your head
description: The escanciador pours from arm's length to aerate it, and you drink the small measure straight down. Anything left goes on the floor.

title: Stand at the edge of the Costa da Morte
description: Where the Romans believed the world ended, and where Camino walkers keep going after Santiago to burn their boots.

title: Walk the complete Roman wall at Lugo
description: Two kilometres of third-century wall with a walkway right around the top, the only fully intact Roman circuit anywhere.

title: Take the boat to the Cies Islands
description: A national park with a daily visitor cap and a beach the locals will tell you is the best in the world. Permits book out in July.

title: Walk the route of the encierro when nothing is chasing you
description: Eight hundred and seventy-five metres from the corral to the ring. Doing it on a quiet morning tells you how narrow Estafeta really is.

title: Cycle the badlands of the Bardenas Reales
description: A semi-desert of eroded clay a hundred kilometres from the Pyrenees, with a military bombing range still active in one corner.

title: Walk into the Ordesa canyon
description: A glacial canyon in the high Pyrenees, with the Cola de Caballo waterfall at the head of it. Shuttle bus only in summer.

title: Look for the Mudejar towers of Teruel
description: Brick and glazed-tile towers built by Muslim craftsmen for Christian patrons after the reconquest. Spain's most overlooked provincial capital.

title: Taste in a Rioja bodega built by an architect
description: The Barrio de la Estacion in Haro has the densest concentration of century-old bodegas anywhere, several of them wrapped in modern architecture.

title: Drive the Sa Calobra road
description: Twelve kilometres of hairpins including a full 270-degree loop where the road ties itself in a knot. Cyclists own it at dawn.

title: Walk the dry stone route through the Tramuntana
description: The GR221 links mountain refuges along a world heritage landscape of terraces and olive groves. Spring, before the heat.

title: Walk a stage of the Cami de Cavalls
description: A 185-kilometre bridle path right around Menorca, first cut so mounted patrols could watch for pirates.

title: Watch the sunset over Es Vedra
description: A four-hundred-metre limestone island off the south-west coast, best seen from the cliffs at Cala d'Hort with nothing playing.

title: Watch the stars from Teide
description: Spain's highest point at 3,715 metres, above the cloud layer and inside one of the world's best protected skies. Permits needed for the summit cone.

title: See what Manrique built in the lava
description: A collapsed lava tube turned into a concert hall and pool, with blind albino crabs found nowhere else living in the lagoon.

title: Walk the Ruta de los Volcanes
description: Along the volcanic spine of the island past the 2021 Tajogaite eruption, with both coasts visible most of the way.

title: Walk in the laurel cloud forest of Garajonay
description: A relict forest of the kind that covered the Mediterranean before the ice ages, kept alive by cloud stripping through the trees.

title: Walk the dunes at Corralejo
description: Eleven kilometres of protected white dunes blown in from the Sahara, with Lobos island sitting just offshore.

title: Climb the Eiffel Tower stairs instead of queueing for the lift
description: The stair ticket is cheaper and the queue is a fraction of the lift's. 674 steps to the second floor, then a lift for the summit.

title: See the Impressionists in a converted railway station
description: Monet, Degas and Van Gogh hung under the glass roof of the old Gare d'Orsay. The clock face on the top floor looks straight across the Seine.

title: Stand under the rebuilt spire of Notre-Dame
description: Reopened in December 2024 after the fire. Entry to the cathedral is free; book a timed slot online to skip the worst of the wait.

title: Walk the ossuary tunnels beneath the fourteenth arrondissement
description: Two kilometres of tunnel lined with the bones of six million Parisians, moved here when the city closed its overflowing cemeteries in 1786.

title: Walk the Promenade Plantee above the street
description: A garden built along a disused railway viaduct in 1993. New York's High Line copied the idea a decade later.

title: Watch the sunset from the steps of Sacre-Coeur
description: The highest natural point in Paris. Come up through the back streets rather than the crowded funicular side.

title: Eat your way along the Rue Mouffetard market
description: One of the oldest market streets in Paris, best on a Sunday morning when the cheesemongers and rotisseries are all open.

title: See the Louvre at night when the queues have gone
description: Open late on Wednesdays and Fridays. The Denon wing after eight is a different museum to the one at midday.

title: Cycle the Grand Canal in the gardens of Versailles
description: The gardens are vast enough that walking eats the whole day. Hire a bike at the canal and ride out to Marie Antoinette's hamlet.

title: Boulder on the sandstone of Fontainebleau forest
description: The birthplace of modern bouldering. Colour-graded circuits run from a child's scramble to some of the hardest problems in Europe.

title: See the Conde collection at Chateau de Chantilly
description: The second-best collection of old masters in France after the Louvre, in a chateau most day-trippers from Paris never reach.

title: Walk the medieval walls of Provins
description: A complete walled fair town from the twelfth century, an hour from Paris and almost entirely overlooked.

title: Time the lavender bloom on the Valensole plateau
description: The lavender is cut in the third week of July, so late June to mid-July is the window. Go at first light, before the coaches.

title: Walk the ochre trail at Roussillon
description: A short loop through old ochre quarries in seventeen shades of red and yellow. Do not wear white shoes.

title: Stand under the Pont du Gard aqueduct
description: A three-tier Roman aqueduct built without mortar around 50 AD. You can swim in the Gardon river underneath it in summer.

title: Look for pink flamingos in the Camargue
description: Salt lagoons at the mouth of the Rhone, with white horses, black bulls and Europe's largest flamingo colony.

title: Swim in the calanques between Marseille and Cassis
description: Limestone inlets with water the colour of a swimming pool. En-Vau is the classic; the walk in is steep and there is no shade.

title: Take the coast path around Cap Ferrat
description: A free public footpath around a peninsula of private villas. Eleven kilometres if you walk the whole circuit.

title: See the Matisse chapel at Vence
description: Matisse designed every element of it in his eighties and called it his masterpiece. Go on a bright morning for the glass.

title: Drive the Route des Cretes above Cassis
description: The highest sea cliffs in France, on a road that closes on high-wind and fire-risk days. Check before you set out.

title: Ride a boat to the car-free island of Porquerolles
description: Vineyards and white-sand beaches twenty minutes off the Var coast, with no private cars. Hire a bike at the port.

title: Walk into the Ecrins from the Pre de Madame Carle
description: France's wildest high national park, with no ski resorts inside its core. The glacier walk from Pre de Madame Carle is the classic day out.

title: Ride the Train des Pignes up from Nice
description: A narrow-gauge line from the coast up through the back-country gorges to Digne. Locals use it; almost no visitors do.

title: See the Lascaux cave paintings in the facsimile
description: The original cave closed in 1963 to save the pigment. Lascaux IV reproduces it millimetre for millimetre, in the same dark and cold.

title: Canoe the Dordogne beneath the castles
description: A gentle paddle from Vitrac past Beynac and Castelnaud, two castles that spent the Hundred Years War glaring at each other.

title: Climb the Dune du Pilat at sunset
description: The tallest sand dune in Europe at around 100 metres, still moving inland a few metres a year. Atlantic on one side, pine forest on the other.

title: Taste your way through Saint-Emilion
description: A world heritage wine village built over a monolithic church carved out of the rock beneath it.

title: Wait for the mist on the Bordeaux water mirror
description: The largest reflecting pool in the world, on the quay in front of the Place de la Bourse. It fogs over every few minutes.

title: Surf the beach breaks at Hossegor
description: A deep offshore canyon funnels swell straight onto the sand here, which is why the pro tour keeps coming back.

title: Ride the Rhune rack railway above the Basque coast
description: A 1924 wooden cog train up a Basque mountain, with pottok ponies and vultures at the top and both coasts visible on a clear day.

title: Cross the Passerelle d'Holzarte footbridge
description: A wire suspension bridge strung 180 metres above a Basque gorge in 1920 by Italian labourers. Not for the queasy.

title: Cycle the salt marshes of the Ile de Re
description: Over a hundred kilometres of flat cycle path between whitewashed villages, oyster beds and salt pans.

title: Walk the double walls of Carcassonne early
description: Fifty-two towers and three kilometres of wall. Stay the night inside and the place is yours after the last coach leaves.

title: See the prehistoric bison at Niaux
description: One of the few original painted caves still open to visitors. You walk 800 metres into the dark with a lamp to reach the Salon Noir.

title: Cross the Millau Viaduct
description: The tallest bridge in the world, its masts higher than the Eiffel Tower. Stop at the D992 viewpoint rather than photographing it at speed.

title: Paddle the Gorges du Tarn
description: Fifty kilometres of limestone canyon with green water and villages wedged into the base of the cliffs.

title: Stand in the Cirque de Gavarnie
description: A natural amphitheatre 1,500 metres high with the tallest waterfall in France down its back wall.

title: Swim under the Pont du Diable at Saint-Guilhem
description: A medieval pilgrim village at the mouth of a gorge, with swimming holes under an eleventh-century bridge.

title: Ride the Train Jaune through the Cerdagne
description: A canary-yellow open-carriage train climbing to 1,593 metres, the highest railway station in France.

title: Look through the telescopes at the Pic du Midi
description: A working observatory at 2,877 metres that lets a handful of people stay overnight. The Milky Way from the terrace is the reason to do it.

title: Eat cassoulet where it was invented
description: Toulouse, Castelnaudary and Carcassonne have argued over the recipe for centuries. Winter is when it makes sense to eat it.

title: Walk up the Puy de Dome volcano
description: A dormant volcano above Clermont-Ferrand with eighty more lined up behind it. The Chemin des Muletiers is the walking route; there is a rack railway if you would rather.

title: Ride over the highest paved pass in the Alps
description: At 2,764 metres the Iseran only clears of snow for about ten weeks a year, which is the whole point of getting there.

title: Swim in Lac d'Annecy
description: Fed by mountain springs and reckoned the cleanest large lake in Europe. The cycle path around it runs on an old railway line.

title: Paddle under the Pont d'Arc
description: A natural stone arch over the river, then thirty kilometres of gorge with one bivouac site halfway. Book the bivouac before you go.

title: Eat in a certified Lyon bouchon
description: Small bistros serving the offal-heavy cooking Lyon built its name on. Look for the Authentique Bouchon Lyonnais plaque on the door.

title: Find the traboules of Croix-Rousse
description: Covered passageways cut between buildings so silk workers could carry cloth in the dry. Many are still open to the public behind unmarked doors.

title: Drive the cliff road through Combe Laval
description: A road blasted into a vertical limestone wall in the 1890s to bring timber out. Tunnels open straight onto a 600-metre drop.

title: Walk the ridge of the Puy Mary
description: The eroded core of Europe's largest extinct volcano, with radiating valleys you can trace from the summit.

title: Walk the customs path around the Pointe du Raz
description: The old smuggler-watching path along Brittany's western tip, where the Atlantic hits the granite properly.

title: Count the standing stones at Carnac
description: More than three thousand menhirs in rows running four kilometres, raised between 4500 and 3300 BC. Older than Stonehenge.

title: Watch the tide come in at Saint-Malo
description: One of the biggest tidal ranges in Europe. At low water you walk out to Chateaubriand's island tomb; six hours later it is gone.

title: Follow the pink granite coast path
description: Wind-rounded boulders the colour of salmon, piled along the sea between Perros-Guirec and Ploumanac'h.

title: Walk Omaha Beach at low tide
description: Five kilometres of open sand the American landings crossed on 6 June 1944. The American cemetery sits on the bluff above it.

title: See the chalk arch and needle at Etretat
description: The cliffs Monet painted more than twenty times. Walk up to the chapel for the view back along the arch.

title: Stand in Monet's garden at Giverny
description: The lily pond, the green bridge and the wisteria, kept as he planted them. Go at opening or an hour before closing.

title: Cycle the Loire a Velo between the chateaux
description: Nine hundred kilometres of signed, mostly flat cycle route along the last wild river in France, linking Chambord, Chenonceau and Amboise.

title: See the double helix staircase at Chambord
description: Two spirals wound around each other so people going up never meet those coming down. Leonardo is thought to have had a hand in it.

title: Stand on the white cliffs of Cap Blanc-Nez
description: The French half of the same chalk as Dover, with England visible across the strait on a clear day and almost nobody there.

title: Drive the Alsace wine route villages
description: One hundred and seventy kilometres of half-timbered villages and riesling, from Marlenheim down to Thann.

title: Climb to the Chateau du Haut-Koenigsbourg
description: A red sandstone castle restored by Kaiser Wilhelm II, looking out over the whole Rhine plain to the Black Forest.

title: Walk the grand cru vineyards below Vosne-Romanee
description: A public track runs between the most expensive farmland on earth. The Romanee-Conti plot is marked by a plain stone cross.

title: Find the source of the Loue
description: A river arriving fully formed out of the base of a cliff, painted by Courbet, who grew up an hour away.

title: Cross the Passage du Gois before the tide turns
description: A four-kilometre road to the Ile de Noirmoutier that is under the sea twice a day. Rescue towers stand along it for people who misread the tables.

title: Walk a stage of the GR20
description: Reckoned the hardest waymarked trail in Europe: sixteen stages along the spine of Corsica. The northern half is the brutal half.

title: Sail into the Scandola reserve
description: Red porphyry cliffs and sea caves reachable only by boat, with ospreys nesting on the stacks.

title: Swim off the Lavezzi islands
description: A granite archipelago between Corsica and Sardinia with water clear enough to see the bottom at fifteen metres.

title: See the Rosetta Stone at the British Museum
description: Free, enormous, and impossible in one visit. Pick three galleries and ignore the rest, or you will see nothing properly.

title: Walk across the Thames on the Tower Bridge glass floor
description: The high walkways were closed for seventy years and reopened with a glass floor forty-two metres above the river.

title: Stand on the Prime Meridian at Greenwich
description: Longitude zero, and the room where the problem of finding it at sea was finally solved by Harrison's clocks.

title: Watch a play standing in the Globe yard
description: Five pounds to stand as a groundling in an open-roofed reconstruction, which is how the plays were written to be watched.

title: Walk the whole of Hampstead Heath to Kenwood
description: Three hundred and twenty hectares of unmanicured London, with swimming ponds open all year and the best free view of the city from Parliament Hill.

title: Eat at Borough Market on a weekday
description: A thousand years of market on the same spot. Saturdays are unbearable; Tuesday lunchtime is the market the traders prefer.

title: Find Sir John Soane's house exactly as he left it
description: An architect's house kept by act of parliament in the arrangement he died with, crammed with sarcophagi and mirrors. Free, and tiny.

title: Ride the whole Elizabeth line end to end
description: Reading to Abbey Wood through tunnels bored under the entire city, past platforms that look like an airport of the near future.

title: Get inside the Stonehenge circle at sunrise
description: Stone circle access is booked separately and outside opening hours, which is the only way to stand among them rather than behind rope.

title: Explore Wells Cathedral and its scissor arches
description: Inverted arches added in 1338 to stop the tower sinking, and an astronomical clock whose jousting knights have run since 1390.

title: Walk the Cheddar Gorge clifftop circuit
description: The deepest gorge in Britain, with a five-kilometre loop along both rims and caves where the oldest complete British skeleton was found.

title: Walk the Jurassic Coast to Durdle Door
description: A limestone arch below a steep chalk path from Lulworth Cove. The whole coast reads as 185 million years laid out west to east.

title: Cross Dartmoor on a letterboxing walk
description: Hundreds of hidden stamp boxes scattered across the moor since 1854. Wild camping is legal here, which it is nowhere else in England.

title: Walk out to St Michael's Mount on the causeway
description: A tidal island with a castle, still lived in by the St Aubyn family. Walk out at low water and take the boat back.

title: See the biomes at the Eden Project
description: Two vast biome domes in a worked-out china clay pit, one rainforest, one Mediterranean. The rainforest canopy walkway is the bit to do.

title: Watch a play at the Minack Theatre
description: An open-air theatre cut into a granite cliff by one woman and her gardener from 1931 onwards, with the Atlantic as the backdrop.

title: Walk the white cliffs from Dover to South Foreland
description: Five kilometres of chalk clifftop to a Victorian lighthouse, with France visible on a clear day and peregrines on the face.

title: Watch seals at Blakeney Point
description: England's largest grey seal colony, with pups on the shingle from November. Boats run from Morston Quay on the tide.

title: See the Sutton Hoo ship burial site
description: The mounds where an Anglo-Saxon king was buried in a ship in the 620s, found in 1939 days before the war began.

title: Punt on the Cherwell in Oxford
description: Punting from the Cherwell Boathouse up past the Parks. Push off the bottom, do not let go of the pole, and expect to fall in once.

title: See the King's College chapel fan vault
description: The largest fan vault in the world, and the Christmas Eve carol service that the BBC has broadcast since 1928.

title: Swim on the rooftop at the Thermae Bath Spa
description: The only natural thermal water in Britain, in a Georgian city built entirely from the same honey-coloured stone.

title: Walk the best-preserved stretch of Hadrian's Wall
description: Steel Rigg to Housesteads runs along the crags where the wall still stands highest. Eighty Roman miles coast to coast if you want the lot.

title: Look up in the Northumberland dark sky park
description: The largest area of protected night sky in Europe, with an observatory in the forest and aurora on the better nights.

title: Cross the sands to Lindisfarne
description: A tidal causeway to Holy Island, with published safe crossing times and a refuge box for people who ignore them.

title: Walk the Malham Cove limestone pavement
description: A seventy-metre curved cliff with a field of clints and grikes on top, and peregrines nesting on the face in spring.

title: Ride the Settle to Carlisle railway
description: Seventy-two miles over the Ribblehead Viaduct and through Blea Moor, saved from closure by a public campaign in the 1980s.

title: Walk the Yorkshire Three Peaks in a day
description: Pen-y-ghent, Whernside and Ingleborough: 39 kilometres and 1,585 metres of ascent, traditionally inside twelve hours.

title: See Whitby Abbey above the harbour
description: The ruin Bram Stoker used for Dracula's landfall, reached by 199 steps from a town that still lands its own crab.

title: Ride the Blackpool heritage trams along the front
description: The oldest electric tramway in Britain, running since 1885, along seven miles of seafront and illuminations in autumn.

title: Row out to the island on Ullswater
description: The steamers have run since 1859. Take one to Howtown and walk the shore path back, which is the finest low-level walk in the Lakes.

title: Climb Scafell Pike from Wasdale
description: England's highest point at 978 metres, up from the deepest lake in the country. The Corridor Route is the interesting way.

title: Take the ferry across the Mersey
description: Fifty minutes on the river with the Three Graces on the skyline, and the song playing on the tannoy whether you want it or not.

title: Walk the Monsal Trail through the tunnels
description: Thirteen kilometres of former railway through four lit tunnels in the Peak District, flat enough for anyone and open to bikes.

title: Walk up Arthur's Seat before breakfast
description: An extinct volcano inside the city, 251 metres up, with the whole of Edinburgh and the Forth laid out at the top.

title: Find the closes off the Royal Mile
description: Narrow alleys running downhill off the spine of the old town, several of them buried under later buildings and open to tours.

title: Ride the Jacobite over the Glenfinnan Viaduct
description: A steam train from Fort William to Mallaig over the curved viaduct. Watching it from the hillside path is free and just as good.

title: Walk into Glen Coe on the Lost Valley path
description: A hanging valley the MacDonalds hid stolen cattle in, up a boulder scramble from the road. The massacre of 1692 happened below.

title: Climb Ben Nevis by the mountain track
description: Britain's highest at 1,345 metres. The summit plateau is in cloud most days and navigating off it has killed people; carry a compass.

title: Look for dolphins at Chanonry Point
description: Bottlenose dolphins feed in the narrows on a rising tide, close enough to the shingle spit to hear them breathe.

title: Walk the machair beaches of Harris
description: Luskentyre and Seilebost are white shell sand against turquoise water, and they are usually empty even in July.

title: Take a boat to Staffa and Fingal's Cave
description: Hexagonal basalt columns and a sea cave that gave Mendelssohn his overture. Puffins nest on the top in early summer.

title: Land on St Kilda
description: Forty miles beyond the Outer Hebrides, evacuated in 1930 and now the largest gannet colony in the North Atlantic. Weather cancels most trips.

title: Walk into the Neolithic village at Skara Brae
description: Older than the pyramids, with stone dressers and box beds still in place, uncovered by a storm in 1850.

title: Watch puffins at Sumburgh Head
description: Puffins nest within a few metres of the cliff path here from May to early August, which is unusually close for Britain.

title: Ride the funicular and walk the Cairngorm plateau
description: The largest area of arctic-alpine plateau in Britain, with reindeer, ptarmigan and weather that turns in minutes.

title: Kayak among the Slate Islands
description: Flooded slate quarries and the Corryvreckan whirlpool nearby, third largest in the world. Go with a guide for the tide.

title: Walk the Speyside whisky trail
description: Half of Scotland's distilleries in one river valley, linked by a walking route on an old railway line.

title: Walk a stage of the Pembrokeshire Coast Path
description: Two hundred and ninety kilometres around the only coastal national park in Britain, with more ascent overall than Everest.

title: Take the boat to Skomer for the puffins
description: Forty thousand puffins and the world's largest Manx shearwater colony. Landing numbers are capped; go on the first boat.

title: Ride the Ffestiniog narrow gauge railway
description: The oldest independent railway company in the world, built in 1836 to bring slate down to Porthmadog by gravity.

title: Cross the Devil's Bridge at the Aberglaslyn Pass
description: A river gorge path along an old railway ledge with chains bolted to the rock where the footing runs out.

title: Zip line over a slate quarry at Penrhyn
description: The fastest zip line in the world at over 160 kilometres an hour, strung across a working slate quarry.

title: Walk the walls of Conwy Castle town
description: Edward I's ring of castles, and the most complete set of medieval town walls in Britain still walkable end to end.

title: Walk the four waterfalls at Ystradfellte
description: You can walk behind Sgwd yr Eira, which drops over an overhang into a pool. The path is genuinely slippery all year.

title: Look for red kites at Bwlch Nant yr Arian
description: Red kites were down to a handful of Welsh pairs in the 1930s. A hundred and more now come in to feed here every afternoon.

title: Cross the Carrick-a-Rede rope bridge
description: A rope bridge thirty metres above the sea to a salmon fishermen's island. Timed tickets, and it closes in high wind.

title: Walk the Dark Hedges avenue
description: A beech avenue planted in the eighteenth century, now closed to traffic after too many people stopped in the middle of the road.

title: Walk the Mourne Wall in the Mournes
description: Thirty-five kilometres of drystone wall built over the summits between 1904 and 1922 to enclose a reservoir catchment.

title: Go underground at Marble Arch Caves
description: A show cave you enter partly by boat, on a global geopark that crosses the border into Cavan.

title: Be first through the gate at the Acropolis
description: The site opens at eight and the marble is lethal in the afternoon heat. The Parthenon has been under restoration since 1975 and will be for a while yet.

title: See the Parthenon marbles that are still in Athens
description: The top floor is laid out to the exact dimensions of the Parthenon, with plaster casts standing in for the pieces held in London.

title: Walk up Lycabettus for the sunset
description: Two hundred and seventy-seven metres above the city, with the Acropolis below and the Saronic Gulf beyond. A funicular runs if you would rather.

title: Eat your way through the Varvakios market
description: The central meat and fish market, with tavernas inside it that open at dawn and serve patsas to people finishing a night shift.

title: Watch the sun go down at the Temple of Poseidon
description: A fifth-century BC temple on a headland an hour from Athens. Byron carved his name into a column, which you should not copy.

title: Test the acoustics at the theatre of Epidaurus
description: Fourteen thousand seats, and a coin dropped in the orchestra is audible in the back row. Summer festival performances still use it.

title: Walk through the Lion Gate at Mycenae
description: The citadel of Agamemnon, with a beehive tomb outside the walls that held the largest unsupported span in Europe for a thousand years.

title: Explore the ghost city of Mystras
description: A Byzantine capital abandoned on a mountainside above Sparta, with frescoed churches and a palace scattered down the slope.

title: Drive the tower villages of the Mani
description: Stone tower houses built for blood feuds, on a bare limestone peninsula that stayed effectively independent for centuries.

title: Walk the stadium at ancient Olympia
description: The original stadium track is still there and you can run the length of it. The games ran here every four years for over a millennium.

title: Stand where the oracle spoke at Delphi
description: The Greeks considered this the navel of the world. The site climbs the mountainside, so the walk up is part of it.

title: Cross the stone bridges of the Zagori
description: Forty-six slate villages linked by arched packhorse bridges, above the Vikos gorge, which is among the deepest in the world.

title: Row to the island in Lake Pamvotida
description: A lake island with no cars, monasteries and the house where Ali Pasha was finally shot through the floorboards in 1822.

title: Ride the Pelion narrow gauge train
description: A 60-centimetre gauge line designed by the father of the painter de Chirico, winding through chestnut forest to the sea.

title: Walk to the summit of Mount Olympus
description: Two thousand nine hundred and eighteen metres, with a refuge halfway and a genuine scramble on the final summit of Mytikas.

title: Eat bougatsa in Thessaloniki in the morning
description: Filo pastry with semolina custard, dusted with icing sugar and cut up with scissors. Greece's second city takes breakfast seriously.

title: See the frescoes at Kastoria's Byzantine churches
description: Fifty-four surviving Byzantine churches around a lakeside town that made its money on fur, most of them small and unlocked on request.

title: Swim in the lagoon at Balos
description: Pink-tinged sand and shallow water at the top corner of Crete, down a rough track or by boat from Kissamos.

title: Walk the palace at Knossos
description: The Minoan palace Evans partly rebuilt in concrete, controversially. Go to the Heraklion museum afterwards for the originals.

title: Ride the boat to Spinalonga
description: A Venetian fortress island used as a leper colony until 1957, and the last one in Europe to close.

title: Walk the Preveli palm gorge to the beach
description: A freshwater river running through a palm forest to a beach, which is not a combination Greece offers often.

title: Climb to the unfinished kouros of Naxos
description: A ten-metre marble statue abandoned in the quarry where it cracked, lying on its back in an orchard since the seventh century BC.

title: Take a boat to Kleftiko on Milos
description: White volcanic rock formations and sea caves used by pirates, reachable only from the water.

title: Walk the medieval street of the Knights
description: The largest inhabited medieval town in Europe, built by the Knights Hospitaller and still lived in behind four kilometres of wall.

title: Arrive into Symi harbour by boat
description: Neoclassical houses in ochre and blue stacked around a horseshoe harbour, built on sponge money and barely altered since.

title: See the cave of the Apocalypse on Patmos
description: The cave where John is said to have received the Revelation, under a fortified monastery that has run since 1088.

title: Walk to the monastery on the cliff at Amorgos
description: A white monastery three metres deep and eight storeys tall, glued to a vertical cliff three hundred metres above the sea.

title: Swim at the Canal d'Amour on Corfu
description: Soft sandstone eroded into channels and arches on the north coast, with the swim-through the whole place is named for.

title: Look down on the shipwreck at Navagio
description: A smuggler's freighter beached in 1980 on white cliffs and blue water. The clifftop viewing platform has been moved for rockfalls.

title: Row on the underground lake at Melissani
description: The cave roof collapsed, so at midday the sun drops straight onto water that reads as electric blue.

title: Walk the petrified forest of Lesbos
description: Twenty-million-year-old sequoia trunks turned to stone by volcanic ash, standing upright where they grew.

title: Swim in the vathres rock pools of Samothraki
description: Granite plunge pools fed by waterfalls off Mount Saos, on an island with no airport and very little tourism.

title: Walk up to the Panagia above Chora
description: A zigzag path from a cliff-edge village to a whitewashed church, with the Aegean two hundred metres straight down.

title: Stand on the floor of the Colosseum
description: The arena-floor and underground tickets are separate and sell out weeks ahead. Book the full experience or you only see it from the stands.

title: Look up through the open oculus of the Pantheon
description: The largest unreinforced concrete dome ever built, still standing after nineteen centuries. Go when it rains and watch the water fall through the hole.

title: Walk the Appian Way out of the city
description: Original Roman basalt paving, closed to traffic on Sundays. Hire a bike at the park office and ride out past the tombs and aqueducts.

title: See the Sistine Chapel at opening
description: Four kilometres of galleries before you reach the chapel. The first entry slot of the day is the only one that is not shoulder to shoulder.

title: Look through the Aventine keyhole
description: A keyhole in a green door frames St Peter's dome perfectly down an avenue of hedges. There is usually a small queue of people who know.

title: Eat cacio e pepe in Testaccio
description: The old slaughterhouse quarter, and still where Romans eat. Four ingredients, and every trattoria will tell you the others do it wrong.

title: Descend through the layers of San Clemente
description: A twelfth-century basilica on a fourth-century church on a first-century Mithraic temple. You walk down through all three.

title: Climb to the abandoned town of Civita di Bagnoregio
description: A village on a crumbling tufa pillar, reached by a single footbridge. Its nickname is the dying town, and the cliff really is going.

title: Find the hundred fountains at Villa d'Este
description: A Renaissance water garden running entirely on gravity, with an organ that plays using nothing but falling water.

title: Climb Brunelleschi's dome
description: 463 steps up between the inner and outer shells of a dome nobody could explain how to build until he did it.

title: See the David without the queue
description: Book a timed slot; the walk-up line regularly runs two hours. The unfinished Prisoners in the corridor are the better surprise.

title: Cross the Ponte Vecchio before the shops open
description: The only Florence bridge the retreating Germans left standing in 1944. At seven in the morning it is empty and the shutters are still down.

title: Sit in the shell of the Piazza del Campo
description: A sloping brick fan divided into nine segments for the nine merchants who governed Siena. The Palio is run around its edge twice a summer.

title: Drive the cypress roads of the Val d'Orcia
description: The landscape every idea of Tuscany comes from. The road from San Quirico to Pienza at dawn is the one you have seen in photographs.

title: Count the towers of San Gimignano
description: Fourteen of the original seventy-two medieval tower houses still stand, built by families competing to be tallest.

title: See the leaning tower and then go inside it
description: Climbing it is the part most people skip. The floor tilts under you on the way up, which the photographs cannot convey.

title: Soak in the free hot cascades at Saturnia
description: Sulphur water at 37 degrees pouring over travertine terraces, open all night and free. Go before seven or after dark.

title: Cycle around the island of Elba
description: Napoleon's first exile, and a proper island of granite coves and steep back roads an hour off the Tuscan coast.

title: Get lost in Cannaregio away from San Marco
description: The quarter where Venetians actually live, with the world's first ghetto at its heart and bacari serving cicchetti along the canals.

title: Ride the number 1 vaporetto down the Grand Canal
description: The slow boat that stops everywhere, which is the point. Stand at the back and it costs a fraction of a gondola.

title: Watch glass being blown on Murano
description: The furnaces were moved out to the island in 1291 so they would not burn Venice down. Go to a working studio, not a showroom.

title: See an opera in the Roman arena at Verona
description: A first-century amphitheatre that has staged opera every summer since 1913. The cheap stone steps are the authentic seats.

title: Walk the Alta Via 1
description: One hundred and twenty kilometres north to south through the Dolomites, sleeping in mountain rifugi. Book the huts months ahead.

title: Meet Otzi the iceman
description: A 5,300-year-old man found melting out of a glacier in 1991, kept in a cold cell you view through a small window.

title: Walk the largest high alpine meadow in Europe
description: Fifty square kilometres of rolling pasture at 2,000 metres, with the Sassolungo standing over it. Cars are barred during the day.

title: Drink coffee in a Trieste caffe
description: An Austro-Hungarian port that still orders coffee in its own vocabulary. Ask for a nero and you get an espresso.

title: See the Roman mosaics at Aquileia
description: Seven hundred and fifty square metres of fourth-century mosaic floor under a basilica, walked over on raised glass.

title: Book ahead for the Last Supper
description: Fifteen minutes in a climate-controlled room, twenty-five people at a time. Tickets are released quarterly and go in minutes.

title: Walk the roof of the Duomo di Milano
description: You can walk among the spires and 3,400 statues on the roof. Take the stairs rather than the lift for the better approach.

title: Take the ferry between the Lake Como villages
description: Varenna, Bellagio and Menaggio sit at the fork of the lake, twenty minutes apart by boat and impossible by road in summer.

title: Ride the Bernina Express over the Alps
description: The highest rail crossing in the Alps without a rack, from Tirano up to 2,253 metres and down into Switzerland. World heritage listed.

title: Climb the Mole Antonelliana in a glass lift
description: A lift runs straight up the middle of the dome with no shaft around it, into the tallest museum building in the world.

title: Hunt truffles in the Langhe in autumn
description: White truffle season runs October to December. Go out with a trifolao and his dog at dawn, then eat what you find.

title: Ride the Skyway to Punta Helbronner
description: A rotating cable car to 3,466 metres on the Italian side of Mont Blanc, looking across at the Matterhorn and Gran Paradiso.

title: Walk the coast path to San Fruttuoso
description: A tenth-century abbey in a cove with no road to it. Walk in over the headland from Portofino and take the boat back.

title: Eat focaccia in Genoa before ten in the morning
description: Genoese focaccia is a breakfast food, dipped in cappuccino by people who will not apologise for it.

title: Walk the streets of Pompeii
description: Sixty-six hectares buried by Vesuvius in 79 AD. Go early, take water, and head for the quieter eastern insulae first.

title: See the better-preserved rooms at Herculaneum
description: Buried deeper and hotter than Pompeii, so the timber, doors and upper floors survived. Smaller, and far less crowded.

title: Climb to the crater rim of Vesuvius
description: A twenty-minute walk up cinder from the car park to a still-steaming crater, with the whole bay laid out below.

title: Eat a pizza where it was invented
description: Marinara or margherita, sixty seconds in a wood oven, eaten folded. The queue outside the famous places moves faster than it looks.

title: Walk the Path of the Gods above Positano
description: Eight kilometres along the ridge from Bomerano to Nocelle, six hundred metres above the sea. Walk it downhill westward.

title: Row into the Blue Grotto
description: You lie flat in a rowing boat to get through the entrance. Only worth it in calm seas and midday light.

title: Stand in the Greek temples at Paestum
description: Three Doric temples from the sixth century BC, better preserved than almost anything in Greece, and usually near-empty.

title: Walk the Valley of the Temples at dusk
description: Seven Greek temples along a ridge above the sea. The site opens at night in summer, which is when to go.

title: Walk on the lava fields of Etna
description: Europe's most active volcano, and often erupting mildly enough to approach with a guide. The Sapienza refuge is the usual start.

title: Eat street food at the Ballaro market
description: Panelle, arancine and sfincione shouted at you in Sicilian. Palermo's markets are Arab in layout and still work that way.

title: Sit in the Greek theatre at Syracuse
description: Carved out of the rock in the fifth century BC and still staging Greek tragedy every May and June.

title: Watch Stromboli erupt after dark
description: The volcano has been erupting every twenty minutes or so for two thousand years. Boats sit offshore below the Sciara del Fuoco at night.

title: Walk the baroque staircases of Ragusa Ibla
description: Rebuilt after the 1693 earthquake in one continuous style, stacked down a ridge with 340 steps between the two halves of town.

title: Swim at Cala Goloritze
description: A white pebble cove under a limestone spire, reachable only on foot down a canyon or by boat. Numbers are capped daily.

title: Look inside a nuraghe
description: Bronze Age stone towers found nowhere else on earth. Sardinia has seven thousand of them; this is the one you can go inside.

title: Sleep in a trullo at Alberobello
description: Fifteen hundred conical drystone houses built without mortar so they could be pulled down when the tax inspector came.

title: Swim off the cliffs at Santa Maria di Leuca
description: The heel of Italy, where the Adriatic and Ionian meet and you can see the colour change from the lighthouse.

title: See the baroque stonework of Lecce
description: The local limestone is soft enough to carve like wood and hardens in the air, which is why every facade here is overrun with detail.

title: Fly the Volo dell'Angelo between two villages
description: A steel cable strung between Castelmezzano and Pietrapertosa, crossed lying flat at 120 kilometres an hour.

title: Walk to the basilica at Assisi
description: Giotto's fresco cycle of the life of St Francis, in a double basilica built into the hillside above the Umbrian plain.

title: Stand under the Cascata delle Marmore when they open the gates
description: A Roman-made waterfall of 165 metres, switched on and off to a published timetable because it feeds a power station.

title: Take a boat to the Spiaggia delle Due Sorelle
description: Two limestone stacks off a beach with no road access, under the Conero cliffs. Boats run from Numana in summer.

title: Eat tagliatelle al ragu in Bologna
description: The recipe is lodged with the Bologna chamber of commerce, and it is not spaghetti bolognese. Forty kilometres of porticoes to walk it off.

title: See the Byzantine mosaics at Ravenna
description: Fifth and sixth-century gold mosaic in eight buildings, the best surviving anywhere outside Istanbul.

title: Taste real balsamic in a Modena acetaia
description: Aged twelve to twenty-five years in a loft of shrinking barrels. It costs what it costs for a reason, and it is nothing like the supermarket version.

title: Climb to the lantern on top of St Peter's dome
description: Five hundred and fifty-one steps, the last of them leaning with the curve of the dome, to the highest point of the smallest country on earth.

title: Stand in the middle of Bernini's colonnade
description: Two granite discs mark the focal points. Stand on one and the four rows of columns line up into a single row.

title: Walk down to the necropolis under St Peter's
description: A Roman street of tombs beneath the basilica, with what is held to be Peter's grave at the end. Twelve people at a time, booked months ahead by email.

title: See the Vatican Gardens on a booked walk
description: Twenty-three hectares of formal garden covering half the country, and the only way to see the dome from behind.

title: Be there for the Wednesday general audience
description: Free tickets from the Prefecture, collected the day before. Held in the square in summer and the Paul VI hall in winter.

title: Walk out to Preikestolen
description: A flat 25-metre square of rock 604 metres above the Lysefjord, with no railing. Four kilometres each way over boardwalk and boulder.

title: Wedge yourself into Kjeragbolten
description: A boulder jammed in a crevice with a thousand metres of air below it. The walk in crosses three steep chain-assisted sections.

title: See the Fram and the Kon-Tiki in one afternoon
description: The ship that went furthest north and south, and the balsa raft that crossed the Pacific, on the same peninsula.

title: Walk the roof of the Oslo Opera House
description: White marble sloping straight out of the fjord, designed to be climbed. It is a public square that happens to be a roof.

title: Chase the aurora above the Arctic Circle
description: Three hundred and fifty kilometres inside the Arctic Circle and directly under the auroral oval. Chase inland if the coast is clouded.
