title: Drive the Senja national tourist route
description: Norway's second largest island, with the peaks of Lofoten and none of the crowds. Tungeneset and Bergsbotn are the stops.

title: Stand at the North Cape at midnight
description: The northernmost point reachable by road in Europe, with the sun still up at midnight from mid-May to the end of July.

title: Walk the Bryggen wharf in Bergen
description: Leaning wooden Hanseatic warehouses on the harbour, burned and rebuilt on the same medieval foundations for six hundred years.

title: Ride the Flam railway down to the fjord
description: Twenty kilometres and 866 metres of descent on one of the steepest adhesion railways in the world, with a waterfall stop.

title: Walk the Besseggen ridge
description: A knife-edge between a green lake and a blue one, four hundred metres apart in height. Boat in, walk out.

title: Look for polar bears from a boat in Svalbard
description: Seventy-eight degrees north, where leaving the settlements without a rifle and a guide is illegal for good reason.

title: See the Vasa, raised whole from the harbour
description: A warship that sank on her maiden voyage in 1628 and was lifted intact in 1961. Ninety-eight per cent original timber.

title: Kayak the Stockholm archipelago
description: Thirty thousand islands, with the right of public access letting you camp on almost any of them for a night.

title: Ride the Stockholm metro for the art
description: Ninety of the hundred stations are decorated, several blasted out of bedrock and left raw and painted. A day ticket is the gallery fee.

title: Sleep in the Icehotel at Jukkasjarvi
description: Rebuilt every December from Torne river ice and melted back into the river each spring. Sleeping bags rated to minus twenty.

title: Walk a stretch of the Kungsleden
description: The King's Trail runs 440 kilometres through Swedish Lapland, with mountain huts a day apart and no roads for most of it.

title: Eat oysters straight off the Bohuslan rocks
description: Sweden's west coast grows flat oysters that are still hand-picked by divers. The season runs when the water is cold.

title: Cycle the walled town of Visby and beyond
description: Three and a half kilometres of medieval wall around a Hanseatic town, and raukar sea stacks along the coast north of it.

title: See the midsummer poles go up in Dalarna
description: Midsummer is the real national holiday. Dalarna does it hardest: flower crowns, a raised pole and dancing until it never gets dark.

title: Swim in the harbour at Islands Brygge
description: The harbour was clean enough to open to swimmers in 2002, in the middle of the city, and it is free.

title: Cycle Copenhagen on the Cykelslangen
description: An elevated bike-only bridge curving over the harbour. Nearly half of all trips to work in this city are by bicycle.

title: Look at the Louisiana sculpture park by the sea
description: A modern art museum built into a garden above the Oresund, with Calder and Giacometti on the lawn facing Sweden.

title: Walk Your Rainbow Panorama at ARoS
description: A circular glass walkway on the roof in every colour of the spectrum, so the whole city changes hue as you go round.

title: Stand where two seas meet at Grenen
description: The Skagerrak and Kattegat collide on a sandspit, and you can see the two wave trains meeting head on.

title: Watch the black sun over the marshes
description: Up to a million starlings murmurate over the Wadden Sea marshes at dusk in spring and again in autumn.

title: Walk to the lake above the ocean at Sorvagsvatn
description: An optical illusion where a lake appears to hang a hundred metres above the sea. Technically Danish, and utterly its own place.

title: Take the ferry to Suomenlinna fortress
description: A sea fortress across six islands, built by Sweden, taken by Russia, now a suburb you reach on a commuter ferry.

title: Sit in the Loyly public sauna on the sea
description: There are more saunas than cars in Finland. This one has a ladder into the Baltic, which is the point in February.

title: Sit in silence in the Kamppi Chapel
description: A curved spruce shell in the middle of the busiest shopping district, built for nothing but quiet. No services, no charge.

title: Cross the Arctic Circle at Rovaniemi
description: The line is painted across the ground at Santa Claus Village, and the reindeer and huskies are a short drive out of town.

title: Sleep under a glass roof in Lapland
description: Glass igloos built so you can watch the aurora from bed without your face freezing.

title: Ski or walk to a wilderness hut in Lapland
description: Open wilderness huts, free and unlocked, are a Finnish institution. Take your own food and leave firewood for the next person.

title: Look for a Saimaa ringed seal
description: Fewer than five hundred exist, all in this one lake system, landlocked since the last ice age.

title: Cycle between the Aland islands on free ferries
description: A Swedish-speaking autonomous province of Finland, with small inter-island ferries that cyclists ride at no charge.

title: Swim in a Reykjavik neighbourhood pool
description: Geothermal outdoor pools open all year at 29 degrees, with hot pots at 44. Wash properly first; they will check.

title: Walk between two continental plates at Thingvellir
description: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge surfaces here, and the Icelandic parliament met on it from 930 AD. The plates pull apart two centimetres a year.

title: Watch Strokkur go off every few minutes
description: The original Geysir gave the world the word and now rarely erupts. Strokkur next door goes up twenty metres every five to ten minutes.

title: Walk behind Seljalandsfoss
description: A sixty-metre fall with a path around the back of the curtain. You will get soaked, and the path ices over in winter.

title: Stand on the black sand at Reynisfjara
description: Basalt columns and sneaker waves that have killed people. Watch the sea, never turn your back on it, and stay well up the beach.

title: Cross the Fimmvorduhals pass
description: Twenty-five kilometres between two glaciers, over ground that was a lava field in 2010, linking Skogar to Thorsmork.

title: Bathe in the Myvatn nature baths
description: The northern answer to the Blue Lagoon, half the price and a fraction of the crowd, beside a lake full of pseudocraters.

title: Watch whales from Husavik
description: Skjalfandi bay has humpbacks most of the summer and blue whales some years. Old oak schooners run the trips.

title: Feel Dettifoss from the east bank
description: The most powerful waterfall in Europe by volume. The east side road is rougher and puts you closer to the edge.

title: Drive the Snaefellsnes peninsula
description: Called Iceland in miniature: a glacier-capped volcano, lava fields, black churches and Kirkjufell all on one loop road.

title: Walk inside a blue ice cave
description: Caves melt out of the glacier each winter and collapse each spring, so no two seasons are the same. Guides only.

title: Walk the medieval walls of Tallinn old town
description: The most complete medieval town centre in northern Europe, with twenty towers still standing and a working town hall from 1404.

title: Visit the Soviet-era Patarei sea fortress
description: A tsarist artillery barracks turned Soviet prison, left almost exactly as it was when it closed in 2002.

title: Walk the bog boardwalks of Lahemaa
description: Raised bogs with pools you can swim in, manor houses and erratic boulders left by the ice, an hour from the capital.

title: Look into the Kaali meteorite crater
description: A crater lake blasted out about 3,500 years ago by a meteorite that hit a populated island, and turns up in Baltic folklore.

title: Look up at Riga's art nouveau facades
description: Riga has more art nouveau than any city in Europe, and one street where every building competes with its neighbour.

title: Eat in the zeppelin hangars of Riga Central Market
description: Five German airship hangars moved here in the 1920s, now one of the largest markets in Europe.

title: Ride the cable car over the Gauja valley
description: An open cable car strung across the valley since 1969, with sandstone caves and three castles in the forest below.

title: Stand where the Baltic meets the Gulf of Riga
description: Two seas meeting over a sandbar, on a coast that was a closed Soviet border zone and so was never developed.

title: Cross into the republic of Uzupis
description: A self-declared artists' republic across a river in Vilnius, with its own constitution bolted to a wall in forty languages.

title: See the interwar modernist architecture of Kaunas
description: Built fast when Kaunas was the temporary capital between the wars, and world heritage listed for it in 2023.

title: Add a cross to the Hill of Crosses
description: Bulldozed three times by the Soviets and rebuilt each night. Over a hundred thousand crosses now, and you may leave one.

title: Climb the dunes on the Curonian Spit
description: Ninety-eight kilometres of sand bar between lagoon and sea, with drifting dunes that buried villages in the nineteenth century.

title: Ride tram 28 through the Alfama
description: A 1930s wooden Remodelado grinding up the hills through the old Moorish quarter. Board at Martim Moniz early or you will stand.

title: Eat a pastel de nata where they were invented
description: The monks' recipe went to the bakery next door in 1837 and has not left the family since. Cinnamon on top, eaten warm, standing up.

title: Watch the sunset from a Lisbon miradouro
description: The highest of the city's viewpoints, with the castle, the river and the bridge all in one frame and a fraction of the crowd.

title: Hear fado in a small Alfama house
description: Two guitars and one voice, and the room goes silent when it starts. The tourist dinner shows are not the same thing.

title: Stand at the westernmost point of Europe
description: A cliff 140 metres above the Atlantic where the mainland runs out. Camoes called it the place where the land ends and the sea begins.

title: See the Joanina library in Coimbra
description: A baroque library that keeps a colony of bats to eat the insects that would otherwise eat the books. They are let out at night.

title: Walk to the Covao dos Conchos funnel
description: A perfectly circular spillway swallowing a lake into a tunnel, built in 1955 and looking entirely unnatural.

title: Cross the top deck of the Dom Luis I bridge
description: Designed by a student of Eiffel. The upper deck carries the metro and a footway 60 metres above the Douro.

title: Taste port in a Vila Nova de Gaia lodge
description: Every big port house has its cellars on the south bank. A tawny tasting flight explains more than any amount of reading.

title: Swim in the lagoons of Peneda-Geres
description: Portugal's only national park, with granite plunge pools, Roman milestones and wild garrano ponies in the hills.

title: Look inside the chapel of bones at Evora
description: Five thousand monks' bones set into the walls by friars making a point about mortality, with the point written over the door.

title: Stargaze on the Alqueva dark sky reserve
description: The world's first certified starlight tourism destination, over Europe's largest artificial lake.

title: Watch the Atlantic from Cabo de Sao Vicente
description: Where Henry the Navigator sent his ships out into the unknown. The lighthouse has one of the strongest beams in Europe.

title: Walk the Rota Vicentina fishermen's trail
description: A path along the cliff edge on sand, used by fishermen to reach their spots. Harder than it looks and far emptier than the south coast.

title: Walk a levada through the laurel forest
description: Irrigation channels cut into the cliffs from the 1500s, with footpaths beside them running into a UNESCO laurisilva forest.

title: Stand on the glass floor at Cabo Girao
description: The highest cliff skywalk in Europe, 580 metres straight down to terraced smallholdings on the shoreline.

title: Look down into the Sete Cidades crater
description: Twin lakes, one green and one blue, in a volcanic caldera. The Vista do Rei viewpoint is the classic, weather permitting.

title: Cook a stew in volcanic ground at Furnas
description: Cozido buried in the hot earth for six hours beside the fumaroles, then dug up at noon and served in the village.

title: Climb Pico, the highest point in Portugal
description: Two thousand three hundred and fifty-one metres of volcano straight out of the Atlantic. Registration and a tracker are compulsory.

title: See the Book of Kells at Trinity
description: A ninth-century gospel book, then the Long Room above it with two hundred thousand volumes on oak shelves.

title: Walk the Howth cliff loop
description: A headland at the end of the DART line, with a six-kilometre cliff path, seals in the harbour and puffins on Ireland's Eye.

title: Drink a pint where it was brewed
description: Seven floors up a giant glass pint, ending in a bar with a 360-degree view of the city. Learn to pour one on the way.

title: Stand inside Newgrange
description: A passage tomb from 3200 BC, older than the pyramids, built so the winter solstice sun runs down the passage to the chamber.

title: Drive the Slea Head loop
description: Beehive huts, a fifteen-hundred-year-old oratory and the Blasket Islands offshore, on a single-track road you drive clockwise.

title: Cycle the Gap of Dunloe
description: A glacial pass between the Purple Mountain and Macgillycuddy's Reeks, with a boat back across the Killarney lakes.

title: Walk the Slieve League cliffs
description: Six hundred metres, nearly three times the Cliffs of Moher, and with a fraction of the visitors. The One Man's Pass is the exposed bit.

title: Walk the Gobbins cliff path
description: An Edwardian path of bridges and tunnels bolted onto a basalt sea cliff, reopened in 2015 after eighty years derelict.

title: Walk the limestone pavement of the Burren
description: A hundred and fifty square kilometres of bare karst where Arctic, alpine and Mediterranean plants grow side by side in the cracks.

title: Take the cable car to Dursey Island
description: Ireland's only cable car, crossing a sound where the water rips through, to an island with no shop and almost no people.

title: Cycle the Great Western Greenway
description: Forty-two kilometres of traffic-free path on an old railway from Westport out to Achill Sound.

title: Climb Benbulben's flat top
description: A limestone table cut by glaciers, with Yeats buried in its shadow at Drumcliffe under his own epitaph.

title: Swim in the Limmat at a Zurich badi
description: The city swims in its own river. The Flussbad Oberer Letten lets you drift 400 metres downstream and climb out at the end.

title: Watch the Zytglogge clock strike
description: An astronomical clock from 1530 with a parade of bears four minutes before the hour. Einstein lived along the same street.

title: Ride the train up to the Jungfraujoch
description: Europe's highest railway station at 3,454 metres, through a tunnel inside the Eiger, onto the Aletsch ice.

title: Walk the Eiger Trail under the north face
description: Six kilometres directly beneath the 1,800-metre north wall, from Eigergletscher down to Alpiglen. Rockfall is audible.

title: See the Matterhorn from the Gornergrat
description: A cog railway to 3,089 metres facing the mountain, with twenty-nine four-thousand-metre peaks visible from the terrace.

title: Walk the larch forests of the Engadin in autumn
description: Larch is a conifer that turns gold and drops its needles. For two weeks in October the whole valley goes copper.

title: Swim in the Verzasca river
description: Water clear enough to look fake, over smooth grey and white rock. The dam upstream is the one Bond jumps off.

title: Cross the Chapel Bridge in Lucerne
description: A covered wooden bridge from 1333 with painted panels in the roof beams, rebuilt after a fire in 1993.

title: Ride the Gotthard Panorama Express
description: A paddle steamer across Lake Lucerne then a train up the old Gotthard line, which loops through the mountain three times.

title: Stand for a night at the Staatsoper
description: Standing tickets go on sale eighty minutes before curtain for a few euros. Tie a scarf to the rail to keep your place.

title: Sit all afternoon over one coffee
description: The Viennese coffee house is UNESCO-listed as an intangible tradition, and nobody will ask you to leave.

title: See the Klimt kiss at the Belvedere
description: The world's largest Klimt collection in a baroque palace, with the gold-leaf painting everyone comes for in one small room.

title: Go inside the Eisriesenwelt ice caves
description: The largest ice cave in the world, forty-two kilometres long. You carry a carbide lamp and climb 700 steps in the cold.

title: Tour the Hohensalzburg fortress
description: One of the largest fully preserved castles in Europe, never taken in nine hundred years, on a rock above Mozart's town.

title: Ride the Nordkette cable car from the old town
description: Twenty minutes from a medieval street to 2,256 metres, on a line with stations designed by Zaha Hadid.

title: Meet the Otztal glacier road
description: The highest paved road in Austria, running to 2,830 metres on a glacier that hosts the first World Cup ski race each October.

title: Climb the Schlossberg clock tower steps
description: Two hundred and sixty steps up a hill in the middle of Graz, to a clock tower whose hands are the wrong way round.

title: Swim in the Worthersee
description: An alpine lake that reaches 26 degrees in summer, warm enough to swim in without flinching, ringed by wooden bathhouses.

title: See the Night Watch at the Rijksmuseum
description: Rembrandt's militia painting, restored in public view behind glass. The library and the Asian pavilion are the quiet corners.

title: Book months ahead for the Anne Frank House
description: The annexe behind the bookcase, kept unfurnished at Otto Frank's request. Tickets release six weeks out and go in minutes.

title: See working windmills at Zaanse Schans
description: Industrial windmills still sawing timber and grinding pigment, moved here to be saved rather than built as a display.

title: Cycle the bulb fields around Keukenhof
description: Seven million bulbs planted every year, open only for eight weeks. The fields outside the gardens are free and just as good.

title: Sit on the wharf cellars in Utrecht
description: A canal with its quays a full storey below street level, the old goods cellars now cafes at the waterline.

title: Take the ferry to Terschelling
description: One of the Wadden islands, thirty kilometres of empty North Sea beach, cranberry fields and more bicycles than cars.

title: Drive the Delta Works storm barrier
description: Nine kilometres of barrier built after the 1953 flood, with sixty-two gates that close when the North Sea rises three metres.

title: Stand in the Grand-Place at night
description: Guild houses in gold leaf around a square Victor Hugo called the most beautiful in the world. Floodlit after dark.

title: Eat frites from a friture with the right sauce
description: Twice-fried in beef fat, in a paper cone, with one of about twenty sauces. Belgians will fight you over the choice.

title: Climb the Belfry of Bruges
description: Three hundred and sixty-six narrow steps to a carillon of forty-seven bells over a canal town that stopped growing in 1500.

title: See the Ghent Altarpiece after its restoration
description: Van Eyck's 1432 polyptych, the most stolen artwork in history, with one panel still missing since 1934.

title: Look at diamonds and Rubens in Antwerp
description: Eighty per cent of the world's rough diamonds pass through four streets here, next to the house Rubens built for himself.

title: Hear the Last Post at the Menin Gate
description: Buglers have sounded it every evening at eight since 1928, apart from the German occupation. Fifty-four thousand names with no known grave.

title: Walk the Ardennes at Durbuy
description: Billed as the smallest city in the world, on a bend in the Ourthe, with wooded hills and the Battle of the Bulge ground beyond.

title: Ride a boat lift on the Canal du Centre
description: Four Victorian hydraulic boat lifts still working, and a modern one that raises barges seventy-three metres in one go.

title: Walk the Bock casemates
description: Twenty-three kilometres of tunnel cut into the rock under the city, which sheltered thousands during the world wars.

title: Walk the Mullerthal Trail
description: Sandstone clefts, moss and ladders through what the country calls its Little Switzerland, an hour from the capital.

title: Take the chairlift above Vianden castle
description: A restored feudal castle on a spur over the Our valley, with an open chairlift up the hill opposite for the view back.

title: Eat currywurst standing up at a Berlin Imbiss
description: Invented by Herta Heuwer in 1949 from ration-shop ketchup and curry powder. Konnopke's has been under the U-Bahn viaduct since 1930.

title: Order a doner the way Berlin invented it
description: The doner in bread was a Berlin invention in the 1970s, not a Turkish one. Salad, sauce and grilled vegetables, which is the local difference.

title: Cycle the Schladitzer See and stop for a currywurst at Wolteritz
description: An open-cast lignite mine flooded into a lake north of Leipzig, with a flat ring road right around it. The beach cafe at Dorfstrasse 25, 04435 Schkeuditz does the currywurst you have earned by then.

title: Eat weisswurst before noon, as the rule demands
description: Made fresh each morning without preservatives, so tradition says they must not hear the midday bell. Sweet mustard, a pretzel, and you suck them out of the skin.

title: Buy a Dresdner Stollen at the Christmas market
description: Germany's oldest Christmas market, running since 1434, and the only place the protected Dresden stollen is sold by the people who bake it.

title: Drink Kolsch from a 200ml Stange until you say stop
description: The Kobes keeps replacing your small glass and marking your beer mat. Put the mat on top of the glass when you have had enough.

title: Eat a Thuringer Rostbratwurst off a charcoal grill
description: Protected by origin, at least 15cm long, and grilled over charcoal with mustard in a roll that is deliberately too small for it.

title: Eat a Fischbrotchen on the harbour
description: Pickled herring, onion and remoulade in a bread roll, eaten by the water. The northern answer to a sausage.

title: Eat a proper Wiener schnitzel, veal and hammered thin
description: If it is pork it is legally a schnitzel Wiener Art, not a Wiener schnitzel. Figlmuller's is pork and the size of the plate; Vienna forgives it.

title: Share a Salzburger Nockerl
description: Three baked peaks of sweetened egg white meant to look like the hills around the city. Made to order and collapses within minutes.

title: Scrape raclette off the wheel
description: Half a wheel of cheese held to the heat and scraped onto potatoes, gherkins and pickled onions. Winter food, and the Valais does it properly.

title: Eat Zurcher Geschnetzeltes with rosti
description: Veal in a cream and white wine sauce with a potato cake beside it, and the one dish the city claims outright.

title: Work through a Trappist beer list
description: Only a handful of breweries anywhere may call themselves Trappist and six of them are Belgian. Westvleteren is sold at the abbey gate by appointment.

title: Eat moules-frites in season
description: Mussels come from the Netherlands, the recipe is Belgian, and the season runs when there is an R in the month.

title: Eat raw herring the Dutch way, held by the tail
description: Hollandse Nieuwe lands in June, brined lightly and served with onion and pickle. Tip your head back and lower it in.

title: Order bitterballen with your beer
description: Crumbed balls of beef ragout, molten inside, served with mustard. The standard Dutch answer to a drink before dinner.

title: Eat bacalhau, one of the several hundred ways
description: Salt cod, imported from the Atlantic since the 1500s, and the country will tell you there is a recipe for every day of the year.

title: Take on a francesinha
description: Steak, sausage and ham between bread, buried in melted cheese and a beer-and-tomato sauce, with an egg and chips. One is a whole day.

title: Eat a full Irish with white and black pudding
description: Rashers, sausage, both puddings, egg, tomato and soda bread. The puddings are the part visitors skip and should not.

title: Eat Galway oysters straight from the bay
description: Native flat oysters, in season only when there is an R in the month, with a festival every September since 1954.

title: Eat pie and mash with liquor and jellied eels
description: A working London food older than fish and chips, down to a handful of shops. The green liquor is parsley sauce, not gravy.

title: Eat fish and chips at a proper seaside chippy
description: Fried in beef dripping in the north, cooked to order, salt and vinegar, eaten out of paper looking at the harbour.

title: Eat haggis, neeps and tatties
description: Sheep offal, oats and pepper in a casing. It is much better than its reputation, and there is a vegetarian version everywhere.

title: Try laverbread and cockles at Swansea market
description: Boiled seaweed rolled in oats and fried with bacon. Welsh breakfast, and an acquired taste worth acquiring.

title: Eat a canele fresh from the oven
description: Burnt-caramel crust, custard middle, baked in copper moulds lined with beeswax. Stale within hours, so buy them warm.

title: Eat bouillabaisse where the fishermen made it
description: Broth first with rouille and croutons, then the fish. A charter sets which species must be in it; anything cheap is not the real thing.

title: See a wheel of parmigiano cracked open
description: Dairies open for morning visits, and the wheels are tapped with a hammer to hear whether they have aged evenly.

title: Eat a cannolo filled to order
description: Sheep's-milk ricotta piped in as you order. Filled in advance the shell goes soft, and Sicilians will tell you so.

title: Eat paella where it comes from, at lunchtime
description: Rabbit, chicken and beans over wood, no chorizo, cooked at midday beside the rice paddies of the Albufera lagoon.

title: Eat fabada in an Asturian sidreria
description: White beans with chorizo, morcilla and pork belly. One bowl is lunch and most of the afternoon.

title: Eat souvlaki from a pita stand after midnight
description: Pork, tomato, onion, tzatziki and chips inside the pita, wrapped in paper. Ask for it apo ola and you get the lot.

title: Eat a Cretan dakos and drink raki with it
description: Barley rusk soaked in tomato with mizithra cheese, and the raki that arrives free at the end of every Cretan meal.

title: Eat pierogi at a milk bar
description: Bar mleczny are subsidised canteens left over from the communist era, still cheap and still serving the same dumplings.

title: Eat svickova with bread dumplings
description: Beef in a root vegetable cream sauce with cranberry and a spoon of whipped cream. The national dish, and rarely on tourist menus.

title: Eat goulash as the soup it actually is
description: Gulyas is a thin paprika soup, not the stew served abroad. The stew you are thinking of is porkolt.

title: Eat fuzi with truffle in Istria
description: Hand-rolled pasta with shaved truffle from the Motovun forest, in the Italian-influenced north-west.

title: Take a fika seriously
description: Coffee and a cardamom bun, sitting down, not at a desk. It is closer to an institution than a snack.

title: Eat fresh brown crab on the Bergen fish market
description: Landed that morning and dressed in front of you, on a quay that has traded fish since the 1200s.

title: Eat smorrebrod at lunchtime with a beer and a snaps
description: Open rye sandwiches, eaten in a set order from fish to meat to cheese. A lunch dish only, never dinner.

title: Eat a Karelian pie with egg butter
description: Rye crust around rice porridge, topped with butter mashed into boiled egg. Sold in every supermarket and eaten daily.

title: Eat an Icelandic hot dog with everything on it
description: Lamb in the sausage, crispy onions underneath, remoulade on top. Ask for eina med ollu and join the queue.

title: Eat sarmale with mamaliga and sour cream
description: Cabbage rolls stuffed with pork and rice, slow-cooked for hours, with polenta. Every family insists on their own version.

title: Eat banitsa for breakfast with ayran
description: Filo layered with white cheese and egg, sold hot from bakeries before work, with a salty yoghurt drink.

title: Eat cevapi with kajmak and onion
description: Small grilled minced-meat rolls in flatbread, with a clotted dairy spread the whole Balkans argues over.

title: Eat a balik ekmek off a boat at Eminonu
description: Grilled mackerel in bread, sold from boats rocking at the quay under Galata Bridge, with onion and lemon.

title: Sit at a ramen counter and order from the machine
description: You buy a ticket from a vending machine at the door and hand it over. Regional styles differ completely: tonkotsu, shoyu, miso, shio.

title: Eat okonomiyaki cooked on the counter in front of you
description: Cabbage batter cooked on a hotplate with whatever you choose in it. Osaka mixes it; Hiroshima layers it and adds noodles.

title: Eat yudofu at a temple restaurant
description: Simmered tofu in kombu broth, developed by Zen monks who ate no meat. Kyoto's soft water is the reason its tofu is famous.

title: Eat boat noodles by the bowl until you stack them
description: Tiny intensely spiced bowls, once sold from canal boats. You keep ordering and the empties pile up as the bill.

title: Eat khao soi in the north
description: Coconut curry noodles with crisp noodles on top, pickled mustard greens and lime. Northern Thai, and barely known abroad.

title: Eat bun cha at lunchtime in Hanoi
description: Grilled pork patties in a bowl of sweet-sour broth with cold noodles and herbs. A lunch dish; the stalls close by two.

title: Eat com tam, broken rice with grilled pork
description: Rice grains broken in milling, once the cheap leftover and now a Saigon breakfast in its own right.

title: Grill your own Korean barbecue with the banchan
description: The side dishes come free and are refilled. Wrap the meat in lettuce with ssamjang and eat it in one bite.

title: Eat bibimbap in the city it comes from
description: Jeonju's version uses beef tartare and rice cooked in beef broth. Mix it thoroughly; not mixing it is the mistake.

title: Eat a Sichuan hotpot and learn what ma la means
description: Numbing peppercorn as well as chilli heat. Order a split pot if you want to be able to taste anything afterwards.

title: Take yum cha slowly on a Sunday morning
description: Tea first, then trolleys. Tap two fingers on the table when someone pours for you; it means thank you.

title: Eat roujiamo and biangbiang noodles in the Muslim Quarter
description: A pork or beef flatbread sandwich claimed as the world's oldest, and a noodle whose character has 58 strokes.

title: Eat chaat in Old Delhi
description: Sweet, sour, hot and crunchy at once. Go where there is a queue and where the water is bottled.

title: Eat a South Indian thali off a banana leaf
description: Endless refills of rice, sambar, rasam and curd, eaten with the right hand. Fold the leaf towards you when you finish.

title: Eat Amritsari kulcha with chole
description: Stuffed bread baked in a tandoor until blistered, crushed with butter, and eaten with chickpeas at a roadside dhaba.

title: Eat assam laksa at a Penang hawker stall
description: Sour tamarind and mackerel broth with thick rice noodles, mint and pineapple. Nothing like the coconut laksa elsewhere.

title: Eat chilli crab with mantou to mop it up
description: Invented in Singapore in the 1950s. Order the fried buns; the sauce is the point and you will want to finish it.

title: Eat gudeg for breakfast in Yogyakarta
description: Young jackfruit stewed for hours in palm sugar and coconut until it goes mahogany. Sweet, and eaten first thing.

title: Eat Cebu lechon carved off the spit
description: Roasted whole over charcoal, stuffed with lemongrass and needing no sauce, which is the Cebuano boast.

title: Eat rice and curry with five or six sides
description: The everyday meal: rice, a curry, a mallum, a sambol and a papadam, mixed with your fingers on the plate.

title: Eat momos with tomato achar
description: Steamed or fried dumplings from the Newar kitchens of the valley, with a roasted tomato and sesame dip.

title: Eat plov cooked in a kazan the size of a table
description: Rice, lamb, carrot and whole garlic, cooked in the morning and sold until it runs out. Every city cooks it differently.

title: Eat khuushuur and drink suutei tsai
description: Fried mutton pastries and salted milk tea. Refusing the tea in a ger is worse manners than not finishing it.

title: Work through a Taipei night market
description: Oyster omelette, beef noodle soup, pepper buns. Stinky tofu is the test; the smell is far worse than the taste.

title: Eat fish amok steamed in a banana leaf
description: Freshwater fish in coconut and kroeung curry paste, steamed rather than boiled, which is what makes it Khmer.

title: Eat mohinga for breakfast
description: Catfish and banana-stem soup with rice noodles, sold from pavement stalls before seven. The national breakfast.

title: Eat ema datshi and mean it
description: Whole chillies stewed in yak cheese. Chilli is the vegetable here, not the seasoning, and the national dish is unapologetic.

title: Eat a full mezze until the table runs out of room
description: Twenty small plates before anything grilled arrives. Order less than you think and it will still be too much.

title: Eat hummus at a dedicated hummusia at breakfast
description: Warm, with olive oil, chickpeas and pita, eaten in the morning at a place that sells nothing else and closes by two.

title: Eat mansaf, and eat it with your right hand
description: Lamb cooked in fermented dried yoghurt over rice and flatbread. The national dish, and a communal one.

title: Eat baklava where it is taken most seriously
description: Forty layers, Antep pistachios, protected by origin. The city has a UNESCO listing for its cooking.

title: Eat machboos and luqaimat at an Emirati table
description: Spiced rice with meat, then dumplings in date syrup. Emirati food is surprisingly hard to find in Dubai unless you look.

title: Eat tacos al pastor cut off the trompo
description: Lebanese shawarma technique on pork with pineapple, brought by immigrants to Puebla in the 1930s. Two small tortillas, always.

title: Eat mole negro in Oaxaca
description: More than thirty ingredients including chocolate and several chillies, cooked over a day. Oaxaca claims seven distinct moles.

title: Eat gumbo and beignets on the same day
description: A roux the colour of a copper penny, and square doughnuts under an unreasonable quantity of icing sugar at Cafe du Monde.

title: Queue for Central Texas brisket at opening
description: Post oak, salt and pepper, twelve hours, no sauce. The good places sell out by early afternoon and the queue starts before opening.

title: Eat a slice folded, standing at the counter
description: Thin, wide, foldable, sold by the slice. The dollar slice is mostly gone but the fold is not negotiable.

title: Eat poutine after midnight
description: Chips, gravy and cheese curds that must squeak. If they do not squeak they are not fresh enough.

title: Eat a Montreal bagel straight from the wood oven
description: Boiled in honey water and baked over wood. Smaller, sweeter and denser than the New York kind, and open all night.

title: Eat jerk pork from a drum pan at Boston Bay
description: Where jerk was commercialised, cooked over pimento wood in a split oil drum. Scotch bonnet, allspice and smoke.

title: Order coffee the way Melbourne taught the world
description: The flat white, the magic and a serious argument about roasts. Italian and Greek migration built this, not a chain.

title: Eat a hangi cooked in the ground
description: Meat and vegetables steamed in an earth oven for hours. In Rotorua some are cooked using geothermal steam instead of hot rocks.

title: Walk the Campuhan Ridge at first light in Ubud
description: A 2km grass ridge between two rivers, quiet before seven and unbearably hot after nine. The obvious first morning in Ubud.

title: See the Tegallalang rice terraces before the buses
description: Terraces watered by subak, a cooperative irrigation system run by temple priests since the ninth century and now World Heritage listed.

title: Get robbed by macaques in the Sacred Monkey Forest
description: Around 1,200 long-tailed macaques in a temple complex in the middle of town. They will take sunglasses, phones and anything shiny - leave it in the room.

title: Bathe in the holy springs at Tirta Empul
description: A purification ritual Balinese Hindus have performed since 962 CE. Sarong required, and the queue moves spout by spout in a set order.

title: Watch a Legong performance in Ubud Palace
description: Gamelan and masked dance in the palace courtyard nearly every evening - a living tradition rather than a tourist show, and cheap.

title: Climb Mount Batur for sunrise
description: A 2am start up an active volcano to watch the sun come up over Lombok. Local guides are effectively compulsory and the trail is enforced as such.

title: See the lake temple at Ulun Danu Beratan
description: A water temple appearing to float on Lake Beratan in the highlands, dedicated to the goddess of lakes and rivers. It is on the 50,000 rupiah note.

title: Walk between the Jatiluwih rice terraces
description: Far larger and far quieter than Tegallalang, with walking loops through working terraces rather than a viewpoint you photograph from a cafe.

title: Swim under Sekumpul Falls
description: Seven falls dropping into one gorge in north Bali, reached by several hundred steps and a river crossing. Widely rated the island's best.

title: Watch the sunrise gate at Lempuyang
description: The Gates of Heaven framing Mount Agung. The famous reflection is a mirror held under a phone by the photographer - everyone queues for hours for it anyway.

title: Snorkel the USAT Liberty wreck at Tulamben
description: A torpedoed US cargo ship pushed off the beach by the 1963 Agung eruption, now lying 30m from shore in water shallow enough to snorkel.

title: Explore the water palace at Tirta Gangga
description: Stepping stones across carp ponds in a royal water garden built in 1946, rebuilt after Agung buried it seventeen years later.

title: Watch the Kecak fire dance at Uluwatu at sunset
description: A sea temple on a 70m cliff, with a chanting circle of about seventy men performing the Ramayana as the sun goes down behind them.

title: Learn to surf the beach break at Canggu
description: Black volcanic sand, forgiving waves at Batu Bolong, and the centre of gravity for Bali's remote-working scene.

title: Surf or watch the reef break at Uluwatu
description: You paddle out through a cave in the cliff. A world-class left over shallow reef, and unforgiving of anyone who overestimates themselves.

title: Eat babi guling in a warung
description: Spit-roast suckling pig stuffed with turmeric, lemongrass and chilli - a ceremonial dish that most warungs sell out of by early afternoon.

title: Look down on Kelingking Beach from the cliff
description: A headland shaped like a dinosaur on Nusa Penida. The descent to the sand is a near-vertical scramble on bamboo rails - people are hurt on it regularly.

title: Snorkel with manta rays at Nusa Penida
description: Reef mantas visit a cleaning station here year-round. The swell can be heavy, and the boat ride out is not for anyone prone to seasickness.

title: Cycle the flat lanes of Nusa Lembongan
description: Seaweed farms, a yellow suspension bridge to Nusa Ceningan, and a fraction of the traffic of Penida next door.

title: Watch dawn break over Borobudur
description: The largest Buddhist temple on earth, built around 800 CE and abandoned for centuries under volcanic ash. Climbing to the upper terraces is now capped and guided.

title: Walk the temple complex at Prambanan
description: A ninth-century Hindu complex of towering candi, badly damaged in the 2006 earthquake and still under restoration. The Ramayana ballet runs here in the dry season.

title: See batik being drawn by hand in Yogyakarta
description: A sultanate city and the cultural centre of Java, where batik tulis is still drawn line by line with a wax pen rather than stamped.

title: Watch sunrise over Mount Bromo from Penanjakan
description: A smoking cone inside a caldera called the Sea of Sand, with Semeru erupting on the horizon behind it. A 3am jeep and genuinely cold at altitude.

title: See the blue fire at Kawah Ijen
description: Ignited sulphuric gas burning electric blue in the dark, above a turquoise acid lake. Gas masks are essential, and miners still carry 80kg of sulphur out by hand.

title: Ride to the crater rim at Tumpak Sewu
description: A 120m curtain of water in a horseshoe amphitheatre. The descent to the base is bamboo ladders and rope in permanent spray - hard, and slippery.

title: Eat your way through a Jakarta street food night
description: Nasi goreng, satay, martabak and kerak telor from carts that appear after dark, in a city of ten million with a food scene drawn from every island.

title: Look into the crater lake at Kawah Putih
description: A pale turquoise sulphur lake in a crater above Bandung, sitting at 2,400m so the air is cool and faintly acidic.

title: Track Komodo dragons on Rinca
description: The largest lizard on earth at up to 3m, found wild on five islands and nowhere else. Rangers carry forked sticks, which is less reassuring in person.

title: Climb Padar Island for the three-bay view
description: About 800 steps to a ridge overlooking three crescent bays, each with differently coloured sand. The most photographed view in eastern Indonesia.

title: Snorkel the pink sand at Komodo
description: Red organ-pipe coral fragments mixed through white sand give the colour - one of only a handful of genuinely pink beaches anywhere.

title: See the three coloured lakes of Kelimutu
description: Three crater lakes that independently change colour - red, green, black, turquoise - as their mineral chemistry shifts. Local belief holds they receive the dead.

title: Climb Mount Rinjani to the crater rim
description: 3,726m, usually done over three days with porters, to a crater holding a lake and a new cone growing inside it. Genuinely hard, and closed in the wet.

title: Snorkel with turtles off Gili Trawangan
description: Three car-free islands where transport is bicycle or horse cart, with green turtles grazing in water shallow enough to snorkel from the beach.

title: Surf the point at Kuta Lombok
description: A string of horseshoe bays with reef breaks for every level, and a fraction of Bali's crowds despite the airport being twenty minutes away.

title: Dive Raja Ampat, the richest reef on earth
description: Surveys record over 1,500 fish and 550 coral species - the highest marine biodiversity ever measured. Getting there takes two flights and a boat.

title: Climb Piaynemo for the karst lagoon view
description: A boardwalk and 320 steps to a platform above a scatter of mushroom-shaped karst islets - the view that defines Raja Ampat in photographs.

title: Dive the wall at Bunaken
description: A vertical coral wall dropping to well over 1,000m, with visibility routinely past 30m and turtles at almost every depth.

title: Muck dive the Lembeh Strait
description: Black volcanic sand rather than coral, and the best critter diving in the world - mimic octopus, hairy frogfish, blue-ringed octopus, all on one dive.

title: Attend a Torajan funeral ceremony
description: Funerals here last days and can happen years after death, with the deceased kept at home in the meantime. Visitors are genuinely welcomed - bring a gift and a guide.

title: Trek to see orangutans at Bukit Lawang
description: Sumatran orangutans in the wild on the edge of Gunung Leuser - one of only two places on earth where the species survives, and it is critically endangered.

title: Stay on Samosir Island in Lake Toba
description: The largest volcanic lake on earth, filling a caldera left by an eruption 74,000 years ago that may have nearly wiped out early humans.

title: Surf the Mentawai Islands
description: Reeled-off perfect reef breaks reached by charter boat from Padang, and among the most consistent waves anywhere in the world.

title: Island-hop the Karimunjawa archipelago
description: 27 islands in a marine park off Java's north coast, most uninhabited, reached by a slow ferry that puts most travellers off entirely.

title: Swim in a cenote near Valladolid
description: Thousands of limestone sinkholes over a flooded cave system, sacred to the Maya and the peninsula's only natural fresh water.

title: Hear the Kukulkan pyramid echo at Chichen Itza
description: Clap at the base of El Castillo and the staircase returns a chirp said to imitate the quetzal. Twice a year a serpent shadow runs down the steps.

title: Ride El Chepe through Copper Canyon
description: A canyon system deeper and four times larger than the Grand Canyon, crossed by a railway with 37 bridges and 86 tunnels.

title: Eat your way through the Oaxaca markets
description: Seven moles, tlayudas, mezcal and chapulines - widely held to be the best regional cooking in Mexico, and it is not close.

title: Meet grey whales in San Ignacio Lagoon
description: Grey whales calve here and mothers routinely push their calves up to the boats to be touched - one of the strangest wildlife encounters anywhere.

title: Snorkel the reef at Akumal
description: Part of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef, the second largest on earth, with green turtles grazing the seagrass close to shore.

title: Climb the Pyramid of the Sun at Teotihuacan
description: A city of over 100,000 people that was already ruins when the Aztecs found it and named it the place where gods were born. Summit access varies - check on arrival.

title: See the Aztec Sun Stone at the Museo Nacional de Antropologia
description: Widely rated among the best museums in the world - the 24-tonne Sun Stone, the Maya collection, and a courtyard fountain shaped like an umbrella.

title: Ride a trajinera through the canals of Xochimilco
description: The last surviving stretch of the Aztec canal and floating-garden system, with painted boats, mariachi for hire and the unsettling Isla de las Munecas.

title: Visit the Casa Azul, Frida Kahlo's house
description: The cobalt house in Coyoacan where she was born and died, kept as she left it. Tickets must be booked online and sell out days ahead.

title: See a lucha libre bout at Arena Mexico
description: Masked wrestling in a 16,000-seat cathedral of the sport, where the crowd's insults are half the performance. Friday nights are the big card.

title: Eat tacos al pastor from a spinning trompo
description: Lebanese shawarma technique applied to marinated pork, carved onto a small tortilla with pineapple flicked on top. Mexico City's defining street food.

title: Stand in the Zocalo and the Templo Mayor beside it
description: One of the largest city squares in the world, built directly over Tenochtitlan - the Aztec temple was found in 1978 by electricity workers digging a trench.

title: Climb the ruins at Uxmal
description: Puuc-style Maya architecture with an oval-based pyramid found nowhere else, and a fraction of the crowds at Chichen Itza an hour away.

title: Swim in the cenote at Ik Kil
description: An open cenote 26m down with vines hanging to the water. Busy - the quieter ones near Valladolid are better if you have a car.

title: Watch flamingos at Rio Lagartos
description: A biosphere reserve holding tens of thousands of American flamingos, plus a pink salt lagoon coloured by the same algae as Australia's Hutt Lagoon.

title: Walk the Paseo de Montejo in Merida
description: A boulevard of mansions built on the henequen fibre boom, in a city repeatedly ranked among the safest in the Americas.

title: See the Maya ruins at Tulum above the sea
description: The only major Maya city built on the coast, walled on three sides, on a cliff above a beach you can swim from. Go at opening to beat both heat and buses.

title: Float the canals at Sian Ka'an
description: A World Heritage biosphere where you drift down ancient Maya-dug canals wearing a life jacket, carried by the current through mangrove.

title: Dive the cenote at Dos Ojos
description: Part of one of the longest underwater cave systems on earth, with halocline layers where fresh and salt water meet and the view goes blurry.

title: Swim with whale sharks off Isla Mujeres
description: One of the largest whale shark aggregations in the world gathers off the Yucatan each summer - hundreds of animals feeding on tuna spawn.

title: Dive the underwater sculpture museum at MUSA
description: More than 500 concrete figures sunk off Cancun by Jason deCaires Taylor, built from pH-neutral marine cement so coral colonises them.

title: Boat through the Sumidero Canyon
description: Walls up to 1,000m high on the Grijalva River, with crocodiles on the banks and a moss formation shaped like a Christmas tree.

title: Reach the jungle ruins of Palenque
description: Maya architecture at its most refined, still half-swallowed by rainforest with howler monkeys overhead. Pakal's tomb was found intact under the main temple.

title: Swim the turquoise cascades at Agua Azul
description: Limestone-rich water over travertine terraces gives the colour - though it browns after heavy rain, so the dry season is the only time it lives up to the name.

title: Spend a few days in San Cristobal de las Casas
description: A highland colonial town at 2,200m, and the centre of Tzotzil and Tzeltal Maya life - the church at nearby San Juan Chamula is unlike anywhere else.

title: Stand on the terraces at Monte Alban
description: A Zapotec capital built by levelling an entire mountaintop around 500 BCE, looking out over three valleys.

title: See the petrified waterfall at Hierve el Agua
description: Mineral springs have built a rock formation that looks exactly like a frozen waterfall, with infinity pools at the top. Access is sometimes closed by local disputes.

title: Spend Dia de Muertos in Oaxaca
description: Comparsas through the streets and families keeping vigil in the cemeteries. It is a family occasion, not a festival - go quietly and ask before photographing.

title: Watch turtles nest at Mazunte
description: A former turtle slaughtering village that reinvented itself as a conservation centre after the 1990 ban - olive ridleys now arrive in mass arribadas.

title: Tour an agave distillery in Tequila
description: The blue agave landscape here is World Heritage listed. A plant takes seven years to mature, and only spirit made in this region may use the name.

title: Hear mariachi in Plaza Garibaldi's home town
description: Mariachi, tequila and charreria all originate in Jalisco. The Hospicio Cabanas here holds Orozco murals painted across its chapel ceiling.

title: Wander the tunnels and alleys of Guanajuato
description: A silver city built in a ravine, where the roads run through former river tunnels under the town and the houses are painted every colour available.

title: Watch the light on the Parroquia in San Miguel de Allende
description: A neo-Gothic pink church designed by a self-taught stonemason from postcards of European cathedrals, in a World Heritage colonial town.

title: Eat mole poblano where it was invented
description: Twenty or more ingredients including chocolate and several chillies, ground for hours. Also the home of chiles en nogada, eaten in the two months poblano chillies are in season.

title: Find the church on top of the Great Pyramid of Cholula
description: By volume the largest pyramid on earth, so overgrown the Spanish mistook it for a hill and built a church on the summit in 1594.

title: Swim at Playa Balandra near La Paz
description: A shallow turquoise bay you can wade most of the way across, with daily visitor caps to protect it. Frequently voted Mexico's best beach.

title: See El Arco at Cabo San Lucas
description: A granite arch at the very tip of the Baja peninsula, where the Sea of Cortez meets the Pacific. Reachable only by water taxi.

title: Dive with sea lions at Espiritu Santo
description: A World Heritage island in the sea Cousteau called the aquarium of the world, with a sea lion colony that plays with snorkellers.

title: Stand in the monarch butterfly forests of Michoacan
description: Hundreds of millions of monarchs arrive after a 4,000km migration and cover the oyamel firs so densely the branches bend.

title: Climb the pyramid of the Niches at El Tajin
description: 365 recessed niches, one for each day. The voladores still perform outside - five men descending from a 30m pole on ropes, a rite recognised by UNESCO.

title: Ride the Basaseachi trail in the Copper Canyon
description: Mexico's second-highest waterfall at 246m, in Raramuri country - the people known for running enormous distances in sandals cut from tyres.

title: Walk the Siq into the Treasury at Petra
description: A 1.2km slot canyon opens onto a facade carved into the rock face by the Nabataeans around 2,000 years ago. Go at opening, before the canyon fills.

title: Climb the 800 steps to the Monastery at Petra
description: Larger than the Treasury and far quieter, because most visitors stop before the climb. A tea shack at the top looks out over the Wadi Araba.

title: Sleep in a Bedouin camp in Wadi Rum
description: Sandstone and granite towers in red desert, run by Bedouin tribes who hold the tourism rights. Stood in for Mars in half a dozen films.

title: Float in the Dead Sea
description: 430m below sea level, the lowest land on earth, and about ten times saltier than the ocean. It is also shrinking by roughly a metre a year.

title: Walk the colonnaded street at Jerash
description: One of the best-preserved Roman provincial cities anywhere, buried by earthquake and sand until the 1920s - the oval forum is almost intact.

title: Walk the Dana Biosphere Reserve
description: Jordan's largest reserve, dropping 1,500m from highland to desert through four biogeographic zones, on a village-run conservation model.

title: Dive the Red Sea reefs at Aqaba
description: Jordan's only coastline, 27km of it, with reefs unusually resilient to bleaching and a deliberately sunk C-130 Hercules at 17m.

title: Go up the Burj Khalifa at sunset
description: 828m and still the tallest building in the world by a wide margin. Book the sunset slot weeks ahead - it is the only one that consistently sells out.

title: Ride a 4WD over the dunes on a desert safari
description: Dune bashing, sandboarding and a camp dinner in the Al Marmoom reserve. Genuinely rough - not a good idea straight after eating.

title: Haggle in the Dubai gold and spice souks
description: Reached by abra across Dubai Creek for about a dirham. Roughly ten tonnes of gold sits in the windows at any time, and the price is always negotiable.

title: Visit the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
description: Holds 40,000 worshippers, with the largest hand-knotted carpet in the world on its floor. Free, and modest dress is provided at the entrance.

title: See the rain of light at Louvre Abu Dhabi
description: Jean Nouvel's 180m dome filters sun through eight layered star patterns, casting a shifting pattern of light on the galleries below.

title: Ride the world's longest zip line at Jebel Jais
description: 2.83km at up to 150km/h, flown head-first off the UAE's highest peak. The mountain road up is itself worth the drive.

title: Swim and climb through Wadi Shab
description: A boat across, 45 minutes on foot, then three pools to swim before squeezing through a crack in the rock to a waterfall inside a cave.

title: Walk the Balcony Walk on Jebel Shams
description: A ledge path along the rim of Wadi Ghul, called the Grand Canyon of Arabia, ending at an abandoned village cut into the cliff.

title: Camp in the Sharqiya Sands
description: Dunes up to 100m in bands of orange and white, still grazed by Bedouin herders. You let tyre pressure down at the edge and drive in.

title: Sail a dhow through the Musandam fjords
description: Sheer limestone inlets called the Norway of Arabia, on a peninsula separated from the rest of Oman by the UAE, with dolphins in the channels.

title: Go to the Friday goat market at Nizwa
description: Livestock paraded in a ring before dawn buyers, beside a 17th-century fort with a round tower built to survive cannon fire.

title: Watch green turtles nest at Ras al Jinz
description: One of the most important green turtle nesting sites in the Indian Ocean, with guided night and dawn visits from a reserve on the easternmost point of Arabia.

title: See Salalah green during the khareef
description: The monsoon turns a desert province green for three months a year - waterfalls, fog and the frankincense trees that made this coast rich.

title: Walk the Old City of Jerusalem
description: One square kilometre holding sites central to Judaism, Christianity and Islam. It sits in East Jerusalem, which most of the world regards as occupied territory.

title: Climb Masada for sunrise over the Dead Sea
description: A fortress on a desert plateau where a Jewish garrison held out against Rome until 73 CE. The Snake Path takes about an hour in the dark.

title: Float on the Sea of Galilee
description: Actually a freshwater lake, and the lowest on earth. The surrounding hills hold Capernaum and the Mount of Beatitudes.

title: Walk the Bauhaus White City in Tel Aviv
description: About 4,000 Bauhaus buildings put up by architects who fled Europe in the 1930s - the largest concentration anywhere, and World Heritage listed.

title: See Banksy's Walled Off Hotel in Bethlehem
description: A hotel built facing the separation wall, billed as having the worst view in the world, beside the Church of the Nativity. Entry is via Israeli checkpoint.

title: Walk the excavations at Jericho
description: Tell es-Sultan has evidence of settlement going back roughly 11,000 years, which makes it a contender for the oldest continuously inhabited place on earth.

title: Float over Cappadocia in a balloon at dawn
description: Up to 150 balloons lift at once over volcanic fairy chimneys. Flights are cancelled for wind more often than people expect - allow spare mornings.

title: Go down into the Derinkuyu underground city
description: Eighteen storeys cut into soft tuff, capable of sheltering 20,000 people with livestock, ventilation shafts and rolling stone doors.

title: Stand under the dome of the Hagia Sophia
description: Built as a cathedral in 537, converted to a mosque in 1453, a museum in 1935 and back to a mosque in 2020. Its dome went unmatched for a thousand years.

title: Get lost in the Grand Bazaar
description: Around 4,000 shops on 61 covered streets, trading since 1461 and among the oldest shopping complexes still operating anywhere.

title: Walk barefoot on the terraces at Pamukkale
description: White travertine terraces built by calcium-rich springs over millennia. Shoes are banned to protect them, and the Roman city of Hierapolis sits on top.

title: Walk the marble street at Ephesus
description: One of the largest Roman sites in the Mediterranean, with the Library of Celsus facade and a theatre that seated 25,000.

title: Watch sunrise among the heads on Mount Nemrut
description: Two-metre stone heads toppled from their bodies on a 2,134m summit, built as a tomb by a king who declared himself a god.

title: See the carved pillars at Gobekli Tepe
description: Monumental stone circles raised around 9500 BCE - roughly 6,000 years before Stonehenge, and by people who had not yet started farming.

title: See the Nabataean tombs at Hegra
description: Saudi Arabia's first World Heritage site - 111 tombs cut by the same civilisation that built Petra, and visited by a fraction of the numbers.

title: Stand at the Edge of the World near Riyadh
description: A 300m escarpment on the Tuwaiq cliffs where the plateau simply stops and an ancient seabed runs to the horizon. 4WD access only.

title: Walk the mud-brick city at Diriyah
description: At-Turaif, the original seat of the Saudi state, built in Najdi mud-brick and World Heritage listed since 2010.

title: Eat and haggle in Souq Waqif
description: Rebuilt in the traditional style on a centuries-old trading site, with a falcon souq and hospital in the middle of it.

title: See the collection at the Museum of Islamic Art
description: I M Pei came out of retirement at 91 to design it, on its own island so nothing could ever be built against it.

title: Drive to the inland sea at Khor Al Adaid
description: One of very few places on earth where the sea reaches into the heart of a desert, on the Saudi border and reachable only by 4WD across dunes.

title: Stand among the columns at Baalbek
description: The largest Roman temple complex ever built, with foundation stones over 800 tonnes that nobody has fully explained the moving of.

title: Take the boat through the Jeita Grotto
description: Two limestone caverns stacked over each other, the upper holding the largest known stalactite in the world at 8.2m, the lower toured by boat.

title: Walk the harbour at Byblos
description: Occupied for around 7,000 years and a candidate for the oldest continuously inhabited city. The Greek name for it gave us the word Bible.

title: Find the Tree of Life in the Bahraini desert
description: A mesquite standing alone in the desert for around 400 years with no obvious water source, roughly two kilometres from anything else.

title: Walk the layers at Qal'at al-Bahrain
description: A tell holding 4,000 years of continuous occupation, from the Dilmun civilisation up to a Portuguese fort on the top layer.

title: Go up the Kuwait Towers
description: Three towers finished in 1979, clad in eight million enamelled steel discs, badly damaged during the 1990 invasion and rebuilt afterwards.

title: Queue before dawn for the Church of the Holy Sepulchre
description: Six Christian denominations share custody under a centuries-old status quo, down to who may move an immovable ladder left on a windowsill since 1757. Arrive before 7am or the queue for the Edicule runs for hours.

title: Step inside the Edicule over Christ's tomb
description: A 2016 restoration lifted the marble slab for the first time in centuries and confirmed a limestone burial bed underneath. Only four people at a time fit inside the shrine, for under a minute each.

title: Leave a written prayer in the Western Wall
description: The last retaining wall of the Second Temple's courtyard, divided into separate men's and women's prayer sections. Notes wedged into the stone are cleared out twice a year and buried on the Mount of Olives.

title: Follow the Western Wall Tunnels beneath the Old City
description: A guided-only route along the wall's full length underground, past a Herodian street and a single foundation stone estimated at 570 tonnes. Tours fill up days ahead during pilgrimage season.

title: Photograph the Dome of the Rock from the esplanade
description: The Noble Sanctuary is open to all visitors outside prayer times, but only Muslims may enter the Dome and Al-Aqsa Mosque themselves. Visiting hours are mornings only and shift again for Ramadan.

title: Walk the fourteen Stations of the Cross on the Via Dolorosa
description: The route runs straight through the working souks of the Muslim and Christian Quarters, so the stations sit between spice stalls and pilgrim shops rather than in isolation. Franciscans process the full route every Friday afternoon.

title: Sit in the quiet of the Garden Tomb
description: A rock-cut tomb outside the Old City walls that some Protestant traditions hold as the true burial site rather than the Holy Sepulchre. Free to enter, and closed Sundays for services.

title: Look over the Old City from the Mount of Olives
description: The classic view takes in the Dome of the Rock across the Kidron Valley, above one of the world's oldest Jewish cemeteries, still in active use. Walk down through the Garden of Gethsemane instead of back the way you came.

title: Bar-hop through Mahane Yehuda Market after dark
description: A produce market by day, and by Thursday night a strip of stalls turned into bars once the fruit crates are cleared. It shuts hard before Friday's Shabbat, then stays quiet until Saturday evening.

title: Wander the stone lanes of Ein Karem
description: Traditionally the birthplace of John the Baptist, now a leafy artists' village folded into Jerusalem's western suburbs. Most day-trippers never make it out here, so the churches and courtyard cafes stay unhurried.

title: Float in the Dead Sea and read a book doing it
description: Buoyant enough to read a paperback while floating, though the water stings any nick or shaving cut and must never reach your eyes. Free public beaches sit alongside the paid resort strip near Ein Bokek.

title: Hike to the waterfalls at Ein Gedi oasis
description: A freshwater oasis dropping through the Judean Desert to the Dead Sea shore, where ibex and hyrax often turn out closer than the crowds. David hid from Saul in these caves, according to the Book of Samuel.

title: Snorkel the coral reef at Eilat
description: Israel's only stretch of Red Sea coast, with reef close enough to reach by wading in at the Coral Beach nature reserve. The underwater observatory nearby is worth it on a windy day when visibility drops.

title: Camp under the stars at Ramon Crater
description: The world's largest makhtesh, an erosion crater rather than an impact one, and Israel's first International Dark Sky Park. Mitzpe Ramon on the rim has telescopes for hire after sunset.

title: Walk the ruins of Capernaum on the Sea of Galilee
description: Jesus's base for his Galilee ministry per the Gospels, where a white limestone synagogue was built directly over an older black basalt one, beside a house shrine marking Peter's traditional home.

title: Visit the Basilica of the Annunciation in Nazareth
description: The largest Christian church in the Middle East, built over the grotto tradition holds as Mary's childhood home. Its courtyard walls carry mosaics of Mary donated by nations worldwide, each rendered in a distinct national style.

title: Taste wine on the Golan Heights
description: Volcanic soil and elevation built an internationally awarded wine industry on a plateau that is still legally disputed and dotted with old minefields fenced off between the vineyard rows.

title: Ride the cable car down to the Rosh Hanikra grottoes
description: Chalk cliffs on the Lebanese border carved by the sea into a network of grottoes, reached by Israel's steepest cable car. A sealed rail tunnel here once carried the Cairo-to-Istanbul line.

title: Browse the artist quarter of Tzfat
description: One of Judaism's four holy cities and the birthplace of Kabbalah, its blue-painted alleys now doubling as a working artist colony. Galleries close from Friday afternoon for Shabbat.

title: Cross the waterfall trail at Banias Nature Reserve
description: A Roman-era shrine to the god Pan sits at the spring that feeds the Jordan River, upstream of a waterfall trail most Galilee itineraries skip in favour of the Dead Sea.

title: Explore the Crusader tunnels beneath Akko's Old City
description: A UNESCO port city built in layers, its Knights Hospitaller halls sitting directly beneath today's street grid. The hummus at the market stalls by the sea wall rivals anything in Tel Aviv.

title: Walk the terraces of the Bahai Gardens in Haifa
description: Nineteen manicured terraces climb Mount Carmel to the golden-domed Shrine of the Bab, Haifa's most photographed view. Free guided tours run once daily and must be booked ahead; otherwise only the top and bottom gates are open.

title: Get lost in the alleys of Old Jaffa
description: A working port older than Tel Aviv itself, its stone lanes hiding artist studios and a flea market that only gets going after 10am. The clock tower square is the best sunset spot over the Mediterranean.

title: See the silver star marking Christ's birthplace in Bethlehem
description: The oldest continuously used church in the Holy Land, entered through a low stone Door of Humility built to stop looters riding horses inside. Christmas week books the grotto below months in advance.

title: Visit the shared shrine over the Cave of the Patriarchs in Hebron
description: Revered as the burial place of Abraham by Jews and Muslims alike, split since 1994 into separate mosque and synagogue sections under tight Israeli military control. Bring your passport; checkpoints here are routine.

title: Eat kanafeh where it was invented, in Nablus's old souk
description: A cheese pastry soaked in syrup and topped with orange semolina, sold hot from copper trays in a soap-making city that has traded in olive oil for a thousand years.

title: Sit in a Ramallah cafe where Palestinian politics gets argued
description: The de facto administrative capital, more liberal and nightlife-driven than anywhere else in the West Bank, with Yasser Arafat's mausoleum and museum inside the government compound.

title: Hike Wadi Qelt past St George's Monastery
description: A dry canyon trail between Jerusalem and Jericho with a Greek Orthodox monastery built straight into the cliff face partway along, still reached only on foot or by donkey.

title: Look down on Mar Saba monastery from the Kidron Valley rim
description: A fifth-century monastery stacked into a cliff face, home to a small community of monks who still bar women from entering; everyone else views it only from the opposite ridge unless invited in.

title: Walk the Roman-era irrigation terraces of Battir
description: A UNESCO-listed village growing eggplant on 2,000-year-old stone terraces watered by an ancient shared-turn system still run by the same families. It is a short walk from a station on the Jerusalem-Tel Aviv rail line.

title: Tour Taybeh, the West Bank's only microbrewery
description: A Christian village that has kept brewing since 1994 despite import taxes on hops and barley that would sink most breweries, and holds an Oktoberfest that draws visitors from across the West Bank.

title: See the mosaic floor at Hisham's Palace near Jericho
description: An unfinished 8th-century Umayyad winter retreat, flattened by an earthquake before it was ever used, its bathhouse floor holding one of the largest mosaics in the world under a modern canopy.

title: Climb the volcano-shaped fortress of Herodion
description: Herod the Great built this cone-shaped palace-fortress from scratch, then was buried inside it in a tomb only rediscovered in 2007. The hill is visible across the hills from Jerusalem itself.

title: Watch the Treasury lit by candles on Petra by Night
description: Twelve hundred paper candles line the Siq three evenings a week for a Bedouin music performance in front of the Treasury. It runs rain or shine and is a separate ticket from daytime entry.

title: Stand where Jesus was baptised at Bethany Beyond the Jordan
description: A UNESCO site on the Jordan River identified by archaeology and early pilgrim accounts as the location of Christ's baptism. The river is now a narrow, muddy channel, with Israel visible a few metres across it.

title: Scramble through the slot canyon at Little Petra
description: A smaller Nabataean satellite site with carved facades and painted ceilings, free to enter and usually empty by mid-morning once the big Petra crowds have moved on. A back trail connects it to Petra for a full day's walk.

title: Watch the sunset over Amman from the Citadel
description: Jebel al-Qal'a has been fortified since the Bronze Age, and its Roman Temple of Hercules columns look out over the Roman Theatre and the whole downtown grid below. Go an hour before sunset for the light on the hills.

title: Explore the Crusader passages of Karak Castle
description: A Crusader stronghold later held by Saladin, built from black basalt with vaulted galleries long enough to march a garrison through unseen. The small museum in the entrance hall is easy to miss but worth the five minutes.

title: Climb Ajloun Castle above the forested hills
description: Built in 1184 to watch for Crusader movement and guard the iron mines below, it is one of the few castles in Jordan built by Muslim forces rather than captured from them. The surrounding hills are Jordan's greenest after spring rain.

title: Look over the Promised Land from Mount Nebo
description: Tradition holds this is where Moses viewed Canaan before he died, and on a clear winter day you can see Jericho, the Dead Sea and the hills around Jerusalem. A mosaic-floored Byzantine church sits at the summit.

title: See the oldest map of the Holy Land in Madaba
description: A 6th-century Byzantine mosaic floor in St George's Church maps the entire Holy Land, Jerusalem included, and is missing whole sections only where later pews were bolted straight through it.

title: Wade the Siq Trail through Wadi Mujib canyon
description: Jordan's answer to a canyoning trip, wading and swimming upstream between sheer walls to a waterfall, with ropes fixed at the harder sections. The reserve closes the trail without notice after heavy rain upstream.

title: Look across three countries from the ruins of Umm Qais
description: Ancient Gadara's black-basalt Roman theatre looks out over the Sea of Galilee, the Golan Heights and the Yarmouk Valley at once. A restored Ottoman village built from the same stones doubles as the site's cafe.

title: Soak under the hot-spring waterfalls of Hammamat Ma'in
description: Mineral water at up to 60C pours straight off a cliff into pools below sea level, a short drive from the Dead Sea's more crowded beaches. Go on a weekday morning before the tour buses from Amman arrive.

title: Find the inscriptions at lonely Shobak Castle
description: Built by the Crusaders in 1115 and rarely visited compared to Karak, with Crusader and Arabic inscriptions still cut into the stone of a spiral staircase down to a hidden well.

title: Watch sunset at the Pigeon Rocks on Beirut's Corniche
description: Two limestone sea stacks just off the Raouche cliffs, best seen from the Corniche promenade where fishermen and joggers share the same stretch of rail. Boats will take you under the arch for a few dollars.

title: See the war-hidden mosaics at the National Museum of Beirut
description: Staff encased the largest artefacts in concrete to protect them through the civil war, and photos of that concrete now hang beside the uncovered originals. The Phoenician sarcophagus collection is the best reason to come.

title: Stand among the last old-growth trees at the Cedars of God
description: A UNESCO grove of a few hundred ancient cedars, some estimated at over a thousand years old, all that is left of forests that once supplied timber to Phoenician ships and Solomon's Temple alike.

title: Hike past cliffside monasteries in the Qadisha Valley
description: A UNESCO gorge where Maronite monks carved hermitages and monasteries directly into the cliff faces from as early as the 4th century, some still inhabited. Gibran Khalil Gibran is buried at a museum on the valley's rim.

title: Walk the Roman hippodrome at Tyre
description: A UNESCO site with one of the best-preserved Roman hippodromes anywhere, once used for chariot races, plus a triumphal arch and necropolis lining the old road into the city.

title: Walk the sea-bound corridors of Sidon's Sea Castle
description: A 13th-century Crusader fortress built on an offshore islet and linked to the mainland by a narrow causeway, in a working fishing city better known locally for its soap khan and covered souks.

title: Tour the 19th-century emir's palace at Beiteddine
description: An Ottoman-era emir's palace with Damascene-style courtyards and mosaic floors lifted from a Byzantine site, still used for a summer arts festival staged in the same courtyards it was built to impress in.

title: Walk the only Umayyad city ruins in Lebanon at Anjar
description: An 8th-century caliph's city laid out on a Roman-style grid and abandoned within decades, unlike anything else surviving from the period in Lebanon. It sits near the Syrian border in a mostly Armenian farming town.

title: Step into the Blue Mosque between prayer times
description: Six minarets caused controversy when it was built, since that matched Mecca's Masjid al-Haram at the time. It closes to visitors five times a day for prayer, so check the schedule posted at the tourist entrance.

title: See the Ottoman treasury inside Topkapi Palace
description: Four courtyards deep into the sultans' seat of power, ending in a treasury holding an 86-carat diamond and the Topkapi Dagger. The Harem section is a separate ticket and worth the extra line.

title: Walk among the columns of the Basilica Cistern
description: A 6th-century underground reservoir holding 336 columns, two resting on giant carved Medusa heads turned sideways and upside down for reasons nobody has confirmed.

title: Cruise the Bosphorus between two continents
description: Public ferries cost a fraction of a tourist boat and cover the same waterfront of Ottoman palaces and fortress walls. Sit on the right side heading north for the better light in the afternoon.

title: Get scrubbed at a 300-year-old Turkish bath
description: Built in 1741 and still working on marble slabs heated from below, with a full wash and scrub delivered by staff rather than done yourself. Bring nothing; towels and sandals are provided.

title: See the Byzantine mosaics of Chora Church
description: Some of the best-preserved Byzantine mosaics and frescoes anywhere, plastered over rather than destroyed when the building became a mosque, which is why they survived at all.

title: Photograph the coloured houses of Balat
description: A former Jewish and Greek quarter along the Golden Horn, its houses now painted in the colours that have made it a filming location, still a working neighbourhood rather than a museum piece.

title: Sleep in a cave hotel carved into the rock in Cappadocia
description: Volcanic tuff carves easily and insulates well, so rooms hollowed straight into the rock stay cool by day and warm at night. Book a room with a terrace for the sunrise balloon show without leaving bed.

title: Duck into rock-cut chapels at Goreme Open Air Museum
description: A cluster of Byzantine monasteries and churches carved into fairy chimneys, several still holding faded frescoes from the 10th and 11th centuries. The Dark Church costs extra and is worth it for the preserved colour.

title: Hike the canyon floor of Ihlara Valley
description: A 100m-deep gorge cut by a river through volcanic rock, its cliff walls hiding over a hundred rock-cut churches. It gets a fraction of Goreme's crowds despite being just as dramatic.

title: Climb to the steepest theatre in the ancient world at Pergamon
description: A hilltop acropolis above modern Bergama, its Hellenistic theatre raked so steeply that 10,000 people fit into a space most cities would need twice the land for.

title: Walk the excavated layers of ancient Troy
