description: A 20m-wide curtain with a dry ledge behind it, five minutes upstream from the rockslide on the same road.

title: Drink Chardonnay where the grapes ripen first
description: The country's Chardonnay capital and the first major wine region to be harvested each year, on fertile Poverty Bay flats.

title: Walk the art deco streets of Napier
description: Flattened by an earthquake in 1931 and rebuilt in two years, entirely in the style of the moment - one of the most complete art deco towns anywhere.

title: Visit the gannet colony at Cape Kidnappers
description: The largest mainland gannet colony on earth, on a cliff at the end of an 8km beach walk that is only passable at low tide.

title: Watch the sun go down from Te Mata Peak
description: 399m of limestone ridge you can drive or walk up, looking across the Heretaunga Plains to Ruapehu on a clear day.

title: Cycle the Hawke's Bay wine trails
description: New Zealand's oldest wine region and its best for Syrah and Bordeaux blends, linked by 200km of flat off-road cycle trail.

title: Photograph Mount Taranaki reflected in the Pouakai Tarns
description: The reflection shot everyone wants, and it needs a windless morning after a wet night. The tarn is small and the walk in is long and steep.

title: Walk the Pouakai Crossing
description: 19km across the flanks of the volcano through goblin forest, swamp and alpine tops. Quieter than Tongariro and arguably more varied.

title: Walk to Dawson Falls on Mount Taranaki
description: An 18m fall over an old lava flow, ten minutes from the road, on the mountain's south side where the forest is thickest.

title: Cycle the New Plymouth Coastal Walkway to the Wind Wand
description: 13km of seafront path past Len Lye's 45m kinetic Wind Wand and the Te Rewa Rewa bridge, which frames the mountain exactly.

title: See the kinetic sculpture at the Len Lye Centre
description: A mirrored stainless steel building holding the work of a New Zealander who spent his life making sculpture that moves, and film scratched by hand.

title: Drive Surf Highway 45 around the mountain
description: 105km of coast road with a break at almost every river mouth, and the volcano over your shoulder the entire way.

title: Walk the Tongariro Alpine Crossing
description: 19.4km past the Emerald Lakes and Red Crater, often called the best day walk in the country. Shuttle booking is compulsory, and the weather turns fast.

title: Ski Whakapapa on an active volcano
description: The North Island's largest ski area, on the slopes of Ruapehu, which last erupted in 2007 and has a crater lake at the top.

title: Ride the Old Coach Road between the viaducts
description: A cobbled 1906 coach road relaid as a cycle trail, passing the Hapuawhenua viaduct - the last surviving curved timber-era viaduct in the country.

title: Canoe the Whanganui Journey to the Bridge to Nowhere
description: Five days down a river that holds legal personhood in its own right, to a 1936 concrete bridge in the bush leading nowhere at either end.

title: Ride the Durie Hill elevator through the hillside
description: You walk 200m into a tunnel, then ride a 1919 public elevator 66m up inside the hill - the only one of its kind in the country.

title: Walk the Te Apiti Manawatu Gorge track
description: A river gorge cutting straight through the ranges, with the Te Ahu a Turanga sculpture above it and a wind farm along the ridge.

title: See the colossal squid at Te Papa
description: Free entry to the national museum, holding the only intact colossal squid on display anywhere and the Gallipoli figures Weta made at 2.4 times life size.

title: Hear kaka and kiwi at Zealandia
description: 225 hectares behind a predator-proof fence, ten minutes from parliament, on a 500-year plan to return the valley to how it was before people arrived.

title: Ride the cable car up to the Botanic Garden
description: Running since 1902 from Lambton Quay to Kelburn, with the best view of the harbour at the top and a walk back down through the gardens.

title: Take the Weta Workshop tour
description: Where the props, armour and creatures for Lord of the Rings were actually made - in an unremarkable suburban shed in Miramar.

title: Walk out to the Red Rocks seal colony
description: A rough coast track from Owhiro Bay to red-stained volcanic rock where male fur seals haul out over winter. Keep 20m back.

title: Climb Mount Victoria for the harbour view
description: 196m above the city with the whole harbour laid out, and the town belt below it doubling as the forest the hobbits hid in from the Black Rider.

title: Drink your way along Cuba Street
description: Wellington roasts and drinks more coffee per head than anywhere else in the country, and this street is where it concentrates.

title: Spend a day on predator-free Kapiti Island
description: A nature reserve cleared of rats since 1998, where takahe walk past you on the track. Numbers are capped daily and permits book out.

title: Take the ferry to Matiu Somes Island
description: A quarantine station, then an internment camp in both wars, now a predator-free reserve with tuatara - twenty minutes out into the harbour.

title: Taste Pinot Noir in Martinborough
description: A village laid out as a Union Jack, ringed by small Pinot producers close enough together to visit on a bicycle in an afternoon.

title: Walk up to the Putangirua Pinnacles
description: Earth pillars left by 120,000 years of erosion, used as the Paths of the Dead. The streambed route is the good one - go when it is dry.

title: Climb the 1,000 steps at Castlepoint
description: A lighthouse on a reef, a lagoon behind it and Castle Rock rising 162m above - and a horse race run on the beach every March.

title: Kayak the Abel Tasman coast to Anchorage
description: The smallest national park and the sunniest - golden granite beaches, tidal crossings and a water taxi that lets you walk one way and paddle the other.

title: Cross the Awaroa tidal inlet on foot
description: Passable for about two hours either side of low tide, and impossible otherwise. The beach was bought for the nation by public crowdfunding in 2016.

title: Look into Te Waikoropupu Springs
description: Among the clearest fresh water ever measured, with 63m visibility. The springs are tapu - you look, you do not touch the water.

title: Walk through the Wharariki Beach arches
description: Twenty minutes over farmland and dunes to Archway Islands and seal pups playing in the rock pools. Wind and spray are part of the deal.

title: Walk out along Farewell Spit
description: A 26km sand hook and internationally recognised bird sanctuary - most of it is closed, so the far end is reachable only by licensed tour.

title: Photograph the jetty on Lake Rotoiti
description: Beech forest to the waterline and mountains behind - and eels and trout so used to people they gather under the jetty planks.

title: Climb to Angelus Hut on the Robert Ridge
description: Twelve kilometres along an exposed alpine ridge to a hut beside a tarn in a rock basin. Fully exposed to weather the whole way.

title: Stand at the geographic centre of New Zealand
description: A short steep walk above Nelson to the zero point of the 1870s survey. Not actually the country's centre, but the marker is real enough.

title: See the winning entries at the WOW museum
description: Garments built from wood, bone, wire and rubbish for a competition that started in a Nelson shed in 1987 and now fills a stadium in Wellington.

title: Walk a section of the Queen Charlotte Track
description: 70km of ridge above drowned river valleys, with boats moving your pack between lodges so you walk with nothing on your back.

title: Ride the mail boat through the Pelorus Sound
description: A working delivery run to households with no road access - you ride along while the skipper drops off post, groceries and the occasional sheep.

title: Taste Sauvignon Blanc where the style was invented
description: The first vines went in in 1973 and within twenty years Marlborough Sauvignon had rewritten what the grape could taste like. Flat enough to cycle.

title: See the aircraft collection at Omaka
description: Peter Jackson's WWI aircraft collection, staged by Weta as full crash scenes with mannequins rather than parked in rows.

title: Watch sperm whales surface off Kaikoura
description: A canyon a kilometre deep sits close to shore, so sperm whales feed here year-round - one of the few places on earth you can count on them.

title: Swim with dusky dolphins at Kaikoura
description: Pods of several hundred duskies, and the rule is that you have to entertain them - sing through your snorkel and they will circle you.

title: Eat crayfish off the roadside at Nins Bin
description: A caravan on the coast road selling crayfish pulled from pots you can see from the counter. Kaikoura literally means to eat crayfish.

title: Punt the Avon through the Botanic Gardens
description: A city still visibly rebuilding after 2011, with a punt service on the river running exactly as it did before.

title: Sit in the Cardboard Cathedral
description: A transitional cathedral built from 98 cardboard tubes after the earthquake destroyed the original - designed by Shigeru Ban and meant to last 50 years.

title: Look for Hector's dolphins in Akaroa Harbour
description: A drowned volcanic crater settled by the French in 1840, and home to Hector's dolphin - the smallest marine dolphin, found only in New Zealand.

title: Drive the Summit Road around the crater rim
description: A narrow road along the rim of two extinct volcanoes, looking down into bays on both sides. Mostly unsealed and best not attempted in fog.

title: Walk to the Devils Punchbowl waterfall
description: A 131m fall an hour's walk from the village, in a pass where kea will strip the rubber from your car if you leave it long enough.

title: Ride the TranzAlpine across the Southern Alps
description: Christchurch to Greymouth in about five hours, through 16 tunnels and over five viaducts, with an open-air carriage for the good bits.

title: Scramble the limestone boulders at Castle Hill
description: A field of weathered limestone tors rated among the best bouldering areas anywhere, and named by the Dalai Lama a spiritual centre of the universe.

title: Walk the Hooker Valley Track to Aoraki
description: Three swing bridges and 10km return to a glacial lake with icebergs in it, under the highest mountain in the country. Flat, and the best value walk in New Zealand.

title: Stargaze in the Aoraki Mackenzie Dark Sky Reserve
description: 4,300 square kilometres of protected night sky - one of the largest reserves of its kind, with the Mount John observatory running tours.

title: See Lake Tekapo turn milk blue
description: Glacial flour suspended in the water gives the colour, and the lupins along the shore in November are gorgeous and entirely invasive.

title: Fly onto the Tasman Glacier
description: The longest glacier in the country at 23km, landed on by ski-plane. Its terminal lake did not exist in 1970 and now grows every year.

title: Soak in the thermal pools at Hanmer Springs
description: Sulphur springs found in 1859, now a set of pools at different temperatures in an alpine village surrounded by forestry.

title: Watch the blowholes at Punakaiki Pancake Rocks
description: Limestone stacked in layers by a process still not fully explained, with blowholes that only really perform on a high tide and a westerly swell.

title: Find the Oparara Arches in the Kahurangi forest
description: A 200m limestone arch 43m high over a tannin-stained river, at the end of a rough logging road most visitors never turn down.

title: Ride the Old Ghost Road end to end
description: 85km following a gold miners' road that was surveyed in the 1870s and never finished, completed as a trail 130 years later.

title: See the Denniston Incline
description: Loaded coal wagons were lowered 518m down a 1-in-1.3 gradient by gravity, hauling empties back up. Families lived at the top for decades without a road.

title: Take a heli-hike onto Franz Josef Glacier
description: The glacier has retreated so far that walking onto the ice from the valley ended in 2012 - helicopter access is now the only way onto it.

title: Walk the Fox Glacier valley to the viewpoint
description: The valley track has been repeatedly closed by rockfall and flooding - check DOC's current status, because the road end moves.

title: Catch the reflection at Lake Matheson
description: Aoraki and Tasman mirrored in dark peat-stained water. It needs a still dawn, and the walk around takes about ninety minutes.

title: See the water colour at Hokitika Gorge
description: Rock flour turns the river an almost luminous turquoise between granite walls, crossed by two swing bridges.

title: Watch the sunset at Ship Creek
description: Driftwood piled by the Tasman on a wild beach, with a swamp forest boardwalk behind and almost nobody stopping.

title: Bungy off the Kawarau Bridge
description: The world's first commercial bungy, opened in 1988, 43m into a gorge with the option of touching the water.

title: Climb Ben Lomond above Queenstown
description: 1,748m and about six hours return from town, with the whole Wakatipu basin below and the Remarkables opposite.

title: Ride the TSS Earnslaw across Lake Wakatipu
description: A coal-fired steamship launched in 1912, the same year as the Titanic, still working the lake daily. You can watch the stokers feeding it.

title: Eat a Fergburger at 2am
description: A burger shop with a permanent queue and no marketing budget, open until 5am. It has become the closest thing Queenstown has to a landmark.

title: Jet boat the Shotover canyons
description: Hamilton jets running at 85km/h through canyons narrow enough to touch, with 360-degree spins. A New Zealand invention, used as designed.

title: Walk to the Routeburn Falls hut
description: 32km over the Harris Saddle between two national parks. One of the ten Great Walks, and huts book out the day bookings open.

title: Ride the Skippers Canyon road
description: A gold miners' road cut into a cliff by hand in the 1880s, single lane with no barrier. Almost every rental agreement in the country forbids it.

title: Climb Roys Peak for the ridge photo
description: 1,228m of relentless zigzag up farmland with no shade, to a viewpoint with a queue on it. Closed for lambing from October to mid November.

title: Photograph That Wanaka Tree
description: A crack willow growing out of the lake, originally a fence post that took root. Probably the most photographed tree in the country.

title: Walk to the Rob Roy Glacier
description: Ten kilometres return into a hanging valley where ice calves off the face while you eat lunch. The access road has several fords.

title: Get lost in Puzzling World
description: A three-dimensional maze with 1.5km of passage, a leaning tower and a room where water appears to run uphill. Genuinely good, not just for children.

title: Cycle the Otago Central Rail Trail
description: 152km of old railway through schist country, viaducts and tunnels, at a gradient never steeper than 1 in 50. The trail that started the country's cycle network.

title: Taste Pinot Noir in Bannockburn
description: The southernmost wine region on earth, on gold-sluiced hillsides - continental extremes give the Pinot its structure.

title: Walk up Baldwin Street, the steepest in the world
description: A 1-in-2.86 gradient at its steepest, reclaimed from a Welsh challenger in 2020. Concrete, because asphalt would run downhill in summer.

title: See the albatross colony at Taiaroa Head
description: The only mainland breeding colony of royal albatross anywhere - birds with a three-metre wingspan landing a few metres from the observatory glass.

title: Ride the Taieri Gorge Railway
description: Out of Dunedin's Flemish Renaissance railway station into a gorge crossed by wrought iron viaducts, on a line finished in 1889.

title: Watch yellow-eyed penguins come ashore on the Otago Peninsula
description: Hoiho are among the rarest penguins on earth and will not land if they can see you - which is why the hides here are dug into the hillside.

title: Find the Moeraki Boulders at low tide
description: Septarian concretions that formed on the sea floor 60 million years ago and are now weathering out of the cliff onto the beach.

title: See the Maori rock art at Duntroon
description: Charcoal and ochre drawings under limestone overhangs in the Waitaki valley, some pre-dating European contact by centuries.

title: Cruise Milford Sound to the Tasman Sea
description: Mitre Peak rising 1,692m straight out of the water. It rains about 200 days a year here, and the waterfalls are better when it does.

title: Stay overnight on Doubtful Sound
description: Three times longer and ten times larger than Milford, reached by boat then bus over Wilmot Pass. The skipper cuts the engines for the silence.

title: Drive the Milford Road through the Homer Tunnel
description: 120km past the Mirror Lakes and Monkey Creek into a 1.2km hand-dug tunnel that drops steeply into the Cleddau valley. Avalanche closures are common.

title: Walk the Milford Track
description: 53.5km over Mackinnon Pass past Sutherland Falls, once billed as the finest walk in the world. One direction only, 40 walkers a day, booked out in minutes.

title: Walk the Kepler Track from Te Anau
description: A 60km loop that starts and finishes in town - unusual for a Great Walk - with a long exposed ridge above the bushline in the middle.

title: See the glowworms in the Te Anau caves
description: A living cave system still being carved by an underground river - you go by boat across the lake, then punt through the dark.

title: Look for kiwi in the wild on Rakiura
description: Stewart Island holds around 20,000 tokoeka, which forage in daylight here - the best chance anywhere of seeing a kiwi that nobody put there.

title: Watch the aurora australis from Rakiura
description: Rakiura means glowing skies. At 47 degrees south with a Dark Sky Sanctuary designation, this is the most reliable aurora viewing in the country.

title: Watch sea lions at Nugget Point
description: An 1869 lighthouse on a knife-edge headland above rock stacks, with fur seals, sea lions and elephant seals all hauling out below.

title: Reach Purakaunui Falls in the Catlins
description: A three-tiered 20m fall through podocarp forest, ten minutes from the road, and probably the most photographed waterfall in the south.

title: Stand on the petrified forest at Curio Bay
description: A 180-million-year-old Jurassic forest fossilised in the rock platform, exposed at low tide, with hoiho coming ashore in the next bay.

title: Reach Slope Point, the southernmost tip
description: The southernmost point of the South Island, marked by a signpost and a stand of macrocarpa trees permanently bent sideways by the wind.

title: See Burt Munro's Indian at Invercargill
description: The actual 1920 Indian Scout from The World's Fastest Indian, still held in a hardware shop in town alongside a serious motorcycle collection.

title: Eat Bluff oysters in season
description: Dredged wild from Foveaux Strait for a short season each year, and treated in New Zealand with a seriousness usually reserved for sport.

title: Island-hop the Yasawa chain by boat
description: A 20-island volcanic chain served by one daily catamaran, so you can step off wherever you like and pick it up again days later.

title: Snorkel the reef off a Mamanuca sandbar
description: The islands closest to Nadi, including the sandbar Cloud 9 and the beach used for Cast Away - easy reef access straight off the sand.

title: Slide the natural waterslides at Bouma, Taveuni
description: The Garden Island - three tiers of waterfall in Bouma National Heritage Park, and the Waitavala natural rock slide locals use as a chute.

title: Dive with bull sharks in Beqa Lagoon
description: A shark reserve where up to eight species turn up on one dive, funded by a levy paid to the local villages that gave up fishing rights.

title: Sit in the Sabeto mud pools near Nadi
description: Geothermal mud pools at the foot of the Sleeping Giant, where you coat yourself, dry off in the sun and rinse in a hot spring.

title: Swim the lagoon at Bora Bora
description: A drowned volcano ringed by a barrier reef and motu - the lagoon runs through half a dozen distinct shades of blue in one afternoon.

title: Climb to the Belvedere lookout on Moorea
description: A lookout between Cook's and Opunohu bays, up through pineapple fields, with Mount Rotui splitting the view in two.

title: Watch the surf at Teahupo'o
description: One of the heaviest waves on earth, breaking over shallow reef at the end of the road on Tahiti Iti. Watching is the sensible option.

title: Drift the Tiputa Pass at Rangiroa
description: The second largest atoll in the world - the incoming tide sweeps you through a pass alongside dolphins, grey reef sharks and manta rays.

title: See the wall of sharks at Fakarava
description: A UNESCO biosphere atoll whose south pass holds hundreds of grey reef sharks stacked against the current - among the densest gatherings anywhere.

title: Stand on the rim of Mount Yasur
description: One of the most accessible active volcanoes on earth - you drive most of the way up and watch lava thrown out of the crater after dark.

title: Dive the SS President Coolidge
description: A 200m troopship sunk by friendly mines in 1942, lying in 20-70m of water and reachable from the beach - one of the great shore-accessible wrecks.

title: Swim the blue holes of Espiritu Santo
description: Freshwater springs filtered through limestone to an almost artificial blue, with rope swings over the deepest ones. Nanda and Riri are the best known.

title: Spend a day at Champagne Beach
description: Named for the volcanic gas that bubbles up through the sand at low tide, on a bay of white sand that is quiet unless a cruise ship is in.

title: Swim the natural pool at the Isle of Pines
description: Kanak country, ringed by columnar pines Cook mistook for basalt - the Piscine Naturelle is a reef-enclosed pool you can wade into.

title: Fly over the Heart of Voh
description: A heart-shaped clearing in the mangroves, formed entirely naturally, made famous by Yann Arthus-Bertrand. Only visible from the air.

title: Snorkel the New Caledonia Barrier Reef
description: The second longest double barrier reef in the world, enclosing one of the largest lagoons - World Heritage listed and remarkably intact.

title: Climb down the ladder into To Sua Ocean Trench
description: A 30m swimming hole in a lava field, joined to the sea by a tunnel, reached by a near-vertical wooden ladder. The name means giant swimming hole.

title: Stay in a beach fale at Lalomanu
description: Open-sided thatched huts on the sand, run by the village, with meals included - the cheapest and best way to sleep in Samoa.

title: Watch the Alofaaga blowholes fire
description: Lava tubes on the Savai'i coast that fire seawater tens of metres up. Locals throw coconuts in to show the force - tip them, it is worth it.

title: Swim with humpback whales in Vava'u
description: Tonga is one of very few countries licensing in-water swims with humpbacks, which come here to calve. Strictly regulated and worth every cent.

title: Walk the Mapu'a 'a Vaea blowholes
description: Five kilometres of coastal terrace riddled with blowholes that fire together on a big swell - the name means chief's whistles.

title: Have a Ha'apai island to yourself
description: 62 islands, most uninhabited, with almost no tourism infrastructure - the quietest corner of an already quiet country.

title: Cross the Aitutaki lagoon to One Foot Island
description: A triangular lagoon widely rated the most beautiful anywhere, with a motu whose one-room post office will stamp your passport.

title: Walk the cross-island track past the Needle
description: Straight over the middle of the island past Te Rua Manga, a volcanic plug locals call the Needle. Steep, muddy and about four hours.

title: Snorkel the Muri lagoon
description: A shallow lagoon protected by four motu, warm enough to stay in all day, with a Saturday night market on the beach behind it.

title: Paddle the Marovo Lagoon
description: The largest saltwater lagoon on earth, enclosed by a double barrier reef, with villages that still carve to order in kerosene wood.

title: Dive the wrecks of Iron Bottom Sound
description: More than fifty ships and hundreds of aircraft sank here during the Guadalcanal campaign. Several sit shallow enough to dive on recreational limits.

title: Visit the skull shrines of Skull Island
description: A tiny island in Vonavona Lagoon holding the skulls of Roviana chiefs and their headhunting trophies. Go with a local guide and ask before photographing.

title: Walk the Kokoda Track
description: 96km over the Owen Stanley Range, eight to ten days, following the 1942 campaign. Guided trekking only, and considerably harder than most expect.

title: Kayak the drowned fjords at Tufi
description: Volcanic rias - the only tropical fjords in the world - with village stays on the ridges above and reef diving at the mouths.

title: Travel the Sepik River by canoe
description: 1,100km through haus tambaran spirit houses and some of the most distinctive carving traditions anywhere. Slow, hot, and genuinely remote.

title: Climb Mount Wilhelm
description: At 4,509m the highest point in Papua New Guinea, usually climbed overnight to reach the summit at dawn before the cloud closes in.

title: Float among the stingless jellyfish of Jellyfish Lake
description: A marine lake holding millions of golden jellyfish that lost their sting in isolation. The population has crashed and recovered before - check it is open.

title: Kayak the Rock Islands of Palau
description: 445 undercut limestone islands in a turquoise lagoon, World Heritage listed. Palau requires every visitor to sign an eco-pledge on arrival.

title: Hook onto the current at Blue Corner
description: Routinely voted the best dive site in the world - you clip a reef hook into dead coral and hang in the current while sharks stream past.

title: Swim the chasms at Limu Pools
description: Niue is one raised coral atoll with no rivers, so the sea is startlingly clear - Limu is a set of pools where fresh water seeps in through the rock.

title: Swim with humpbacks off Niue
description: One of the few places permitting in-water encounters, and the whales come within metres of the shoreline drop-off. Population about 1,700 people.

title: Walk the convict ruins at Kingston
description: Part of the same World Heritage convict listing as Port Arthur, and the site of the harshest penal settlement in the system.

title: Take the boat to Phillip Island off Norfolk
description: Stripped bare by introduced rabbits and now slowly revegetating - red and ochre soil, seabird colonies, and a steep scramble to the top.

title: Dive the ghost fleet of Chuuk Lagoon
description: More than 50 Japanese ships and 250 aircraft sunk in two days in 1944, now the largest concentration of wrecks on the seabed anywhere.

title: Explore the basalt city of Nan Madol
description: Around 100 artificial islets built from basalt logs on a reef flat, abandoned by 1800 - a World Heritage site being reclaimed by mangroves.

title: Dive the fleet sunk at Bikini Atoll
description: Warships including the carrier Saratoga, sunk by nuclear tests in 1946. The islanders were removed and have never been able to return permanently.

title: Cycle the length of Majuro atoll
description: A 50km ribbon of land rarely more than a few hundred metres wide, with lagoon on one side and ocean on the other the entire way.

title: Fly-fish the flats of Kiritimati
description: Christmas Island - the largest coral atoll by land area on earth, and among the best bonefish flats anywhere. Also the first place on the planet to see each new year.

title: Reach the Phoenix Islands Protected Area
description: One of the largest and most remote marine protected areas on earth, reachable only by expedition vessel and visited by almost nobody.

title: Snorkel the Funafuti Conservation Area
description: One of the least visited countries on earth - a few thousand tourists a year - and among the most exposed to sea level rise.

title: Walk Command Ridge on Nauru
description: The highest point on the island, with Japanese WWII guns and a view over the phosphate pinnacles left by a century of strip mining.

title: Swim through the caves at Sawa-i-Lau
description: The second chamber is only reached by ducking through a short submerged passage with a local guide - the crew for The Blue Lagoon lit it with nothing but the natural skylight above.

title: Share a kava bowl in a Fijian village ceremony
description: Clap once before you drink, empty the coconut shell in one go, then clap three times after - Navala's thatched bure village in the highlands still runs the sevusevu properly rather than as a show for cruise groups.

title: Watch the Sawau tribe walk on white-hot stones
description: A hereditary gift said to come from a spirit god centuries ago, performed barefoot across stones heated for hours in a pit - only Sawau men from this one island are said to hold it.

title: Dive the soft corals of Rainbow Reef
description: The Somosomo Strait between Taveuni and Vanua Levu funnels current through the reef, and the soft corals only open into full colour on the running tide - ask the dive shop which window they're timing for.

title: Walk the shifting dunes at Sigatoka
description: Fiji's only national park protecting sand dunes, and also one of its largest archaeological sites - pottery and human remains over 2,600 years old keep surfacing as the wind reshapes them.

title: Eat your way through Suva's municipal market
description: Fiji's real capital rather than the resort coast - a two-storey market thick with kava roots, fire-roasted cassava and Indo-Fijian curry stalls, busiest and cheapest early on a Saturday.

title: Walk the wooden storefronts of old Levuka
description: Fiji's first colonial capital and now a UNESCO World Heritage town, barely changed since the 1880s - reachable only by a slow ferry or a rough road over Ovalau's interior.

title: Stand on the ash fields below Tavurvur volcano
description: The 1994 eruption buried the old town of Rabaul in ash and shifted the provincial capital to Kokopo - Tavurvur still smokes constantly, and a local guide is not optional given how fast conditions change.

title: Walk into the Japanese barge tunnels at Kokopo
description: Rabaul held over 100,000 Japanese troops by 1943, and the hand-dug tunnels built to hide barges and field hospitals from Allied bombing still run deep into the hillsides around Kokopo.

title: Watch a thousand tribes perform at the Goroka Show
description: PNG's biggest sing-sing, timed around Independence Day - clans that would never otherwise share a stage turn up in bird-of-paradise plumes and clay paint to out-perform each other for a weekend.

title: See the highlands sing-sing at the Mount Hagen Show
description: Started in the 1960s to defuse tribal fighting by turning rivalry into performance - hundreds of groups still travel for days on foot to compete in war paint that took hours to apply.

title: Watch the yam harvest festival on the Trobriand Islands
description: Anthropologist Malinowski's 'Islands of Love' - a matrilineal society whose yam harvest is marked by competitive Milamala dancing, and the real challenge is simply finding a boat or charter flight out here.

title: Watch the land divers of Pentecost Island
description: The original bungee jump - men dive head-first off 20m wooden towers with vines tied to their ankles, timed to the yam harvest. The vine length is judged by eye alone, and it has gone wrong before.

title: Drink kava at a Port Vila nakamal at dusk
description: Ni-Vanuatu kava is stronger and drunk in near silence, unlike the social bowls elsewhere in the Pacific - order a shell, spit once, drink it in one go, and expect your lips to go numb.

title: Walk a bush-medicine trail through Ekasup village
description: A short drive from the resorts but run entirely by the custom village it sits in - a demonstration of pig-killing ceremony, bush medicine and hunting traps rather than a show staged for cruise days.

title: Walk the 25km lagoon beach at Ouvea
description: Often rated among the best beaches on earth and among the least visited - a 1988 hostage crisis kept tourism away for years, and the Kanak community here still controls access to parts of the island.

title: Walk among giant kauri and the drowned forest at Riviere Bleue
description: A dam flooded part of the forest decades ago, leaving dead trunks standing in the lake water - also one of the last strongholds of the kagu, a flightless bird found nowhere else on earth.

title: Ride to the Vaipo waterfall in the Hakaui Valley
description: One of the tallest waterfalls in French Polynesia, reached by boat then a hike up a valley so steep and narrow the sun barely gets in - the Marquesas get a fraction of the visitors Tahiti does.

title: Find Gauguin's grave above Atuona
description: Paul Gauguin and Jacques Brel are buried a few metres apart in a small hillside cemetery above the harbour, both having chosen to end their lives on one of the most remote inhabited island groups on earth.

title: Feed the sacred blue-eyed eels at Faie
description: Freshwater eels over a metre long with genuinely blue eyes, considered sacred by the village and fed by hand from the bridge - Huahine also holds some of the best-preserved marae temples in the Society Islands.

title: Tour a vanilla plantation on Taha'a
description: Taha'a grows most of French Polynesia's vanilla, hand-pollinated flower by flower since its natural pollinator doesn't exist here - it shares a lagoon with Raiatea and gets none of Bora Bora's crowds.

title: Climb Mount Vaea to Robert Louis Stevenson's grave
description: Stevenson built his last home here and is buried on the summit above it, exactly where he asked to be - his Samoan name, Tusitala, means teller of tales.

title: Swim the cave pool at Piula
description: A freshwater pool inside a lava cave next to a theological college, connected to the ocean through an underwater passage that only confident swimmers should attempt.

title: Walk the ring road of car-free Manono Island
description: No cars and barely any noise - a 90-minute circuit on foot past four villages, with Apolima and Savai'i visible across the strait the whole way round.

title: Stand under the Ha'amonga 'a Maui trilithon
description: Coral limestone slabs weighing up to 40 tonnes each, raised around 1200AD for a king with no written record of how it was done - sometimes called the Stonehenge of the Pacific, though nobody agrees on its purpose.

title: Walk the rainforest and sea cliffs of 'Eua
description: A short ferry from Tongatapu but geologically its opposite number, uplifted rather than volcanic - caves, a colony of flying foxes you can watch leave at dusk, and cliffs used to spot migrating humpbacks.

title: Crawl into Anatakitaki cave on Atiu
description: Home to the kopeka, a swiftlet found nowhere else, which echolocates in total darkness like a bat - the tour ends with a swim in an underground pool most visitors don't expect.

title: Hear the hymn harmonies at a Rarotonga Sunday service
description: Visitors are genuinely welcome at the CICC churches, and the unaccompanied four-part harmony is one of the most striking things you'll hear in the Pacific - dress modestly and stay for the whole service.

title: Walk Bloody Ridge above Honiara
description: Also called Edson's Ridge - a few hundred US Marines held this position against repeated night assaults in 1942, a turning point in the Guadalcanal campaign. Rusting artillery still sits in the grass.

title: Track turtles and hornbills on Tetepare Island
description: The largest uninhabited island in the South Pacific, protected by the descendants of the people who once left it, who now run it as a community conservation project rather than sell the logging rights.

title: Swim the royal bathing chasm at Matapa
description: A narrow, sheer-walled inlet once reserved for Niuean royalty to bathe in - calm at low tide, dangerous in a swell, and a five-minute walk from Talava.

title: Walk through the Talava Arches
description: A collapsed sea cave leaving a set of limestone arches on Niue's wildest coast, reached by a track through the Huvalu forest that keeps almost everyone away.

title: Find the Japanese bunkers on Betio beach
description: The Battle of Tarawa in 1943 killed more than 6,000 people in 76 hours - concrete bunkers and rusting guns still sit in the sand where the fighting stopped, mostly unmarked and unfenced.

title: Snorkel the WWII wrecks in Funafuti lagoon
description: US forces built the airstrip that is now Funafuti's runway in 1943 - wrecked aircraft and landing craft from that build-up still lie in the shallow lagoon a short swim from shore.

title: Walk the freshwater lagoon at Buada
description: Nauru's only body of fresh water, sitting in a subsided pit left by phosphate mining, ringed with banana and pandanus that a century of strip-mining left almost nowhere else on the island.

title: Walk into the phosphate pinnacles of Topside
description: A century of phosphate mining stripped the island's interior to a moonscape of coral limestone pinnacles - Nauru was briefly the highest per-capita income country on earth because of it, and one of the poorest soon after.

title: Walk the WWII battlefield on Peleliu
description: One of the bloodiest and most disputed battles of the Pacific war, fought over an island of questionable strategic value - rusted tanks, planes and artillery still lie in the jungle at Bloody Nose Ridge exactly where they stopped.

title: Coat yourself in mud at the Milky Way
description: A lagoon of pale limestone mud said to be a natural skin treatment - scoop it from the seabed, coat yourself, dry off in the sun, then rinse in water so turquoise it looks tinted.

title: Dive with manta rays in the German Channel
description: A channel blasted through the reef by German phosphate miners a century ago, now a cleaning station where reef mantas circle divers for as long as the current allows.

title: See the stone money banks of Yap
description: Giant carved limestone discs, some over 3m across, still hold real value and change ownership without moving - the village simply agrees who owns which one, and it stays exactly where it was quarried.

title: Walk the basalt ruins of Lelu
description: A walled royal and religious complex built with the same basalt-log technique as Nan Madol, on an islet now joined to Kosrae's main town by causeway and largely reclaimed by jungle.

title: Dive the wrecks of Kwajalein Atoll
description: One of the largest lagoons on earth by enclosed area, and the site of a brutal 1944 battle before it became a US missile-testing base - Japanese wrecks sit alongside a still-active military range.

title: Walk the invasion beach at War in the Pacific park
place: War in the Pacific National Historical Park
description: US forces landed here in 1944 to retake Guam after two and a half years of Japanese occupation - the Asan Bay Overlook and the gun emplacements above it are the clearest place in Micronesia to grasp the scale of the war.

title: Stand at the cliff of Two Lovers Point
description: A Chamorro legend of two lovers who leapt rather than be separated - now a glass-floored overlook above Tumon Bay, busiest at sunset.

title: Snorkel the reef flat at Tumon Bay
description: A shallow, current-free reef right off Guam's main hotel strip - easy enough for a first snorkel, though the coral closest to shore shows decades of sunscreen and foot traffic.

title: Reach the wild north coast at Ritidian Point
description: A wildlife refuge at Guam's northern tip protecting the island's last strip of undeveloped reef and beach, with limestone forest and nesting sea turtles where the rest of the island has long since been built over.

title: Eat kelaguen at the Chamorro Village night market
description: A Wednesday-night street market in the capital with barbecue, red rice and kelaguen - grilled meat cured in lemon, chilli and coconut - alongside live Chamorro dance.

title: Hike the ridge above Vatia in the National Park of American Samoa
description: The only US national park south of the equator, and one of the least visited in the entire system - rainforest running straight down to the reef, with flying foxes overhead in daylight instead of at dusk.

title: Snorkel the reef off Ofu Beach
description: Regularly named among the best beaches in the US national park system and among the emptiest - getting to the Manu'a group at all takes a small plane or a boat, which is exactly why it stays this way.

title: Watch seabirds nest on Pola Island
description: A sheer volcanic islet just off Vatia village, too steep for predators to reach, so red-footed boobies and other seabirds nest on it in full view from the shore.

title: Stand at Banzai Cliff and Suicide Cliff
description: In 1944, told by their own propaganda that surrender meant torture, hundreds of Japanese civilians and soldiers jumped from these cliffs rather than face the advancing US forces. Memorials from several nations now stand at the top.

title: Dive the sunbeams inside The Grotto
description: A collapsed limestone cavern reached by a steep staircase and a swim through a narrow entrance, opening into shafts of light that regularly rank it among Asia-Pacific's best dive sites - and among its more dangerous on a rough day.

title: Stand in the pits where the atomic bombs were loaded
description: Enola Gay and Bockscar were loaded from these two concrete pits at what was briefly the busiest airfield in the world - Tinian now has a few thousand residents and North Field is largely reclaimed by jungle.

title: Take the boat to Managaha Island
description: A small uninhabited islet inside Saipan's lagoon, ringed by a reef shallow enough to wade, and considered sacred ground by Chamorro and Carolinian islanders alike.

title: Look into the crater lake at Lalolalo
description: A volcanic crater lake ringed by 80m cliffs, with the remains of a WWII American anti-aircraft battery still standing at the rim from when Wallis was a Pacific staging base nobody now remembers.

title: Visit the basilica of Saint-Pierre-Chanel on Futuna
description: Built where the missionary Pierre Chanel was killed in 1841, later canonised as the South Pacific's only Catholic martyr-saint - a pilgrimage site most of the world has never heard of.

title: Sail 24 hours to Tokelau on the supply ship
description: No airstrip exists or is planned - the only way in is an overnight sailing from Apia on the government vessel, landing by small boat since none of the three atolls has a harbour large ships can enter.

title: Swim the lagoon at Nukunonu
description: The largest of Tokelau's three atolls by land area, its motu linked by causeways, in one of the least visited territories on the planet - a few dozen tourists a year, by most estimates.

title: Land at Bounty Bay and walk Adamstown
description: Home to around 40 people, nearly all descended from the Bounty mutineers and their Tahitian companions - the ship's anchor and a cannon, salvaged from Bounty Bay, sit outside the courthouse.

title: Climb to Christian's Cave above Adamstown
description: Fletcher Christian is said to have sat here watching the horizon for ships that might find him - reaching Pitcairn at all means a supply ship from Mangareva that runs only a few times a year.

title: Climb to the Cristo Rei statue above Dili
description: A 27m statue on a headland east of Dili, built during Indonesian occupation and now flanked by a stairway with stations of the cross - a quiet beach sits on the far side away from the city.

title: Climb Mount Ramelau for sunrise
description: Timor-Leste's highest point, climbed overnight so pilgrims and trekkers reach the Virgin Mary statue at the summit before dawn - on a clear morning you can see both coasts of the island at once.

title: Swim at Streets Beach, a lagoon in the middle of Brisbane
description: A free man-made sand beach and lagoon on the river opposite the CBD, left over from World Expo 88.

title: Hold a koala at Lone Pine, the world's first koala sanctuary
description: Opened in 1927 and still the largest koala sanctuary anywhere - reachable by river cruise from the city.

title: Watch the city light up from Mount Coot-tha
description: Brisbane's lookout hill, with the botanic gardens, a planetarium and the whole city grid laid out below at dusk.

title: Ride the free CityHopper ferry along the Brisbane River
description: A completely free ferry looping between Sydney Street and North Quay - the cheapest river cruise in Australia.

title: Eat your way through the shipping containers at Eat Street Northshore
description: Friday to Sunday evenings only. A riverside night market built from around 180 repurposed shipping containers, open Friday to Sunday evenings.

title: See a contemporary show at GOMA
description: The largest modern art gallery in Australia, free to enter, and home to the Asia Pacific Triennial.

title: Watch the Crocoseum show at Australia Zoo
description: The Irwin family zoo at Beerwah, built around a 5,000-seat stadium for crocodile and free-flight bird demonstrations.

title: Road-trip the Sunshine Coast from Caloundra to Noosa
description: An hour north of Brisbane - surf beaches, a volcanic hinterland and a noticeably slower pace than the Gold Coast.

title: Have breakfast on Hastings Street at Noosa Heads
description: Queensland's most polished beach town, where the main street runs straight onto a north-facing swimming beach.

title: Find the wild koalas on the Noosa National Park coastal track
description: A 5.4km headland walk past Tea Tree Bay and Hells Gates, with koalas in the trees near Tea Tree and dolphins offshore.

title: Learn to surf on the gentle break at Noosa Main Beach
description: One of very few north-facing beaches on the east coast, which makes it unusually calm and ideal for a first lesson.

title: Drive the Glass House Mountains lookout circuit
description: Thirteen volcanic plugs rising abruptly from the plain, named by Cook in 1770 and deeply significant to the Jinibara and Kabi Kabi peoples.

title: Climb Mount Ngungun at sunrise
description: The most achievable of the Glass House peaks - 2.8km return to a ledge looking straight across at Tibrogargan and Beerwah.

title: Walk the Mooloolaba Spit at first light
description: A patrolled beach, an esplanade of cafes and a trawler harbour where you can buy prawns straight off the boat.

title: Swim the calm passage water at Bulcock Beach, Caloundra
description: Sheltered behind Bribie Island, with a tidal current that locals ride like a lazy river on the run-out.

title: See the Gold Coast skyline from the water
description: 57km of surf beach backed by high-rises and canal estates - Australia's most unapologetic holiday city.

title: Look down from the SkyPoint observation deck at Surfers Paradise
description: Level 77 of Q1, and the Climb takes you outside to 270m - the tallest external building climb in the country.

title: Watch the point break from the Burleigh headland at sunset
description: A world-class right-hand point break, a headland national park full of brush turkeys, and the best sunset view back up the coast.

title: Walk the Twin Falls circuit at Springbrook
description: Gondwana Rainforests World Heritage on the rim of an ancient volcano - a 4km track that goes behind two waterfalls.

title: See the glow worms in the cave at Natural Bridge
description: A waterfall pouring through the roof of a basalt cave, whose ceiling fills with glow worms after dark.

title: Walk the treetop canopy bridges at O'Reilly's
description: Ancient Antarctic beech forest on the caldera rim, with 160km of track and a suspended boardwalk 15m up in the canopy.

title: Walk the Tamborine Rainforest Skywalk
description: A plateau of rainforest, wineries and galleries forty minutes from the coast, with a 300m steel walkway through the canopy.

title: Step into the man-made Glow Worm Caves at Tamborine
description: A purpose-built cave housing a glow worm colony, so you can see them in daylight hours and in any weather.

title: Get mobbed by lorikeets at the Currumbin morning feed
description: A not-for-profit sanctuary running a wildlife hospital, famous for the wild rainbow lorikeet feeding twice a day.

title: Ride the DC Rivals HyperCoaster at Movie World
description: Home to the tallest, longest and fastest roller coaster in the Southern Hemisphere, plus a daily parade.

title: Take on the Giant Drop at Dreamworld
description: Australia's largest theme park, with a serious thrill-ride lineup and a genuine tiger conservation program on site.

title: Drop through the Kamikaze at Wet'n'Wild
description: A huge water park on the Pacific Motorway, heated in winter, with a wave pool and a dive-in cinema.

title: Balance under the Pyramid boulders at Girraween
description: Enormous granite domes and precariously balanced boulders in Queensland's cold high country, near the wineries of Stanthorpe.

title: Drive the beach highway on K'gari
description: Formerly Fraser Island - the largest sand island on earth, where the beach is a gazetted road and only 4WDs get on. Butchulla country.

title: Swim in the pure silica sand of Lake McKenzie
description: A perched dune lake sitting on compacted sand and leaves, holding rainwater so pure almost nothing can live in it.

title: Float down Eli Creek on K'gari
description: Four million litres an hour of crystal clear freshwater running to the sea - walk up the boardwalk and float back down.

title: Photograph the rusting Maheno on Seventy-Five Mile Beach
description: A former luxury liner and WWI hospital ship blown ashore by a cyclone in 1935 and slowly disappearing into the sand.

title: Walk the Urangan Pier at Hervey Bay
description: A 868m pier left from an old sugar and timber jetty, on a bay so sheltered it has no surf at all.

title: Have a humpback swim up to the boat in Hervey Bay
description: The world's first Whale Heritage Site - humpbacks stop here to rest with their calves, and often come to inspect the boats.

title: Tour the Bundaberg Rum distillery
description: Distilling since 1888 from the region's sugar cane molasses - the tour ends in the barrel house and the tasting bar.

title: Watch a loggerhead turtle nest at Mon Repos
description: The largest loggerhead nesting concentration in the South Pacific - ranger-guided night visits, November to March. Book ahead.

title: Snorkel with manta rays at Lady Elliot Island
description: A coral cay at the southern tip of the Great Barrier Reef, reached by light plane, with resident manta rays year-round.

title: Snorkel the lagoon at Lady Musgrave Island
description: A coral cay ringed by a 3,000-hectare lagoon you can boat right into - camping is allowed, with a permit and all your own water.

title: Surf the northernmost surf beach on the east coast at Agnes Water
description: The Great Barrier Reef blocks swell everywhere north of here, so this is the last real surf beach on the Queensland coast.

title: Watch the sun set over the water at the Town of 1770
description: Named for Cook's second Australian landing, and one of the only spots on the east coast where you watch the sun set into the sea.

title: Straddle the Tropic of Capricorn marker at Rockhampton
description: The beef capital of Australia, sitting exactly on the Tropic of Capricorn, with a spire on the highway marking the line.

title: Hear a choir sing in the Cathedral Cave at Capricorn Caves
description: Privately run limestone caves with famous acoustics, and a chamber where a shaft of sunlight lands only near the summer solstice.

title: Swim the Yeppoon foreshore lagoon
description: The Capricorn Coast's main beach town, with a free stinger-safe lagoon on the foreshore and Keppel Bay islands offshore.

title: Snorkel straight off the sand at Great Keppel Island
description: Seventeen beaches and fringing coral you can swim to from shore, thirty minutes by ferry and far quieter than the Whitsundays.

title: Take the Cape Hillsborough sunrise kangaroo walk near Mackay
description: Wallabies and kangaroos come onto the beach at dawn to feed on mangrove pods - one of the most photographed sunrises in Queensland.

title: Walk the rainforest at Eungella, an island of forest in the dry
description: Rainforest isolated from the coast for thousands of years, with species found nowhere else, an hour inland from Mackay.

title: Wait for a platypus at Broken River, Eungella
description: Purpose-built viewing platforms over a clear river, and the single most reliable place in Australia to see a wild platypus.

title: Base yourself at Airlie Beach for the Whitsundays
description: The mainland gateway to the islands, with a free stinger-safe lagoon and a marina full of sailing boats going out for two nights.

title: Sail the Whitsundays for two nights
description: 74 islands inside the Great Barrier Reef, sheltered enough to sail comfortably and close enough together to anchor somewhere new each night.

title: Walk the length of Whitehaven Beach
description: 7km of 98% pure silica sand that stays cool underfoot in full sun and squeaks as you walk.

title: See the swirling sand from the Hill Inlet lookout
description: The tide pushes white silica and blue water into shifting marbled patterns at the northern end of Whitehaven - go at low tide.

title: Climb Passage Peak on Hamilton Island
description: The most developed Whitsunday island, but a 2.9km climb to 239m gets you above all of it for a view over the whole group.

title: Walk the Living Reef coral lagoon at Daydream Island
description: A small resort island with a free-form outdoor coral lagoon running through the middle of it, holding around 100 species.

title: Swim the Cairns Esplanade Lagoon
description: The launching point for the reef and the Daintree - the town beach is mudflat, so the free saltwater lagoon is where everyone swims.

title: Watch the wading birds on the Cairns Esplanade mudflats
description: An internationally recognised shorebird site - migratory waders arrive from Siberia and Alaska every summer, right beside the boardwalk.

title: Dive the Great Barrier Reef
description: The largest living structure on earth, 2,300km long and visible from space - outer reef sites are far better than the inner ones.

title: Snorkel off the sand at Green Island
description: A true coral cay with rainforest growing on it, 45 minutes from Cairns, where the reef starts a few metres off the beach.

title: Visit the turtle rehabilitation centre on Fitzroy Island
description: A continental island of rainforest and coral beaches, with a volunteer-run turtle hospital and a good climb to the lighthouse.

title: Swim at Four Mile Beach in Port Douglas
description: The comfortable base between the reef and the Daintree. Stinger nets go up from November to May - swim inside them.

title: Stand in the oldest surviving rainforest on earth
description: Around 180 million years old and continuously forested since - Kuku Yalanji country, and the only place the reef meets rainforest.

title: Stand where the rainforest meets the reef at Cape Tribulation
description: Two World Heritage areas touching at one beach. Do not swim - this is estuarine crocodile and stinger country.

title: Take a Dreamtime walk at Mossman Gorge
description: Kuku Yalanji guides lead a smoking ceremony and bush tucker walk through the gorge - the swimming holes are cold and clear.

title: Browse the Kuranda village markets in the rainforest
description: A village on the Atherton escarpment reached by train one way and cable car the other, with markets running since the 1970s.

title: Ride the Kuranda Scenic Railway past Barron Falls
description: An 1891 line hand-cut through 15 tunnels and 37 bridges up the escarpment, stopping at the Barron Falls lookout.

title: Glide over the canopy on the Skyrail Rainforest Cableway
description: 7.5km of gondola metres above World Heritage rainforest, with boardwalk stops on the way - take a glass-floor car.

title: Do the waterfall circuit on the Atherton Tablelands
description: Cool volcanic highlands behind Cairns - crater lakes, dairy country, and a 17km loop linking three swimmable waterfalls.

title: Swim under Millaa Millaa Falls
description: The most photographed waterfall in Australia - an 18m curtain into a round swimming hole, with a shampoo ad filmed here.

title: Explore the ruined Spanish castle at Paronella Park
description: A Catalan immigrant built a mock castle, ballroom and tunnels in the rainforest in the 1930s, powered by his own hydro plant. Now a ruin, lit at night.

title: Look for a cassowary at Mission Beach
description: 14km of palm-backed beach and the best chance in Australia of seeing a wild southern cassowary. Keep your distance - they are dangerous.

title: Stand at the base of Wallaman Falls
description: Australia's highest single-drop waterfall at 268m, with a steep 3.2km track down to the plunge pool and back.

title: Dive the SS Yongala wreck out of Townsville
description: A 1911 shipwreck 90m down the coast, considered one of the best wreck dives in the world - advanced certification required.

title: Walk up Castle Hill in the middle of Townsville
description: A 286m pink granite monolith rising out of the suburbs, walked daily by half the city before the heat comes up.

title: Find wild koalas on the Forts Walk, Magnetic Island
description: WWII gun emplacements at the top of a 4km walk, through one of the densest wild koala populations in northern Australia.

title: Hire a topless Barbie car at Nelly Bay
description: The Magnetic Island ferry terminal, where the local tradition is hiring a brightly coloured open-top Moke to do the island loop.

title: Feed a cassowary at Billabong Sanctuary
description: A small eco-certified wildlife park south of Townsville built around a natural billabong, with hands-on keeper sessions all day.

title: Walk the gold-boom streets of Charters Towers
description: Once so rich it was called The World, with its own stock exchange - the grand arcade and verandahs are still standing.

title: Walk inside the Undara lava tubes
description: Among the longest lava tube systems from a single volcano on earth, formed 190,000 years ago - guided access only.

title: See the Curtain Fig Tree near Atherton
description: A strangler fig that toppled into a neighbouring tree and dropped a 15m curtain of aerial roots - reached by a short boardwalk.

title: Climb Grassy Hill at Cooktown where Cook beached the Endeavour
description: The Endeavour was repaired here for 48 days in 1770 - the town holds both that history and strong Guugu Yimithirr presence.

title: Drive to the Tip of Cape York
description: The northernmost point of mainland Australia - a serious 4WD expedition with river crossings, only passable in the dry season.

title: Step inside Addis Ababa's newly opened Palace Museum
description: Explore recently restored rooms, gardens and the former emperor's car collection in a residence long closed to the public. Addis Ababa is outside Ethiopia's listed do-not-travel areas but is rated high caution; reconsider travel overall and re-check official advice, opening and local conditions immediately before visiting.

title: Read everyday Ethiopia at the university Ethnography Museum
description: Study instruments, jewellery, woodwork, religious art and domestic objects representing many of Ethiopia's language groups inside a former imperial palace. Addis Ababa is outside the listed do-not-travel areas but is rated high caution; reconsider travel overall and re-check advice, campus access and museum hours before visiting.

title: Find Addis Ababa's firsts in its city museum
description: See early photographs of the capital and a specialist display of local firsts, including Ethiopia's first motor car and telephone. Addis Ababa is outside Ethiopia's listed do-not-travel areas but is rated high caution; reconsider travel overall and re-check current advice, access and opening hours before visiting.

title: See Eritrea's archaeological record at the National Museum
place: National Museum of Eritrea archaeology visit
description: Visit the small national collection in Asmara for archaeological material and interpretation of Eritrea's cultural and natural heritage. Smartraveller advises reconsidering Eritrea overall; Asmara is outside the listed border and town do-not-travel zones, but re-check advice and museum access and consider whether travel remains appropriate.

title: Meet rescued primates with Mefou's sanctuary guides
description: Tour a rainforest sanctuary caring for chimpanzees, gorillas and monkeys rescued from the illegal wildlife trade while supporting local conservation employment. Centre Region is outside Cameroon's listed do-not-travel regions; the country remains high caution, so re-check advice and access and arrange trusted transport directly with the sanctuary.

title: Join Ebodjé's community turtle project
place: Ebodjé turtle museum and conservation walk
description: Visit an organised fishing-village ecotourism project with a turtle museum and guided conservation focus during the November-to-January nesting period. South Region is outside Cameroon's listed do-not-travel regions and borders named in the warning; Cameroon remains high caution, so re-check advice, road access and local arrangements before travel.

title: Climb into Mount Nimba's high grasslands with a guide
description: Dense lowland forest gives way to montane grassland on Guinea's highest massif, whose endemic wildlife includes a viviparous toad. The core area is a strict reserve and World Heritage site in danger, so arrange any visit through local authorities rather than treating it as an open trail.

title: Take a boat from Conakry to the Îles de Los
description: The forested islands sit just offshore from the capital and are one of the national tourism office's principal beach destinations. Boat conditions and return arrangements vary, so confirm both before leaving Conakry.

title: Walk to the cascade at Voile de la Mariée
description: A narrow sheet of water drops through greenery outside Kindia, giving the falls their bridal-veil name. Water volume changes markedly, so ask locally about recent conditions before making the detour.

title: Trek between escarpments and waterfalls in Fouta-Djalon
description: The highland plateau links deep valleys, grasslands and numerous river sources rather than a single signed route. Use a local trekking guide to connect villages and waterfalls and to check road and river conditions.

title: Look across the gorge at Kinkon Falls
description: The Kokoulo River plunges from the Fouta-Djalon plateau near Pita. The tourism guide identifies the falls but gives no operating details, so confirm the approach and safe viewpoint locally.

title: Cool off beside the cascades of Soumba
description: These rocky cascades provide a nature stop within reach of Conakry and are listed by the national tourism office among Dubréka's principal sites. Treat swimming as conditional on current flow and local advice.

title: Follow a local guide to Kambadaga Falls
description: Kambadaga is one of several named waterfall sites around Pita but receives far less attention than the region's headline falls. The official guide lists the site without access details, making local guidance essential.

title: Walk down to the cascades of Saala
description: Saala is a documented waterfall excursion from Labé in the Fouta-Djalon highlands. The tourism guide does not publish trail or water conditions, so go with someone who knows the current route.

title: Cross the channels of the Bijagós by boat
description: The World Heritage archipelago contains 88 islands and islets shaped by tides, estuaries and mangroves. Shallow banks make navigation part of the experience; use an experienced local operator and verify park permissions.

title: Track saltwater hippos with a guide on Orango
description: The Bijagós are the only place where hippos live in seawater on an almost permanent basis. Sightings are never guaranteed, and the park's community base at Anôr should be used to arrange a guided outing.

title: Watch green turtles nest on Poilão with park guides
description: Poilão holds Africa's most important green-turtle nesting beach, with tens of thousands of nests recorded in peak years. Access belongs inside a park-arranged trip; confirm the relevant nesting window and visitor rules before travel.

title: Trace the slave-trade history of Cacheu's fort and museum
description: Cacheu was an early Portuguese colonial capital and slave-trading port; the protected-area authority's visitor circuit links its fort, chapel and slavery museum. Begin at the park office to confirm access and find a guide.

title: Walk Cantanhez forest trails with a local guide
description: Cantanhez protects some of Guinea-Bissau's largest dense-forest blocks and habitat for chimpanzees, colobus monkeys and buffalo. Arrange a guide at IBAP or the park headquarters in Iemberém; wildlife sightings are not assured.

title: Paddle across Lagoa de Cufada to the birdwatching lookout
description: IBAP's documented route crosses Guinea-Bissau's largest freshwater lake by canoe to a lookout over the lake and forest. The park headquarters in Buba provides current information and local guides.

title: Paddle the Rio Blimbom through Cacheu's mangroves
description: This named park circuit threads mangroves, bird habitat and sacred forest near Cacheu. Boat visits depend on the tide, so arrange the canoe and timing at the Cacheu or São Domingos park office.

title: Canoe from Canamina into Cantanhez's forest mosaic
description: IBAP lists Canamina as a discovery trail combining dense forest, mangroves and primate habitat. It is a specific community-based route within Cantanhez, arranged through the park rather than an unsigned independent excursion.

title: Walk Chinguetti's lanes to its square-minaret mosque
description: Chinguetti grew as a caravan and Islamic-learning centre, with courtyard houses packed around a mosque whose square minaret rises from the old quarter. The mosque is an active religious site, so confirm respectful visitor boundaries locally.

title: Climb through the stone ruins of Ouadane's old ksar
description: Ouadane was one of four medieval caravan towns whose dense lanes and patio houses adapted urban life to the desert. Its old mosque is partly ruined, and local guidance helps distinguish conserved fabric from later settlement.

title: Cross the concentric ridges of the Richat Structure
description: The vast circular landform known as the Eye of Africa lies beyond Ouadane and makes sense on the ground as a sequence of rocky rings. Treat it as a remote guided desert journey and confirm vehicle, water and route conditions before departure.

title: Sail a traditional lanche through Banc d'Arguin
description: Shallow coastal waters, islands and mudflats support one of the world's great concentrations of migratory shorebirds. Motor craft are prohibited in the park's tourism guidance, so arrange a trip aboard an Imraguen sailing lanche and verify current permits.

title: Watch painted pirogues land at Nouakchott's fish market
description: Hundreds of brightly painted fishing boats return to the beach and unload directly into the market, making late afternoon the key moment. Keep clear of working crews and ask before photographing people at close range.

title: Ride alongside the desert iron-ore train
description: The railway carries iron ore from Zouérat to the mineral port at Nouadhibou across a long Saharan corridor. Passenger arrangements and safety conditions can change, so use an authorised local operator and verify the current way to travel before departure.

title: Rest beneath the palms at Terjit oasis
description: A spring-fed ribbon of palms occupies a narrow gorge in the Adrar and offers a striking pause between desert stages. The tourism office names Terjit as an oasis excursion from Atar but gives no fixed visitor arrangements, so confirm locally.

title: Camp beneath the granite monolith of Ben Amera
description: Ben Amera rises alone from the desert and is promoted by Mauritania's tourism office as a wilderness bivouac. Reaching it is a remote overland undertaking; arrange a knowledgeable driver and carry supplies appropriate to current conditions.

title: Walk beneath Kakamega's ancient rainforest canopy
description: Follow forest trails through Kenya's surviving fragment of Central African tropical rainforest, an Important Bird Area rich in primates, birds and butterflies. Carry water, food and rain protection, and confirm trail and guide arrangements before setting out.

title: Cross the wetland boardwalk at Saiwa Swamp
description: A raised boardwalk threads through Kenya's smallest national park, where patient visitors may spot sitatunga, De Brazza's monkeys and wetland birds. Bring drinking water, food and footwear that can handle mud.

title: Look for rare roan antelope in Ruma
description: Explore the Lambwe Valley on a wildlife drive or guided walk in Kenya's last remaining sanctuary for the endangered roan antelope. The park lies beyond Homa Bay, so confirm road conditions and arrive with water and food.

title: Snorkel the protected reefs of Kisite-Mpunguti
description: Take a licensed boat from the Shimoni coast to snorkel coral habitat in the Kisite marine park and adjoining Mpunguti reserve. Reef life can include turtles and dolphins; check sea conditions and operator arrangements before departure.

title: Scan Mwea's waterways for elusive birds
description: Drive through the reserve at the meeting of the Tana and Thiba rivers, watching dams and river margins for waterbirds such as Pel's fishing owl and the endemic Hinde's babbler. The final approach includes dirt road, and visitors should carry water and food.

title: Hike across quiet Ndere Island
description: Reach this small Lake Victoria national park by boat from Kisumu, then walk open island terrain shared by impala, zebra and fish eagles. Arrange the crossing and return in advance and keep clear of shoreline wildlife including hippos and crocodiles.

title: Follow the 4WD route to Kora's riverine wilderness
description: Kora links granite inselbergs, the Tana River and the conservation history around Kampi ya Simba. Kenya Wildlife Service says the entire road network requires 4WD, so carry water, food and reserve fuel and confirm gates and conditions before the remote journey.

title: Read deep time along the Karoo Fossil Trail
description: Follow a short paved trail past genuine fossils and petrified wood inside Karoo National Park. The 400-metre route is wheelchair accessible and offers an unusually direct look at the region's prehistoric record.

title: Climb the technical Pienaars Pass 4x4 route
description: Tackle a six-kilometre purpose-built 4x4 challenge in Karoo National Park. SANParks describes it as unsuitable for beginners; register at reception, pay the separate fee and confirm vehicle requirements before entering.

title: Watch the rising tide fill Geelbek with waders
description: Settle into the Geelbek hide as the tide rises across the Ramsar-listed lagoon and pushes feeding waders toward shore. Time the visit from low tide onward and bring binoculars for the smaller species that move first.

title: Climb Salpeterkop with a park guide
description: Join a guided, strenuous climb to Salpeterkop and its South African War history above Mountain Zebra National Park. Good fitness is required, and hikers should confirm current age limits, departure times and booking arrangements.

title: Fly-fish the Riet River at Lilydale
description: Practise catch-and-release fly fishing on the Riet River from Mokala's Lilydale section. Ask the park about permits and conditions; access to some fishing spots requires a high-clearance or 4x4 vehicle.

title: Climb to the painted tombs of Beni Hasan
description: Explore a Middle Kingdom cemetery cut into the cliffs above the Nile. Twelve of the upper cemetery's 39 rock-cut tombs retain decoration, including unusually detailed scenes of work, sport and daily life.

title: Explore Dendera's roof and temple chambers
description: Move through the well-preserved Temple of Hathor beneath its astronomical ceiling, then add the separately ticketed roof and underground chambers if open. Check current access and ticketing on arrival.

title: Study the battle reliefs at Medinet Habu
description: Walk through Ramesses III's remarkably preserved mortuary temple and examine carved battle narratives away from the West Bank's busiest monuments. The wider complex also held a palace, storehouses and stables.

title: Trace Cairo's domestic history at Gayer-Anderson
description: Explore two connected historic houses arranged around the separate reception and family spaces of an elite Cairo home. The museum combines preserved architecture with Gayer-Anderson's wide-ranging collection of art and objects.

title: Walk Elephantine's ruins to the ancient Nilometer
description: Take a short boat ride to an island archaeological landscape of ancient houses, temple remains and a Nilometer used to read the river. Allow time for the small museum and confirm boat return arrangements before landing.

title: Watch hippos and wetland birds in Rusizi National Park
description: The reserve is about fifteen minutes from central Bujumbura and combines lagoons, flooded grassland and palm forest. Go with an experienced guide and treat wildlife distance as non-negotiable.

title: Hike with a ranger beneath Kibira's montane canopy
description: Kibira protects more than 40,000 hectares along the Congo-Nile divide. Access is through Busekera or Rwegura, and the tourism ministry describes ranger-led walks rather than independent entry.

title: Hear the royal drums performed at Gishora
description: The hilltop residence holds the sacred-drum sanctuary associated with Burundi's UNESCO-listed royal drum tradition. Arrange the visit rather than assuming a performance is running when you arrive.

title: Walk between the cascades of Karera Falls
description: Karera divides into six branches over three levels amid forest in southeastern Burundi. Wet rock and changing water levels make local guidance more useful than the modest walking distance suggests.

title: Follow the stream at Burundi's southern Nile source
description: A small pyramid on Mount Kikizi marks the source identified in 1934 by Burkhart Waldecker. The slight stream here is presented locally as the Nile's southernmost source.

title: Take a guided savannah walk in Ruvubu National Park
description: Burundi's largest protected ecosystem covers more than 50,000 hectares and holds buffalo, antelope, monkeys and hippos. The official tourism guidance points visitors to experienced guides for short or full-day outings.

title: Picnic above Rwegura Dam on Kibira's edge
description: Rwegura is one of Kibira's two official access points, but the dam viewpoint is a worthwhile stop in its own right. Pair it with a ranger-led forest visit and confirm current access locally.

title: Soak at Mugara's hot springs beside Kigwena Forest
description: The springs sit inside the low-elevation Kigwena Forest Reserve near Lake Tanganyika. Facilities and access conditions are lightly documented, so confirm locally before making the detour.

title: Climb the volcanic slopes of Mount Karthala
description: Karthala dominates Grande Comore and the national tourism office lists it among Ngazidja's natural sites. Use a local guide and verify volcanic and trail conditions before departure.

title: Walk Moroni's old quarter to the Friday Mosque
description: Moroni reflects the trading links between Africa, Arabia and Asia that shaped Ngazidja. Dress respectfully and treat the mosque as an active place of worship, with interior access dependent on local permission.

title: Boat among the islets of Mohéli Marine Park
description: The protected seascape is one of the national tourism office's named natural sites on Mohéli. Use a registered local boat operator and follow current park rules around reefs and wildlife.

title: Climb to Mutsamudu Citadel above the medina
description: Anjouan's capital has the archipelago's best-preserved medina, overlooked by a citadel with views across the old town. Confirm opening access locally because the tourism office gives no fixed visitor schedule.

title: Swim off Mitsamiouli's north-coast beach
description: The national tourism office lists this beach on Grande Comore's north coast. Check sea conditions on arrival and carry what you need, as services can be limited away from town.

title: Swim below Anjouan's green escarpments at Moya Beach
description: Moya is one of the beaches identified by the national tourism office on steep, volcanic Anjouan. Road and sea conditions deserve a same-day local check.

title: Hike to crater-ringed Lake Dzialandzé
description: The national tourism office identifies Dzialandzé as an Anjouan natural site, beyond the island's better-known medina and beaches. Arrange a local guide because trail detail and facilities are not published consistently.

title: Circle the rim of Lac Salé on Grande Comore
description: This small crater lake is an official Ngazidja natural-site listing near the island's northern tip. Stay on established ground around the rim and ask locally about current access.

title: Hike from Pas de Bellecombe toward Piton de la Fournaise
place: Piton de la Fournaise crater approach
description: The road reaches the Enclos viewpoint, but access farther onto the volcano changes with eruptions and official closures. Check the observatory and prefecture status before leaving.

title: Hike into roadless Cirque de Mafate
description: Mafate has no roads and its villages are reached on foot or by helicopter. Plan food and lodging ahead because even village supplies arrive mainly by air.

title: Climb Piton des Neiges from Cilaos
place: Piton des Neiges ascent from Le Bloc
description: The Le Bloc route begins inside Cirque de Cilaos and climbs to the roof of the Indian Ocean. Mountain weather changes quickly, so check trail notices and refuge availability.

title: Enter a lava tunnel with a qualified guide
description: Guided trips enter passages formed by the 2004 and 2007 flows near Sainte-Rose and Saint-Philippe. Booking is required and operators supply helmets and lights; bring long trousers and sturdy shoes.

title: Stop beneath the waterfalls of Cirque de Salazie
description: Voile de la Mariée can be seen from the road into Salazie, while reaching its lower pools needs a hike. Heavy rain feeds the falls but can also make trails unsafe.

title: Learn how Bourbon vanilla is cured at La Vanilleraie
description: The official museums-and-gardens route recommends this working vanilla stop in the north. Reserve a guided time if you want the production explanation rather than only the shop.

title: Trace indenture history at Lazaret de la Grande Chaloupe
description: The former quarantine site anchors the official western museums route and interprets settlement, slavery and indenture. Check opening days before taking the coastal detour.

title: Walk to Takamaka's forested waterfall viewpoints
