description: Takamaka's trails overlook a wet, deeply cut landscape of pools and falls above Rivière des Marsouins. Rain can transform footing and river levels quickly, so use current local trail advice.

title: Walk the crater rim around Lac Dziani
description: The marked circuit takes about an hour above the turquoise crater lake. Swimming is forbidden because its alkaline water is corrosive.

title: Snorkel with green turtles off N'Gouja Beach
description: Green and hawksbill turtles use Mayotte's lagoon year-round and N'Gouja is a recognised observation beach. Keep clear of resting animals and never touch or feed them.

title: Climb Mount Choungui for a lagoon panorama
description: At 594 metres, Choungui is Mayotte's second-highest summit and overlooks the south and lagoon. The final climb is steep, so check trail conditions and use a local guide if unfamiliar with the route.

title: Boat to the white sand of the Choizil islets
description: The two undeveloped islets sit about 800 metres offshore and have no shade, food or water. Walking access exists only at low tide and the rising sea can cut off the return, making a local boat the safer choice.

title: Ride the public barge between Petite-Terre and Grande-Terre
description: The roughly fifteen-minute crossing is everyday transport for Mahorais and gives an immediate view across the island and lagoon. Check the current passenger timetable at the terminal.

title: Follow the coast into Saziley Marine Reserve
description: The southern trail rises above protected beaches and looks toward the white-sand islet offshore. Carry water and follow current reserve guidance around turtle nesting areas.

title: Paddle through Bouéni Bay's mangrove channels
description: Mayotte's best-known mangrove covers about 200 hectares and shelters nearly 28 bird species. The tourism board recommends a guide because the route mixes dry passages with kayak or pirogue sections.

title: Snorkel the clear shallows between the Choizil islets
description: Reef shelter gives the islets unusually clear water for fish and coral viewing. There are no facilities or shade, so travel with a professional and bring sun protection and drinking water.

title: Climb through cloud forest toward Pico Basilé
description: At 3,011 metres, Pico Basilé is the country's highest point and the summit can reveal Cameroon across the Gulf when cloud lifts. Confirm protected-area access and go with local guidance.

title: Step inside Malabo's twin-towered cathedral
description: The pink neo-Gothic cathedral opened in 1916 and its two towers rise about 40 metres. Respect services and confirm interior access before entering.

title: Hike to the forest waterfalls at Ureka
description: The falls lie in a Bubi sacred landscape near beaches used by nesting turtles. Visits should be locally guided so community and conservation restrictions are respected.

title: Track rainforest wildlife in Monte Alén National Park
place: Monte Alén National Park guided trek
description: The protected rainforest supports primates, antelope and exceptional birdlife. Infrastructure is limited, so arrange permits, transport and a guide before leaving Bata.

title: Boat to the beaches of Corisco Island
description: The tourism ministry promotes Corisco for its undeveloped beaches and clear water. Boat and lodging logistics require advance local arrangement rather than a spontaneous day trip.

title: Explore Annobón's volcanic island landscapes
description: Annobón combines steep green terrain, beaches and a crater-lake landscape far from the mainland. Confirm flights, local transport and accommodation before committing.

title: Visit the monumental basilica at Mongomo
place: Basilica of the Immaculate Conception Mongomo
description: The national tourism ministry identifies it as one of Africa's largest basilicas. It is an active religious site, so verify opening access and dress accordingly.

title: Watch the Río Benito flow beneath Mbini Bridge
description: The modern bridge across the Río Benito frames a quieter mainland stop with nearby beaches and local food. Treat it as a daylight detour and confirm transport back.

title: Visit a Batammariba takienta with a local guide
description: Koutammakou is a living cultural landscape, not an open-air museum. A community guide can explain how the mud tower-houses connect domestic, farming and ritual life.

title: Take the guided history tour inside Wood Home
description: The 1835 house interprets the region's clandestine slave trade through a guided visit. The tourism ministry lists the tour at about one hour; confirm current hours and price.

title: Walk down to the forest pool at Womé waterfall
description: Womé is a recognised tourism site near Kpalimé with local guides at the village. Rain changes the path and pool conditions, so follow on-site advice.

title: Explore Fazao-Malfakassa with park guidance
description: Togo's largest reserve spans roughly 2,000 square kilometres across the Fazao and Malfakassa ranges. Wildlife is not guaranteed, and access should be arranged with current park guidance.

title: Ask before photographing at Akodésséwa Fetish Market
description: This is a working centre of traditional medicine and Vodun practice. The tourism ministry explicitly tells visitors to ask before photographs and not touch objects without permission.

title: Shop for wax cloth in Lomé's Grand Marché
description: Assigamé is closely linked with the Nana Benz traders who built regional businesses around wax cloth. Keep valuables secure and ask before photographing vendors.

title: See the old ironworking furnaces at Nangbani
description: The Ministry of Tourism has identified the historic furnaces for visitor-site development. Because formal interpretation remains limited, arrange a local guide in the Bassar area.

title: Hike with local guidance to Kpètè Bèna waterfall
description: This Wawa Prefecture cascade was selected by the tourism ministry for a formal visitor-site feasibility study. Confirm current access and guide arrangements in Badou.

title: Surf the long point breaks at Robertsport
description: Liberia's tourism authority highlights Robertsport for long, consistent waves suitable for several experience levels. Arrange a local surf guide and check the day's conditions.

title: Hike with a guide in Sapo National Park
description: Sapo is Liberia's largest protected area and shelters pygmy hippos, forest elephants and chimpanzees, though sightings are never assured. Remote access and rainforest travel require advance guide and transport planning.

title: Trace Liberia's founding history on Providence Island
description: The island was the 1822 landing point for freed African-American settlers and is central to Liberia's national story. Redevelopment began in 2026, so confirm public access before visiting.

title: Swim below the first cascade at Kpatawee Falls
description: The first waterfall is close to the road; reaching the second requires about an hour's brisk hike. Use the lifeguarded area and check water conditions after heavy rain.

title: Paddle a dugout canoe on Lake Piso
description: Liberia's largest lake is a tidal lagoon rich in birdlife near Robertsport. The tourism authority says traditional canoe trips can be arranged through local guesthouses.

title: Read Liberia's history inside the National Museum
description: The museum's surviving and restored collections cover ethnic heritage, photographs, art and national history. Confirm opening hours locally because published visitor information is inconsistent.

title: Boat through the coast and wetlands around Marshall
description: The national tourism authority promotes Marshall as a day trip on the Grand Bassa coast. Arrange a licensed local operator and clarify the route before departure.

title: Hear the local history of Yeala's walls and tunnels
description: Liberia's tourism authority began work in 2026 to preserve Yeala's ancient walls, nine tunnels and oral history. Visitor infrastructure is emerging, so only go with local arrangements.

title: Meet rescued chimpanzees at Tacugama Sanctuary
description: Tacugama combines chimpanzee rehabilitation with forest conservation inside the Western Area Peninsula National Park. Book the guided visitor experience rather than arriving unannounced.

title: Walk with a guide among Tiwai Island's primates
description: The 1,200-hectare Moa River island supports 11 primate species and now forms part of Sierra Leone's first World Heritage property. Access and overnight logistics should be arranged in advance.

title: Tour the ruins of Bunce Island's slave-trade fortress
description: The island lies about 32 kilometres upriver from Freetown and preserves remains tied to the transatlantic slave trade. Boat access and interpretation are best arranged with a knowledgeable guide.

title: Cross by boat to the linked Banana Islands
description: Dublin and Ricketts islands are joined by a stone causeway, while forested and beach landscapes differ between them. The islands are reached by water, so verify transport and return timing.

title: Swim in the clear river mouth at River Number Two Beach
description: This community-managed beach is one of the National Tourism Board's headline coastal sites. Check currents where river and sea meet and use local facilities.

title: Take a guided wildlife trip in Outamba-Kilimi
description: The National Tourism Board identifies the park for hippos, chimpanzees and other wildlife. Its remoteness makes transport, guiding and current access checks essential.

title: Birdwatch with community guides in Gola Rainforest
description: Gola and Tiwai were inscribed together as Sierra Leone's first World Heritage property in 2025. Arrange the trip through current conservation and community channels.

title: Boat to the slave-trade remains on Plantain Island
description: This small Atlantic island preserves traces of its seventeenth- and eighteenth-century slave-trading role. Transport and interpretation are limited, so arrange both before leaving Freetown.

title: Watch green pottery take shape in Tamegroute
description: Tamegroute's open-air workshops use simple kilns to make the village's distinctive pottery alongside its old religious quarter. Ask before entering a workshop or photographing artisans, and confirm visiting arrangements locally.

title: Eat oysters beside the lagoon at Oualidia
description: Oysters are farmed in Oualidia's sheltered lagoon and sold close to where they are raised. Choose a local producer or restaurant overlooking the water and check the day's availability rather than relying on a fixed menu.

title: See regional ceramics in Safi's national museum
description: Safi's museum brings together archaeological and ethnographic ceramics from across Morocco in the country's best-known pottery city. Verify current opening details before going, then pair the collection with the working pottery quarter.

title: Scan Dakhla Bay for flamingos and dolphins at Punta Sarga
description: The southern end of the Dakhla peninsula overlooks lagoon habitat used by migratory birds, turtles, rays and humpback dolphins. Treat sightings as a possibility rather than a promise and ask locally about a safe approach.

title: Walk among Kitulo's highland wildflowers
description: Kitulo is Africa's first botanical national park, protecting high plateau grasslands celebrated for their flowers. Bloom and trail conditions vary, so check with TANAPA before timing the journey around any particular display.

title: Circle Rubondo Island by boat
description: A park boat excursion reveals forested shores, beaches and Lake Victoria wildlife including waterbirds, crocodiles, hippos and otters. Arrange the trip through the park and regard every wildlife encounter as uncertain.

title: Look for black rhinos in Mkomazi's sanctuary
description: Mkomazi protects reintroduced black rhinos and an African wild dog breeding programme in a park reached through Same. Confirm the currently offered sanctuary experience with TANAPA; conservation work does not guarantee a sighting.

title: Follow the forest trail to Sempaya's steaming springs
description: Boiling water and steam emerge inside Uganda's only true lowland tropical rainforest, revealing the Rift Valley's active geology. Start at the Sempaya park gate and stay on the managed trail around the scalding water.

title: Hike the bird-rich Nyaburogo Gorge trail
description: This seven-kilometre ranger route begins at Toro-Semliki reserve headquarters and crosses savannah, woodland and gorge forest. It is especially strong for birds and primates, though sightings remain dependent on the day.

title: Track rhinos with community guides near Serowe
place: Khama Rhino Sanctuary guided game drive
description: This resident-managed sanctuary protects both black and white rhinos in Kalahari sandveld and funds local benefits through tourism. Book a guided drive through the sanctuary and treat close sightings as wildlife luck, not entitlement.

title: Watch waterbirds at the community-run Nata sanctuary
description: Botswana's first community-based conservation project is managed by four nearby villages and channels tourism proceeds into local development. Bird numbers depend on rainfall and pan conditions, so ask the sanctuary what is present before setting expectations.

title: Hike to the waterfalls inside Goo Moremi Gorge
description: Perennial streams cut pools and waterfalls into the Tswapong Hills within a community-managed conservation area. Arrange the hill trail with the Moremi-Manonnye project and check current water and path conditions.

title: Birdwatch beside the Okavango rapids at Popa Falls
description: Namibia's smallest game park protects riverine forest where the Okavango breaks across a quartzite ledge. More than 400 bird species have been recorded around the park; the low rapids are most visible when river levels permit.

title: Camp self-sufficiently among Nkasa Rupara's wetlands
description: Reed channels, lagoons and termitaria islands form Namibia's largest protected wetland and support the country's largest buffalo concentration. A recovery-equipped 4WD and complete self-sufficiency are required; verify flood and access conditions before entry.

title: Hike the mountain trails of the Naukluft section
description: The mountain section of Namib-Naukluft protects Hartmann's mountain zebra habitat and offers trails through an arid escarpment landscape. Choose a route through the park office and verify permits, weather and water needs before setting out.

title: Cross Khaudum's deep-sand tracks in a two-vehicle convoy
description: Few tracks cross this unfenced Kalahari wilderness, where elephants and African wild dogs range between waterholes. Namibia's park authority requires at least two 4WD vehicles and recommends substantial water and food reserves; reconfirm conditions before entering.

title: Meet makers at Red Rocks Rwanda
description: Red Rocks is a community cultural centre in the hills near Musanze, with experiences centred on local life and creativity. Arrange a session directly and confirm the day's programme before travelling.

title: Walk through Rwanda's sacred Buhanga forest
description: This compact forest preserves a place associated with the initiation rituals of Rwanda's former kings. Visit with local interpretation so the forest's living cultural meaning is understood as well as its ecology.

title: Share food and stories with the Roots of Nyabingi
description: A rural community initiative in northern Rwanda combines local food, dance, history, birdwatching and optional walking or boating. Book through a local organiser and choose the activities that suit current conditions.

title: Descend into Bulla Regia's underground villas
description: Bulla Regia's Roman houses were designed with rooms below ground for relief from summer heat. Explore the surviving domestic architecture and mosaics with a guide, confirming site access locally.

title: Trace pre-Roman history among Makthar's dolmens
description: Makthar brings a Roman triumphal arch together with much older dolmens, revealing layers that predate the empire. Confirm opening arrangements before making the inland journey.

title: Hike the wilder trails of Mlawula
description: Mlawula protects a varied savannah, woodland and Lubombo mountain landscape rich in birds and plants. Its rougher character and limited facilities reward prepared walkers who confirm trail conditions before setting out.

title: Browse owner-run craft studios beneath Mantenga's big tree
description: This long-running craft centre gathers owner-run businesses selling beadwork, textiles, jewellery, woodcarving and contemporary Swati design. Talk with makers and check individual studio hours on arrival.

title: Join a ranger-led walk across Aride Island
description: Aride's wardens lead visitors through plantation and coastal forest to the island summit, with seabirds and rare plants along the way. Independent walking is prohibited and boat landings depend on sea conditions, so arrange the visit with an authorised operator.

title: Hike among coco de mer palms at Fond Ferdinand
description: Fond Ferdinand protects a quiet coco de mer sanctuary on southwestern Praslin, with hiking trails through its palm forest. Confirm the current guided-walk or ticket arrangements before visiting.

title: Hear living history at the Kome cave dwellings
description: Families descended from communities that sheltered here during the Lifaqane era still inhabit the cave dwellings. Take the guided visit offered through the tourist centre and treat homes and residents with care.

title: Read Lesotho's deep past at Liphofung Cave
place: Liphofung Cave and Cultural Heritage Site
description: Liphofung preserves archaeological and cultural evidence reaching back to the Late Stone Age. Use the site's interpretation to understand the cave's layered heritage and confirm access conditions locally.

title: Track habituated mandrills at Lékédi
description: Lékédi runs guided small-group approaches to free-ranging habituated mandrills in its 14,000-hectare park. The animals set the pace, so expect a physical outing and reserve directly with the park.

title: Follow the forest discovery trail at Raponda Walker
description: This protected forest near Libreville includes a discovery trail and canopy tower designed to introduce visitors to Gabon's forest biodiversity. Arrange a guide and verify current access before leaving the city.

title: Study the ancient Numidian form of Imedghassen
description: Imedghassen is an early monumental Numidian mausoleum whose form reflects Algeria's pre-Roman funerary tradition. View the protected monument respectfully and confirm local access before the trip from Batna.

title: Find the late-antique Djeddars near Frenda
description: The Djeddars are monumental funerary structures dating to the fifth and sixth centuries, extending Algeria's indigenous mausoleum tradition into late antiquity. Arrange local guidance and confirm which areas are accessible.

title: See hand-built pottery in Rabil
description: Rabil is one of Cabo Verde's surviving centres of traditional pottery, where clay is shaped by hand and fired using inherited methods. Ask locally about a workshop visit and seek permission before photographing makers.

title: Swim in Juncalinho's volcanic rock pools
description: Natural pools cut into São Nicolau's rocky shore provide a quiet place to experience the island's volcanic coast. Check swell, tides and local advice before entering the water.

title: Walk or cycle through Banco's urban rainforest
description: Banco offers a forest walk or cycle close to central Abidjan, adding a green counterpoint to the city's markets and skyline. Confirm the current entrance, route and guide arrangements before setting out.

title: Walk the old botanical garden at Bingerville
description: Bingerville's botanical garden is promoted as a quieter walking stop within an Abidjan weekend itinerary. Confirm current opening and local transport arrangements before visiting.

title: Walk among the granite hills of Dassa
description: Granite formations, caves and places of spiritual importance rise above Dassa-Zoumè. Choose a suitable trail with local guidance and respect sites used for worship or pilgrimage.

title: Paddle to the Bouche du Roy
place: Bouche du Roy guided canoe trip
description: At the Bouche du Roy, the Mono River meets the Atlantic amid mangroves, dunes and wetlands. Visit by canoe or boat with a local guide, checking weather and wildlife conditions first.

title: Follow Angola's money story at the Coin Museum
description: The Coin Museum traces exchange from nzimbu shells and salt to the kwanza through numismatic collections and audiovisual displays. Check the museum's current programme and closing time before visiting.

title: Look for wildlife in Quiçama near Luanda
description: Quiçama protects a large coastal, river and savannah landscape south of Luanda, with varied habitats and wildlife. Arrange the visit through a reputable local operator and confirm road and park conditions before departure.

title: Trace coffee from plantation to cup at Monte Café
description: The museum at Roça Monte Café explains the island's coffee culture from planting and harvest through drying and the finished drink. Arrange ahead where required and combine the displays with the surrounding coffee community.

title: Watch forest birds from Abuko's hides
description: Abuko protects a rare pocket of gallery forest, pools and savannah close to Banjul, with a bird walk, education centre and photo hides. Visit early or late in the day and follow reserve guidance around wildlife.

title: Snorkel the reefs around Moucha and Maskali
place: Moucha and Maskali islands reef trip
description: These low coral islands near Djibouti City combine mangroves, beaches and shallow reefs rich in marine life. Travel with a reputable local boat operator and confirm sea and security conditions on the day.

title: See regional art at the Musée du Cercle africain
description: Pointe-Noire's regional museum presents African art and photography in a compact exhibition space. Confirm current public access before visiting and allow time to engage with the local context of the collection.

title: Trace Chizarira's hidden gorges
description: Explore a remote escarpment park of deep gorges, springs and broad Zambezi Valley views. Access finishes with a dirt-road climb to headquarters; arrive self-sufficient with food, water, first aid and camping equipment if staying overnight.

title: Watch waterbirds gather on Kazuma Pan
description: Drive the open grassland of one of Zimbabwe's least-visited parks when rain fills its pans and draws large numbers of waterbirds. Entry arrangements and road conditions should be confirmed with ZimParks because the border-area park is remote.

title: Descend to Chinhoyi's blue Sleeping Pool
description: Walk carefully into Zimbabwe's extensive limestone-and-dolomite cave system to see the clear blue Sleeping Pool. The rocks can be slippery, and the caves carry both documented local history and continuing spiritual significance.

title: Birdwatch and boat at quiet Umzingwane
description: Spend a low-key day birdwatching or boating at a recreational park about 38 kilometres southeast of Bulawayo. Bring supplies and keep well back from the shore where crocodiles and hippos are present.

title: Walk the Potholes route in Umfurudzi
description: Arrange a scenic walk to the Potholes within Umfurudzi's established tourism zone. The current park plan permits hiking, walking safaris, swimming and picnicking there; confirm access and guiding with management before travel.

title: Swim below the veils of Kundalila Falls
description: Follow the Kaombe River to a 70-metre fall surrounded by a natural botanical garden. Visitors can view the Luangwa Valley from above or swim in the deep pool below; check water conditions before entering.

title: Camp beside remote Lumangwe Falls
description: Detour nine kilometres from the Kawambwa-Mporokoso road to a broad waterfall that sustains a pocket of rainforest. Simple visitor facilities allow camping, but the remote location calls for supplies and current road advice.

title: Find the three cascades of Kabweluma
description: Walk to three successive cascades five kilometres downstream from Lumangwe, with a wooded ravine and rock paintings nearby. Kabweluma is a revered local shrine, so follow local guidance and behave respectfully.

title: Walk behind the water at Chisimba Falls
description: Explore trails and viewpoints around three linked falls on the Luombe River, including a path behind the water into a sacred cave. Respect the site's Bemba spiritual rules and use care on wet ground.

title: Follow the long cascade sequence at Chipoma
description: Trace a 500-metre sequence of rapids and small falls on the Chimanabwe River, with a total drop of about 40 metres. The official tourism page says the falls reach their maximum flow in January and gives the turnoff south of Chinsali.

title: Hike to the waterfalls above Gurué
description: Reach clear cascades near the Licungo headwaters by 4x4 approach or on foot, then continue on ecological trails through the Namuli landscape. Arrange local guidance and check track conditions before leaving Gurué.

title: Walk from tea country into the Namuli Mountains
description: Explore the highland scenery around Mount Namuli, where mountain slopes meet tea and coffee country. The national tourism authority presents the range for nature and agricultural tourism; arrange a guide and current route advice locally.

title: Climb to Chinhamapere's sacred rock art
description: Hike with a local guide to rock paintings at Chinhamapere, a place the national tourism authority describes as sacred to nearby communities. Ask permission locally, follow cultural guidance and confirm trail conditions before climbing.

title: Snorkel Inhaca's biologically rich coast
description: Cross Maputo Bay to snorkel around an island recognised for biological importance and diverse marine life, including coral, turtles and marine mammals. Use a local operator and check tides, weather and protected-area rules.

title: Track Coquerel's sifakas in Ankarafantsika
description: Walk a signed circuit through dry forest habitat for Coquerel's sifaka and other endemic wildlife. Madagascar National Parks says the park is accessible throughout the year via the RN4; use its local guiding system.

title: Walk the Simpona circuit for silky sifakas
description: Hike between Camp Mantella and Camp Marojejya through the transition from lowland to mid-altitude forest, watching for the rare silky sifaka. The drier window from August to mid-November is the park's preferred general visiting period.

title: Follow Baie de Baly's Bemosary beach circuit
description: Join a park agent or local village guide for a six-hour beach-and-forest circuit in Baie de Baly. The route is designed for spotting day lemurs, chameleons, snakes and forest birds.

title: Climb Zahamena's Bemoara forest circuit
description: Take the steep three-hour Bemoara route through eastern rainforest habitat for indri, ruffed lemurs, orchids and giant ferns. Confirm local access and guiding before travelling to this rarely visited park.

title: Hike with community guides to Dindéfélo Falls
description: Walk through a community-managed reserve to the Dindéfélo cascade while supporting trained local guides and conservation. Current reporting confirms regular visitors and a locally collected entry fee; arrange the visit through the reserve.

title: Explore Palmarin's community reserve
description: Book a locally managed nature visit in Palmarin at the edge of the Saloum landscape. The reserve's deputy conservator describes tourism revenue as part of its community conservation model and confirms year-round visitation.

title: Join an ecoguide in Guembeul reserve
description: Visit this Ramsar wetland with a community ecoguide to watch birds and learn how the reserve breeds threatened antelope for transfer to other protected areas. The reserve receives visitors year-round and has a small welcome area for local crafts.

title: Walk the bird-rich forests of Dzalanyama
description: Take a shaded forest walk in Dzalanyama, one of the reserves highlighted by Malawi's tourism department for hiking and strong birdlife. Confirm a suitable route and local access before departure.

title: Hike beneath Ntchisi's shady canopy
description: Walk in the cool forest of Ntchisi, which Malawi's official tourism site recommends for pleasant trails and birdwatching. Ask locally about current trail conditions and whether guidance is needed.

title: Meet Malawi's deep past at Karonga Museum
description: See dinosaur fossils alongside early-human and prehistoric material at the Culture and Museum Centre Karonga. The government tourism page identifies the museum as a partnership with Malawi's Department of Museums and Monuments.

title: Walk the gentle Coq Du Bois Loop
place: Bras d'Eau Coq Du Bois Loop
description: Follow a gentle forest loop past an old orchard in Mauritius's quieter Bras d'Eau National Park. Stop at the visitor centre for current trail information and watch for endemic birds around the woods and Mare Sarcelle.

title: See shipwreck relics at Mahébourg Museum
description: Explore an 18th-century mansion containing old maps, weapons, a dodo skeleton and material recovered from shipwrecks and naval battles. The national heritage building also has extensive gardens and a reconstructed colonial village.

title: Trace Dutch and French history at Frederik Hendrik
place: Frederik Hendrik Museum and fort ruins
description: Visit a small museum and the ruins of a Dutch fort at Vieux Grand Port. Archaeological finds and surviving spaces including a prison, bakery and blacksmith workshop span roughly four centuries of island history.

title: Take the short forest path to Asenema Falls
description: Walk five minutes from the road on a marked rainforest trail to a small waterfall outside Akropong. Flow is strongest in the rainy season from April to October, and the approach has broad views over the Akuapem Hills.

title: Hike the demanding path to Nchiraa Falls
description: Take a challenging rural hike to Nchiraa Waterfalls about 30 kilometres north of Wenchi. Ask locally about the route and consider combining the trip with the nearby Wurobo ancestral caves.

title: Watch Mona monkeys at Duasidan
description: Visit a small sanctuary about 10 kilometres southwest of Dormaa Ahenkro to see Mona monkeys moving through bamboo habitat. Confirm current opening and local guiding arrangements before making the detour.

title: Climb Yaxhá above twin jungle lakes
description: Walk a forested Maya city where causeways link plazas and temples above two lakes.

title: See living Maya ceremony at Iximché
description: Explore the Kaqchikel capital and respect any ceremonies taking place at its active sacred altar.

title: Read the carved stories at Quiriguá
description: Follow a compact park of monumental carved stelae amid lowland forest.

title: Trace two cultures at Tak’alik Ab’aj
description: Walk terraces and monuments showing the long transition between Olmec and Maya traditions.

title: Find an ancient city inside modern Guatemala City
description: Walk surviving mounds and plazas from a Maya city now enclosed by the capital.

title: Canoe Crooked Tree’s wetland at birding pace
description: Paddle lagoons and marsh with a local guide, watching waterbirds and wetland wildlife.

title: Stand beneath Nim Li Punit’s tall carved stelae
description: Explore a southern Maya site known for a plaza of carved stone monuments.

title: Hike from Maya mounds to Bocawina waterfalls
description: Choose a short or longer forest trail linking small Maya sites and waterfalls.

title: Walk the short jungle trail at Billy Barquedier
description: Follow a forest trail to a freshwater waterfall and swimming area.

title: Hike El Imposible with a community guide
description: Use the park’s local guides for forest trails, viewpoints and river crossings.

title: Pair civil-war history with the hill above Perquín
description: Visit the local museum, then take the short trail above town for views across Morazán.

title: Walk the living collections at Lancetilla
description: Explore tropical plant collections and forest trails near Tela.

title: Ride the rail-and-boat route into Cuero y Salado
description: Enter a coastal wetland refuge for guided wildlife watching among mangroves and rivers.

title: See ancient deposits inside the Talgua Caves
description: Take the managed cave route through limestone chambers associated with archaeological remains.

title: Reach El Castillo’s river fortress by boat
description: Travel the San Juan River to a small settlement dominated by its historic fortress and museum.

title: Walk the old cemeteries of Greytown
description: Visit the historic British, Freemason, American and Catholic burial grounds with local guidance.

title: Boat into Los Guatuzos wetlands
description: Arrange a guided wetland visit from the Río San Juan region for waterbirds and forest wildlife.

title: Hike to La Estanzuela’s dark-rock cascade
description: Follow the community reserve trail to a waterfall where guided climbing may be offered.

title: Trace pre-Columbian engineering at Guayabo
description: Walk marked trails past stone roads, mounds and still-functioning waterworks.

title: Descend into Barra Honda with a park guide
description: Reserve the guided descent into a limestone cave and stay within the park’s strict group limits.

title: Walk the dry-forest shore at Bahía Junquillal
description: Explore a managed coastal refuge of dry forest, beach and calm coves.

title: Explore Las Baulas beyond the surf towns
description: Visit the marine park’s beach and estuary habitats, following current ranger controls.

title: Hike the seasonal forest of Diriá
description: Walk a small inland national park protecting transition forest and headwater streams.

title: Walk Panamá’s recovering salt-flat landscape
description: Choose a marked trail through arid salt flats, dry forest and archaeological traces.

title: Hike between Alto de Piedra’s waterfalls
description: Follow an undeveloped forest route to a chain of cascades near Santa Fe.

title: Join a managed turtle watch on Isla Cañas
description: Cross the mangroves by local boat and use an authorised guide during nesting activity.

title: Walk the Panamanian side of La Amistad
description: Arrange a local guide for cloud-forest trails in the transboundary protected area.

title: Climb the Balcony of Iberia trail
description: Follow a demanding park trail through wet forest to a high plateau and waterfall.

title: Row through Taco Bay’s mangroves
description: Take the park’s small-boat route through mangroves where manatees may be observed without guarantees.

title: Meet eastern Cuba’s natural history in Gibara
description: Visit the small local museum’s rooms on birds, reptiles, geology and marine life.

title: Explore Tanque Azul with a qualified local operator
description: Use a specialist operator for the flooded cave system in the Caletones reserve.

title: Travel the far-east road to Punta de Maisí
description: Follow a locally arranged excursion to Cuba’s eastern tip, its lighthouse and coastal viewpoints.

title: Walk Holywell’s Oatley Mountain Trail
description: Take the one-hour forest circuit past several mountain viewpoints.

title: Explore Cockpit Country with Maroon guides
description: Join a community guide to learn how limestone caves shaped Maroon resistance and rural life.

title: Hike and eat with the Bunker’s Hill community
description: Walk to forest caves, hear local and Maroon history, and share traditionally prepared food.

title: Read Jamaica’s layered history at Seville
description: Explore the great house collection and grounds spanning Indigenous, Spanish, British and African histories.

title: Follow cacao from farm to chocolate in Canducito
description: Book the rural cacao route to meet growers and learn the crop’s local production cycle.

title: Explore Dominican folk culture at Centro León
description: Use the permanent galleries to connect music, visual art and everyday Dominican identity.

title: Walk the cascades of Saltos de Jima
description: Follow the protected riverside trail through forest to a chain of cascades, checking conditions locally.

title: Walk Clifton’s Lucayan, Loyalist and African landscapes
description: Follow trails through ruins, dunes, wetlands and the remains of enslaved community life.

title: Walk Eleuthera’s native-plant trails
description: Explore interpreted trails focused on Bahamian plants, bush medicine and coppice habitats.

title: Watch flamingos with an Inagua guide
description: Arrange local transport and guiding to observe the island’s protected flamingo habitat.

title: Learn community conservation at Casa Pueblo
place: Casa Pueblo and Bosque del Pueblo
description: Visit the community cultural centre, then arrange access to the forest it helped protect.

title: Tour Hacienda Buena Vista’s water-powered works
description: Reserve a guided visit to the restored coffee estate and its historic hydraulic machinery.

title: Enter Nariva Swamp with a wetland guide
description: Arrange an appointment-based visit for wetland birds and other wildlife without sighting guarantees.

title: Walk Lopinot’s cocoa house and village trails
description: Explore the estate’s cocoa house, bridge and paths while confronting its plantation history.

title: Read the sugar landscape at Morgan Lewis Mill
description: Visit the windmill exterior and equipment exhibit, checking restoration access before setting out.

title: Land on Maria Major with an authorised guide
description: Join a National Trust boat visit; independent landing is prohibited and nesting closures may apply.

title: Learn cassava and Creole traditions at Fond Latisab
description: Join a locally hosted cultural visit centred on foodways, music and traditional skills.

title: Make Grenadian chocolate from tree to bar
description: Prebook the small-group workshop that follows cocoa from propagation and drying to chocolate.

title: Read Carriacou’s island history in its community museum
description: Visit the locally run collection on archaeology, seafaring, crafts and island traditions.

title: Swim inside Owia’s lava-rock pool
description: Visit the Atlantic-edge pool only in settled conditions and follow local safety advice.

title: Look for the Saint Vincent parrot on Vermont trail
description: Use the managed forest trail quietly for a chance, never a promise, of seeing the endemic parrot.

title: Confront plantation history at Betty’s Hope
description: Walk the restored mill and ruins while learning about the enslaved people who powered the estate.

title: Hike Wallings with its community custodians
description: Use the community reserve’s forest trails and current local route guidance.

title: Listen for parrots on the Syndicate trail
description: Walk the short forest loop quietly for a chance, never a promise, of seeing endemic parrots.

title: Tour Kalinago Barana Autê with a community guide
description: Learn about structures, crafts and foodways through interpretation by Kalinago hosts.

title: Trace water, labour and rock art at Wingfield
description: Walk the estate yard to see its unusual aqueduct and nearby rock carving, with local interpretation.

title: Tour Fairview’s house and volcanic-stone bath
description: Visit the restored great house and garden while keeping enslaved plantation labour central to the story.

title: Follow aloe from field to factory in Hato
description: Take the guided plantation, museum and factory visit to understand Aruba’s aloe industry.

title: Walk San Nicolas with the mural curator
description: Join a small guided walk explaining the artists and stories behind the town’s street gallery.

title: Hear many voices at Savonet Museum
description: Explore audiovisual and object-based accounts of Indigenous, enslaved and later communities.

title: Walk the Cathedral of Thorns labyrinth
description: Book a guided visit to Herman van Bergen’s thorn-built art labyrinth and performance space.

title: Walk Grand Cayman’s old-growth Mastic Trail
description: Use the National Trust trail through inland forest for endemic birds and reptiles.

title: Meet Cayman’s blue-iguana recovery programme
description: Take the managed conservation tour at the botanic park rather than treating wildlife as a photo prop.

title: Read Cheshire Hall beyond its stone ruins
description: Use a guided heritage visit to understand Loyalist cotton production and enslaved labour.

title: Walk Wade’s Green with historical context
description: Explore surviving plantation structures while centring the lives and labour of enslaved people.

title: Walk Virgin Gorda’s Cornish copper ruins
description: Explore engine-house and chimney remains on exposed coastal cliffs, keeping clear of shafts.

title: Find Tortola’s last windmill at Mount Healthy
description: Visit the compact park and view plantation-era mill remains with appropriate historical context.

title: Learn Crucian traditions at Estate Whim
description: Tour the great house and grounds, then seek living-history demonstrations by local tradition bearers.

title: Paddle Salt River Bay after dark
description: Use a permitted local operator for a low-light paddle and follow conditions and park guidance.

title: Step inside early Bermuda at Carter House
description: Visit the small museum, settler-cabin reconstruction and native garden during published opening days.

title: Walk Spittal Pond’s nature and freedom trail
description: Follow the reserve paths to coastal geology and Jeffrey’s Cave, tied to an enslaved man’s escape.

title: Hike La Soufrière from Saint-Claude
description: Check volcano, weather and trail notices before climbing the marked summit route.

title: Study slavery and its legacies at Mémorial ACTe
description: Explore interpretation of the slave trade, slavery and their abolitions.

title: Walk the wind-cut Pointe des Châteaux
description: Take the signed coastal path and keep back from exposed cliff edges and surf.

title: Cross to Fort Napoléon above Terre-de-Haut
description: Visit the fort museum and grounds after confirming ferry and opening times.

title: Explore Grande Rivière valley below La Grivelière
description: Explore the accessible valley only; Habitation La Grivelière itself is closed for renovation.

title: Climb Mount Pelée by the Aileron route
description: Start early, check mountain weather and use the established volcanic trail.

title: Cross the canopy bridges at Jardin de Balata
description: Walk tropical collections arranged around a Creole house, including elevated canopy bridges.

title: Tour Habitation Clément’s house, art and rum heritage
description: Explore the restored house, former distillery, gardens and contemporary-art programme.

title: Cross the arid Savane des Pétrifications
description: Carry water and sun protection for an exposed walk through Martinique’s unusual dry landscape.

title: Walk Domaine d’Émeraude’s interpreted forest
description: Choose a short interpreted forest circuit and visit the pavilion on island biodiversity.

title: Cross to Musée Archipélitude on Île aux Marins
description: Cross in season to see island customs and traditional skills interpreted in the old school and preserved houses.

title: Trace island life at Musée Héritage
description: Explore ten rooms on local social, religious, medical, school and fishing history during the museum’s summer season.

title: Walk the headlands of Cap de Miquelon
description: Follow the marked coastal route with clothing for fast-changing North Atlantic weather.

title: Follow the marked trail to Anse à Henry
description: Use the well-marked coastal trail and its rest benches, checking wind and ground conditions.

title: Walk the Grand Barachois lagoon with a nature guide
description: Join the seasonal small-group walk for shorebirds and seals viewed at respectful distance.

title: Walk the quiet battlefield loop at Horseshoe Bend
description: A quiet loop crosses the Horseshoe Bend battlefield while signs explain the landscape and its contested history.

title: Land on the Arctic dunes of Kobuk Valley
description: Bush planes reach the Great Kobuk Sand Dunes; once down, there are no trails or developed facilities.

title: Thread the rock pinnacles on Echo Canyon Loop
description: Echo Canyon Loop threads between Chiricahua’s rhyolite pinnacles on a rugged route mapped by the park.

title: Walk among the Plum Bayou earthworks
description: Trails circle Plum Bayou’s ceremonial mounds and plaza, with archaeological interpretation at the visitor centre.

title: Take a first lava-tube walk in Mushpot Cave
description: Mushpot offers a self-guided introduction to Lava Beds’ tubes, with cave hazards checked before entry.

title: Find ancient stumps on the Petrified Forest Loop
description: The Petrified Forest Loop passes Florissant’s fossil stumps in open montane country.

title: Walk from an artist’s farm to Weir Pond
description: Weir Pond Trail leaves the historic studios for the woodland and pond that shaped the artists’ setting.

title: Hike the Brandywine woods at Beaver Valley
description: Beaver Valley’s woodland paths reveal a rural corner of First State National Historical Park.

title: Watch lotus and wetland birds at Kenilworth
description: Kenilworth’s boardwalk links cultivated aquatic gardens with tidal wetland habitat inside Washington.

title: Cross the inlet to compact Fort Matanzas
description: A small ferry crosses the inlet to Fort Matanzas, so the fort visit depends on current boat operations.

title: Step inside Ocmulgee’s reconstructed Earth Lodge
description: Inside Ocmulgee’s reconstructed Earth Lodge, the clay floor is an original survival from the ancient council chamber.

title: Follow the lava shore to Kaloko Fishpond
description: Kaloko’s immense dry-stacked seawall shows how Native Hawaiian fishpond engineering worked with the tides.

title: Walk the quieter granite trails at City of Rocks
description: City of Rocks’ maintained footpaths wind between granite fins and emigrant-landmark formations.

title: Read labour history across Pullman’s factory town
description: Pullman’s factory grounds connect an ambitious planned community with the labour conflict embedded in its streets.

title: Enter the riverside rotunda at Vincennes
description: The Vincennes rotunda interprets George Rogers Clark’s Revolutionary campaign beside the Wabash River.

title: Walk the restored prairie at Herbert Hoover’s birthplace
description: Restored tallgrass surrounds Hoover’s birthplace, adding an ecological walk to the compact historic site.

title: Trace Black homesteading history in Nicodemus
description: A township walk links Nicodemus’ surviving buildings to the history of Black homesteaders on the plains.

title: Walk the open-air mining story at Blue Heron
description: Blue Heron preserves a coal community as an outdoor exhibit of structures, stories and former mine life.

title: Walk the layered grounds of Oakland Plantation
description: Oakland’s buildings and grounds hold intertwined histories of plantation owners, enslaved people and later workers.

title: Hear the Wabanaki and French story above Saint Croix Island
description: A shore trail overlooks Saint Croix Island while interpreting both Wabanaki presence and the early French settlement.

title: Find the Civil War batteries at Fort Foote
description: Wooded paths at Fort Foote lead to surviving earthworks and river-defence batteries south of Washington.

title: See an early ironworks turn by water power
description: Reconstructed furnaces, forge and waterwheels make early iron production tangible at Saugus.

title: Read copper-country history above Hancock
description: Quincy’s hillside retains shafts, hoist buildings and smelting history; partner tours vary by season.

title: Circle the pipestone quarries with cultural context
description: Pipestone’s short Circle Trail links prairie, quarry features and a living Indigenous cultural landscape.

title: Walk the compact Brices Cross Roads battlefield
description: The compact Brices Cross Roads landscape makes the battlefield’s movements legible without a long driving tour.

title: Follow George Washington Carver’s woodland trail
description: Carver Trail crosses the woods and fields of George Washington Carver’s childhood landscape.

title: Watch ranch history stay practical at Grant-Kohrs
description: Grant-Kohrs keeps ranch history practical through preserved work buildings and live demonstrations.

title: Climb past fossilised spiral burrows at Agate
description: The Daemonelix Trail climbs to corkscrew-shaped fossil burrows preserved in Nebraska’s prairie bluffs.

title: Walk a desert wash rich in Ice Age clues
description: Tule Springs has undeveloped desert routes, where careful walking protects exposed Ice Age fossil resources.

title: Walk between sculpture and woodland at Saint-Gaudens
description: Saint-Gaudens combines an artist’s home and studios with sculpture placed throughout quiet garden grounds.

title: Trace water power beside Paterson Great Falls
description: Paterson’s falls and old raceways show how river power drove one of America’s earliest industrial cities.

title: Walk Quarai’s Spanish Corral Trail beyond the mission
description: The one-mile dirt loop leaves Quarai’s main ruins for piñon-juniper woodland, native plant stories and the stone remains known as the Spanish Corral.

title: Leave the house tour for Sagamore Hill’s salt marsh
description: Sagamore Hill’s nature trail slips beyond the historic house through woodland to a salt marsh.

title: Cross the reconstructed bridge at Moores Creek
description: Moores Creek’s short path crosses a reconstructed bridge and follows the compact Revolutionary battlefield.

title: Enter a reconstructed Hidatsa earthlodge
description: The reconstructed earthlodge at Knife River introduces Hidatsa village architecture through a place visitors can enter.

title: Tour Colonel Charles Young’s preserved home
description: Charles Young’s preserved home gives a focused account of a pioneering Black officer and the Buffalo Soldiers.

title: Walk the sombre Washita battlefield trail
description: Washita’s walking trail treats the 1868 attack as a sombre landscape for learning and reflection.

title: Follow a ranger into the marble Oregon Caves
description: A ranger-led route enters Oregon’s marble caves; stairs, low passages and seasonal bookings shape the visit.

title: Step into the tavern at Allegheny Portage Railroad
description: The Lemon House restores the tavern that served travellers transferring across the Allegheny Portage Railroad.

title: See early textile power at Old Slater Mill
description: Old Slater Mill places water-powered textile machinery inside the Blackstone Valley’s industrial story.

title: Walk the siege trench to Ninety Six Star Fort
description: A trail and surviving siege trench lead to Ninety Six’s distinctive earthen Star Fort.

title: Tour a preserved Minuteman launch-control site
description: Small guided groups descend into Delta-01, a preserved Minuteman launch-control facility.

title: Look into the Obed gorge from Lilly Bluff
description: A short path reaches Lilly Bluff for a broad view into the forested Obed gorge.

title: Stand above an in-situ mammoth nursery herd
description: Waco’s dig shelter lets visitors stand above Columbian mammoth remains still preserved where they were found.

title: Climb to a ranger-led Timpanogos cave tour
description: The Timpanogos visit combines a steep mountain approach with a reserved ranger-led cave tour.

title: Walk the wooded carriage roads above Woodstock
description: Historic carriage roads form a quiet walking network through the managed forest above Woodstock.

title: Tour Maggie Walker’s Jackson Ward home
description: A guided visit to Maggie Walker’s Jackson Ward home connects domestic rooms with her civil-rights leadership.

title: Walk the military and boarding-school layers of Fort Spokane
description: Fort Spokane’s grounds carry two difficult layers: a military post and a later Indian boarding school.

title: Walk the near-empty rail streets of Thurmond
description: Thurmond’s depot and near-empty rail streets preserve the scale of a former New River boom town.

title: Climb an Ice Age Trail spur to Gibraltar Rock
description: This Ice Age Trail segment climbs through woods to Gibraltar Rock’s sandstone overlook.

title: Walk Fort Laramie beyond the parade ground
description: Beyond Fort Laramie’s parade ground, restored buildings reveal everyday life at the frontier post.

title: Pause in the memorial garden at La Paz
description: La Paz’s small memorial garden holds César and Helen Chávez’s graves and honours the farmworker movement.

title: Begin Tubman’s Eastern Shore story in the landscape
place: Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad visitor trail
description: The visitor centre anchors Tubman’s story in the marshes, farms and waterways of Maryland’s Eastern Shore.

title: Listen and reflect at Sand Creek Massacre
description: Sand Creek’s overlook is a place to learn from Cheyenne and Arapaho history and reflect on the massacre.

title: Walk the remains of Minidoka incarceration camp
description: Minidoka’s walking route crosses surviving features of the Japanese American incarceration camp.

title: Walk the hoodoos with Indigenous cultural context
description: Writing-on-Stone pairs hoodoo trails with an Indigenous rock-art landscape that requires respectful interpretation.

title: Walk the river lots and church at Batoche
description: Batoche’s trails, church and river-lot landscape place Métis history back on the ground where it unfolded.

title: Hike Pukaskwa’s coast to the White River bridge
description: Pukaskwa’s demanding coastal day hike reaches a suspension bridge above the White River gorge.

title: Land among limestone monoliths in Mingan
description: Local boats land on Mingan islands where erosion has shaped freestanding limestone monoliths.

title: Cross to the preserved Roosevelt summer cottage
description: Campobello’s preserved Roosevelt cottage and grounds retain the scale of a family summer retreat.

title: Join a guided Mi’kmaq petroglyph walk at Kejimkujik
description: A guided Kejimkujik walk provides culturally respectful access to Mi’kmaq petroglyphs not open for casual viewing.

title: Cross the floating boardwalk into Greenwich dunes
description: Greenwich’s trail crosses a floating boardwalk before entering Prince Edward Island’s dune system.

title: Read Basque whaling history beside Red Bay harbour
description: Red Bay’s exhibits and archaeology reconstruct the Basque whaling station that operated on this Labrador harbour.

title: Walk tundra trails from Tombstone’s interpretive centre
description: Short tundra trails begin near Tombstone’s interpretive centre; backcountry plans require a separate level of preparation.

title: Walk between stelae deep in Calakmul’s forest
description: Calakmul’s plazas, structures and many stelae emerge from a forest setting far from Mexico’s busiest Maya circuit.

title: Climb Yagul’s terraces above the Tlacolula Valley
description: Yagul spreads palaces, murals and a ballcourt across a steep hill above the Tlacolula Valley.

title: Read desert architecture in the walls of Paquimé
description: Paquimé’s earthen walls and planned spaces trace trade between northern desert cultures and Mesoamerica.

title: Approach Cañada de la Virgen with its required guide
place: Cañada de la Virgen archaeological zone
description: Cañada de la Virgen is reached through controlled local transport and a walk to its astronomical ceremonial structures.

title: Cross volcanic desert to El Pinacate’s crater overlooks
description: El Pinacate’s route crosses a protected volcanic desert of craters, lava and immense dune fields.

title: Walk the rounded plazas of Huastec Tamtoc
description: Tamtoc’s rounded buildings and central plaza reveal a substantial Huastec settlement near Tamuín.

title: Walk between organ-pipe cliffs in Sierra de Órganos
description: Sierra de Órganos’ trails enter a protected valley of narrow, organ-pipe rock towers.

title: Find the sun shaft inside Xochicalco’s observatory cave
description: Xochicalco’s hilltop city includes a rock-cut observatory where sunlight enters through a vertical shaft.

title: Walk the curved yácata platforms at Tzintzuntzan
description: Tzintzuntzan’s broad platform carries the curved yácata structures of the former Purépecha capital.

title: Trek to the copper-tinted water of Arroyo Turquesa
description: Make the six-hour return hike to a mineral-coloured stream near Cerro Mercedario at almost 4,000 metres. Go acclimatised and confirm mountain conditions with a local guide.

title: Cross the petrified white waves of Campo de Piedra Pómez
description: Travel with a local high-altitude guide into a protected field of pale volcanic stone more than 3,000 metres above sea level. Wind has sculpted the rock into an uncanny frozen sea.

title: Walk the red slot canyons of the Cuevas de Acsibi
description: Ride by 4WD from near Seclantás, then hike roughly four hours through narrow red formations and past Kakán rock art. Entry requires a specialist guide.

title: Drive among the black cones of La Payunia volcanic reserve
description: Join an authorised excursion into a remote reserve of hundreds of volcanic cones, dark lava slopes and red-black ridges. The protected landscape sits about 300 kilometres from Mendoza city.

title: Explore Somuncurá's volcanic plateau with local baqueanos
description: Cross the isolated Patagonian steppe by 4WD with local route knowledge, then walk or ride across a volcanic tableland dotted with seasonal lagoons. Access is weather-dependent and services are sparse.

title: Camp beneath the forest sky at Salto Encantado
description: Follow forest viewpoints around a 64-metre waterfall, then stay for the park's small-scale camping and occasional Guaraní sky interpretation. Confirm the astronomy programme before travelling.

title: Hike with a guide to the Río Jordán thermal pools
description: Walk through Yungas forest to mineral-rich blue-green pools warmed to around 30°C. Visits require a guide, and river and trail conditions should be checked locally.

title: Reach the solitary cone of Arita on the high salt flat
description: Cross the high-altitude Salar de Arizaro with a local driver to see a near-perfect 200-metre volcanic-and-salt cone rising from the plain. Carry cold-weather gear despite the stark desert setting.

title: See mineral colours ring the Salto del Agrio
description: Walk to the rim where the Agrio River drops more than 80 metres into an ochre amphitheatre. Iron and sulphur tint the water and surrounding rock red, yellow and green.

title: Soak beside geysers in Sajama National Park
description: Explore Sajama's high-altitude geothermal field and thermal water beneath Bolivia's highest peak. Register with park staff, use a local guide and prepare for cold, wind and altitude.

title: Travel by river into Manuripi wildlife reserve
description: Arrange a guided river journey into a nationally protected Amazon reserve promoted as a developing nature destination. Confirm permits, transport and seasonal access before departure.

title: Enter Amboró's cloud forest with a registered guide
description: Approach the protected ecological corridor from the Samaipata side for guided walks in cloud forest and foothills. Access varies by sector, so arrange a registered guide and current park advice.

title: Swim below the Saltos waterfalls in the Cerrado
description: Hike through Chapada dos Veadeiros to a series of falls and natural pools. The official tourism board identifies the dry months from April to October as the most reliable period for local adventure travel.

title: Walk water-carved rock at Vale da Lua
description: Follow the trail to smooth, water-sculpted rock channels that resemble a lunar surface. Check rainfall and local restrictions because water levels can transform the formations quickly.

title: Hike to the framed horizon at Mirante da Janela
description: Climb through open Cerrado and rock formations to a natural window overlooking the Chapada horizon. Start early, carry water and use marked local access.

title: Visit Santa Bárbara waterfall with the Kalunga community
description: Walk through native vegetation to a turquoise waterfall near the Chapada park, arranging the visit through the local Kalunga area. Capacity and guide rules should be confirmed before travel.

title: Hike to the lip of Cachoeira da Fumaça
description: Take the high trail to a waterfall dropping roughly 390 metres from the Chapada plateau. Flow changes seasonally, so confirm conditions and carry enough water for exposed sections.

title: Enter the long limestone passages of Lapa Doce
description: Walk a guided section of a cave system extending for about 25 kilometres beneath Chapada Diamantina. Use an authorised local guide and do not assume every passage is open.

title: Paddle the flooded forest of Marimbus
description: Canoe or kayak across a broad wetland of rivers and aquatic plants, often starting near Remanso and continuing toward the Roncador River. Arrange the route locally because water conditions vary.

title: Share a wetland journey from the Remanso quilombola community
description: Begin a locally arranged Marimbus journey from a quilombola community reached by dirt road. Keep the visit community-led and pair the wetland trip with an introduction to local history.

title: Boulder on the old diamond paths above Igatu
description: Climb with a qualified local guide in Igatu's Serra Alta or Califórnia sectors, then trace stonework left by the diamond era. This is technical rock terrain, not an unguided sightseeing stop.

title: Walk among old-growth trees in Alerce Andino
description: Take a forest trail in one of the quieter northern parks on Chile's 17-park Patagonian route. Expect rain even in summer and confirm trail status with CONAF.

title: Hike between fjords and forest in Hornopirén
description: Explore a remote park of temperate forest, lakes and steep terrain along the Patagonian Parks Route. Public transport is limited, and route and weather checks are essential.

title: Walk the forest trails of Pumalín Douglas Tompkins
description: Link short forest walks and volcanic viewpoints in a park on Chile's long Patagonian route. Allow extra time for ferry and road disruptions and check individual trail openings.

title: Climb to the turquoise lagoon below Cerro Castillo
description: Tackle a steep Patagonian day hike to the lagoon beneath the castle-like ridge. Wind and fast weather changes make current park guidance and proper mountain equipment essential.

title: Watch guanacos cross Patagonia National Park
description: Walk or drive slowly through the Chacabuco Valley for open-steppe wildlife and broad mountain views. It is one of 17 parks on a route with limited transport in its most isolated sections.

title: Follow the Sierra Nevada trail above Conguillío's lava fields
description: Climb through ancient araucaria forest above volcanic lagoons and Llaima's lava landscape. Roads are largely gravel and winter access can require 4WD.

title: Hike to Selkirk's Lookout across Robinson Crusoe Island
description: Cross native island forest to a high pass with views to both coasts. Reaching Robinson Crusoe Island itself requires a charter flight and boat transfer, so reserve well ahead.

title: Walk with local guides to the Cerro Azul pictographs
description: Travel from San José del Guaviare with a local guide to rock shelters covered in ancient painted figures. Follow current community, conservation and security advice.

title: Walk beneath the sandstone span of Puerta de Orión
description: Follow a locally guided trail through the Guaviare's old sandstone landscape to a freestanding natural portal. Confirm road, rain and security conditions before leaving San José.

title: Paddle quietly into Laguna Negra
description: Take a community-arranged canoe excursion on a dark-water lagoon near San José del Guaviare. Keep noise low for wildlife and check wet-season access locally.

title: Climb the granite dome of Cerro de Mavecure
description: Journey by river from Inírida and climb ancient granite with Indigenous community guidance. The remote logistics and local access arrangements make this a planned expedition.

title: Boat the Orinoco rapids of El Tuparro
description: Arrange an authorised journey into remote Orinoco savanna and river country, where granite outcrops break the current. Check park access and regional security immediately before travel.

title: Walk the former prison island trails of Gorgona
description: Reach this offshore national park by authorised boat, then follow rainforest trails around former prison remains and rich marine habitat. Sea conditions and park rules determine access.

title: Paddle and walk with community guides at Añangu
description: Combine canoe travel, forest walks, wildlife watching and cultural interpretation at an approved Yasuní visitor site. Use an authorised operator and respect community protocols.

title: Watch river-edge wildlife at Tambococha
description: Visit one of Yasuní's designated sites for guided canoeing, walking and flora-and-fauna observation. Entry and exit hours are controlled, so travel only through an authorised itinerary.

title: Explore the forest around Indillama by canoe and foot
description: Move between river and rainforest at a low-volume designated Yasuní visitor site. Keep the experience guide-led and confirm the permitted route before departure.

title: Join a small community visit at Nueva Providencia
description: Arrange cultural interpretation, canoeing and wildlife observation at an official Yasuní visitor site. Treat the community as host, not scenery, and follow the operator's access window.

title: Canoe to the forest site of Mandaripanga
description: Use a permitted Yasuní operator for a river-and-forest day at this designated visitor location. Wildlife sightings are never guaranteed and park timing rules apply.

title: Camp by Jatuncocha lagoon with advance park approval
description: Stay beside a remote Yasuní lagoon only through an operator that has requested the required advance camping reservation. Pack for humidity and strict low-impact travel.

title: Kayak among Huancaya's stepped emerald lagoons
description: Stay at least two days in Huancaya to walk, paddle or ride beside small waterfalls and green lagoons in the landscape reserve. The overland trip from Lima is long.

title: Walk through winter-green hills at Lomas de Lúcumo
description: Choose a three-to-six-hour community trail through seasonal vegetation, rock art and wildlife habitat outside Lima. The hills are at their greenest from June to November.

title: Camp among the strange stone figures of Marcahuasi
description: Carry cold-weather camping equipment onto an Andean plateau of weathered rock formations above San Pedro de Casta. Altitude and low night temperatures demand preparation.

title: Walk the mist-fed trails of Lachay reserve
description: Follow a choice of walking circuits through coastal hills transformed by winter mist, watching for foxes and seasonal flowers. June to October brings the richest green cover.

title: Walk the painted village streets of Antioquía
description: Explore a small Andean town whose white buildings carry bright painted borders, flowers and animals, then walk to local viewpoints or fruit fields. It is roughly three hours from Lima.

title: Look across fruit orchards from Azpitia
description: Pause in a rural fruit-growing district above the Mala River valley, pairing the viewpoint with a slow local meal or short country walk. It is a low-key diversion south of Lima.

title: Soak in the Tumac springs outside Cajatambo
description: Make the long mountain journey to cobbled Cajatambo, then walk locally to warm springs in the surrounding valley. Verify road and facility conditions before setting out.

title: Climb to the stone citadel of Rúpac
description: Travel through Huaral and Pampas, then hike to high stone ruins above the cloud line. Camp only with local advice and carry warm layers and water.

title: Watch flamingos at the Campo María salt lagoon
description: Visit a salt lagoon and conservation refuge on Paraguay's Chaco-and-Pantanal route for dry-forest and wetland birdlife. Arrange local access and take supplies for heat and isolation.

title: Walk with Guaraní hosts in the Mbaracayú forest
description: Arrange a small-scale forest and cultural visit in one of the remaining Alto Paraná Atlantic Forest landscapes. Use community-approved guides and respect local access conditions.

title: Descend the gorge trail at Quebrada de los Cuervos
description: Follow a marked trail into a narrow gorge cut by the Yerbal Chico stream, through unusually lush eastern hill vegetation. Check the current booking and guide rules before arriving.

title: Follow the Tembetarí interpretive trail in Villa Serrana
description: Walk a 1.6-kilometre interpretive route through hill forest, fungi and streams near Cerro Pelado. The two-hour experience can be guided and is deliberately small-scale.

title: Walk the machinery floor of the former Anglo works
place: Museum of the Industrial Revolution, Fray Bentos
description: Tour the renewed museum inside a former meat-processing complex that reshaped global food production. The machinery and workers' landscape give a tangible view of industrial history.

title: Stay with the Makushi community at Rewa Village
description: Reach a community-owned lodge at the meeting of the Rewa and Rupununi rivers for guided fishing, wildlife and forest experiences. The journey requires internal flights, boats or 4WD transfers.

title: Boat between rainforest islands and colonial forts on the Essequibo
description: Arrange a licensed river guide to link small islands, forest banks and surviving fort sites on Guyana's largest river. Distances and currents make this a planned boat day.

title: Boat into Bigi Pan for scarlet ibis and flamingos
description: Use a local boat guide to enter the protected western wetland, watching ibis, flamingos and mangrove wildlife from the lagoon. Current government work highlights unresolved management issues, so verify operator and access arrangements.

title: Walk the forest loop of the Sentier des Géants
description: Follow a roughly three-hour park-marked circuit past giant rainforest trees and a rocky creek outside Maripasoula. Check the evolving track condition with the park or tourism office first.

title: Travel by pirogue and foot to Gobaya Soula falls
description: Ride about 20 minutes upriver from Maripasoula, then walk a maintained forest trail to local swimming falls on the Atachi Baaka foothills. Arrange transport and current advice locally.

title: Hike to the Falklands' highest summit, Mount Usborne
description: Climb to the 705-metre high point of the islands for wide views across East Falkland. Arrange land access, tell someone your route and carry strong boots and layered clothing.

title: Walk the coast to Cape Pembroke Lighthouse
description: Take the roughly three-hour walk to the archipelago's easternmost lighthouse through ponds, coves and exposed coast. Check land access and the countryside code before setting out.

title: Land at Neko Harbour and climb the marked snow ridge
description: Make an expedition-supervised continental landing, then follow the guided or marked snow route to the rocky overlook while staying ready to clear the beach if glacier calving sends waves ashore.

title: Sail the ice-choked Lemaire Channel
description: Watch the cliffs of Booth Island and the Peninsula close around the ship through this narrow west-coast passage, understanding that ice can force the expedition leader to turn back or reroute.

title: Post a card from Port Lockroy's living museum
description: On a scheduled expedition landing, step into Bransfield House's seasonal museum and post office to see early polar-science artefacts and support the heritage trust that conserves the site.

title: Visit Damoy Hut and trace Antarctica's former air link
description: Join a permission-cleared heritage landing at the former British air-transit hut, inspect its preserved interior in a small group and view the old skiway landscape without venturing onto the crevassed glacier.

title: Enter Base W's time capsule on Detaille Island
description: When ice, weather and prior permission align on a far-south voyage, land on slippery rock and enter the shuttered 1950s base in a closely supervised group, leaving every artefact untouched.

title: Join a permitted visit to Scott's Terra Nova hut
place: Scott's Terra Nova hut at Cape Evans
description: If the expedition's permits, sea ice and weather align, a trained guide may lead small groups through Scott's 1911 base and its artefact landscape. Hut entry needs a key and is never guaranteed; the nearby Magnetic Hut is closed.

title: Seek a landing beside Antarctica's first expedition huts
description: A rare small-boat landing may reach the 1899 Southern Cross base on Ridley Beach, where the first buildings erected on the continent stand among historic stores. Permit, guide and key are required, while nesting penguins and fast-changing ice can restrict or cancel access.

title: Walk the sea ice toward Snow Hill's emperor colony
description: Join a specialist ship-and-helicopter attempt to reach the emperor penguin colony, then walk across sea ice from a landing point kept safely away from the birds. Sea-ice thickness, weather and wildlife welfare decide whether the colony can be reached.

title: Trace Paulet Island's guided hut-and-volcano route
description: If ice, tide and nesting Adélies allow a landing, walk in a tightly managed small group toward the 1903 stone hut and volcanic lake. There is no free roaming: changing colony distribution can shorten the route or turn the visit into a small-boat viewing instead.

title: Climb Devil Island's flagged south-peak trail
description: From a conditions-dependent small-boat landing, follow the single flagged track above Devil Island's twin volcanic cones to a Weddell Sea viewpoint. The steep ridge, shifting pack ice, reefs and penguin traffic require close expedition-guide control and can make the longer walk unavailable.

title: Read living trees at the Omiya Bonsai Art Museum
description: Study seasonal display trees and the craft vocabulary behind them at a specialist museum in Omiya, a low-key stop beyond central Tokyo.

title: Climb Ikaho's stone steps between hot-spring inns
description: Follow the old stone stairway through a compact mountain onsen town and soak only after checking the current bath rules.

title: Ride the little railway into Kurobe Gorge
description: Take the narrow-gauge train past wooded ravines and river bridges on a mountain detour well beyond Japan's standard Golden Route.

title: Walk the mossy approach to Heisenji Hakusan Shrine
description: Cross a carpet of moss beneath cedars at an overlooked Fukui shrine complex on the historic approach to sacred Mount Hakusan.

title: Climb the steep keep at Maruoka Castle
description: Use the rope-assisted wooden stairs inside a small surviving hilltop keep in often-overlooked Fukui Prefecture.

title: Hike Mount Daisen instead of joining the Fuji crowd
description: Climb western Honshu's snow-capped volcanic landmark for broad views on a demanding alternative promoted beyond the usual Fuji circuit.

title: Ski the quieter powder runs at Appi Kogen
description: Choose more than five kilometres of northern Honshu ski trails as a lower-profile alternative to Hakuba and Niseko.

title: Meet pearl culture and ama divers on Mikimoto Island
description: Visit the island museum associated with the first cultured pearls and watch a demonstration of the region's ama diving tradition.

title: Float beside Okhotsk drift ice in a drysuit
description: Join a specialist guided drysuit outing at Abashiri and move carefully among winter sea ice, subject to daily conditions.

title: Cruise Kawasaki's illuminated factory canals
description: See working industrial plants reflected in the canals on a small night boat, a specialist urban tour away from Tokyo's landmark circuit.

title: Walk a section of the Ontake Kodo pilgrimage road
description: Trace an old mountain pilgrimage highway past shrines and forested approaches, choosing a legal open section for current conditions.

title: Ferry into the hidden-Christian history of the Goto Islands
description: Link small island churches and coastal settlements by ferry while respecting worship spaces and the archipelago's layered hidden-Christian history.

title: Trek and paddle through Iriomote's subtropical wilds
description: Use a local guide to combine mangrove paddling with a forest walk on a rugged island whose wildlife and waterways demand low-impact travel.

title: Hike and kayak around remote Okushiri Island
description: Pair a coastal hike with a weather-dependent paddle on a small island off southwest Hokkaido reached by ferry or limited flights.

title: Make washi by hand in Minobu
description: Learn the sequence of fibre, water and screen in a small-town papermaking session highlighted among Japan's local treasures.

title: Forge a kitchen knife with a Kochi craftsperson
description: Book a supervised workshop with a regional bladesmith to shape a practical keepsake while learning why Tosa forged tools endure.

title: Watch cormorant fishing from the Nagara River
description: Board an evening riverboat to observe trained cormorants and torch-lit fishing, a seasonal regional tradition outside the major-city circuit.

title: Step inside a clan courtyard in the Fujian tulou
description: Explore selected circular and square earthen clan houses among tea and rice fields, using authorised visitor routes and respecting lived-in spaces.

title: Walk among Jingmai Mountain's old tea forests
description: Move between Blang and Dai villages and old understorey tea groves in a living cultural landscape managed through community traditions.

title: Cycle between Kaiping's village watchtowers
description: Link fortified multi-storey diaolou and farming villages on quiet local roads, stopping only where current access is permitted.

title: Boat beneath the Zuojiang Huashan cliff paintings
description: View ancient red figures high on limestone cliffs from an authorised river boat without approaching or touching the fragile art.

title: Climb through Hailongtun's mountain fortress ruins
description: Follow steep stone gates across an archaeological tusi stronghold above Zunyi, one component of a dispersed World Heritage property.

title: Trace Quanzhou's overlooked maritime shrines and docks
description: Walk a selective route between religious, commercial and port remains that document Quanzhou's Song-Yuan trading world.

title: Camp between Badain Jaran's tall dunes and lakes
description: Enter with an experienced local desert operator to reach interdune lakes and immense sand towers; routes and conditions require advance checking.

title: Sketch the lanes and courtyards of Xidi Village
