description: Study lanes, ancestral halls and merchant houses in Xidi, the quieter companion village within the same inscription as already-busy Hongcun.

title: Paddle through Hanxiang's bridge-lined waterways
description: Pair kayaking or paddleboarding with a walk among traditional-style bridges, pavilions and old trees in a tucked-away suburban water garden.

title: Read a vanished lake ecosystem at Chengjiang
description: Use the site museum and permitted interpretation areas to understand an exceptional early-Cambrian fossil assemblage without collecting material.

title: Walk the first coastal stage of the Haeparang Trail
description: Follow 16.9 kilometres of coast from Oryukdo toward Haeundae, treating the route itself—not its famous endpoint—as the adventure.

title: Follow Sokcho's Sea Scent section of the Dulle Trail
description: Link coastal rock viewpoints and Oeongchi Port on a waymarked section of Korea's immense perimeter trail.

title: Search out the quiet corners of Haenam's Usuyeong coast
description: Explore the secluded southwest edge around Usuyeong, where mountain gardens and island-facing coast sit far from Korea's standard city circuit.

title: Eat and walk through Huinnyeoul's hillside alleys
description: Trace 14 regenerated lanes above the sea, then continue to the coastal tunnel and small haenyeo exhibition rather than stopping at a photo wall.

title: Climb to Ttangkkeut at Korea's southwest edge
description: Walk the headland at the village whose name means 'end of the land', an intentionally secluded stop at the far end of Haenam.

title: Walk the wave-cut coast of Heping Island
description: Follow managed paths across weathered coastal rock and harbour views on a compact Keelung detour outside Taipei's headline sights.

title: Pair Daxi Old Street with its riverside history
description: Look beyond the snack stalls to carved shopfronts and river-trade history in a smaller northern town promoted beside better-known Taipei stops.

title: Cycle the shore roads beside Shimen Reservoir
description: Ride a selected open section beside the reservoir and forested hills, checking construction and water-management restrictions before departure.

title: Hike beneath giant trees at Sun Link Sea
description: Walk cool forest paths and waterfall routes in a Nantou recreation area overshadowed by the county's Sun Moon Lake circuit.

title: Meet Taiwanese glove puppetry in Yunlin
description: Seek out a local performance or museum display in the county identified by Taiwan Tourism as the birthplace of its celebrated puppetry tradition.

description: The Neolithic chamber aligns with the rising sun near the equinoxes, with a medieval chapel above. The site also interprets forced labour from the occupation.

title: Time a low-tide walk toward La Corbière Lighthouse
description: The causeway disappears quickly under Jersey's large tidal range. Read the warning signals and turn back with ample time rather than following other walkers blindly.

title: Watch conservation work in action at Jersey Zoo
description: The Durrell site focuses on threatened species and the methods used to recover them. Allow time for keeper talks rather than treating it as a quick animal checklist.

title: Walk the headlands of Jersey National Park
description: The protected landscape is spread around the coast rather than behind one entrance gate. Pick a signed section to match weather, bus access and available daylight.

title: Watch sunset from the ruins of Grosnez Castle
description: The roofless headland fortress offers open Atlantic views with little shelter. Bring layers and keep well back from cliff edges in strong wind.

title: Walk the moonlike seabed to Seymour Tower with a guide
description: The tower stands nearly two kilometres offshore inside a fast-flooding intertidal zone. The tourism authority says to attempt the crossing only with a registered guide.

title: Enter the restored command bunker at Battery Moltke
description: Volunteer open days reveal the multi-level fire-control bunker behind the former coastal battery. Dates are limited, so plan around the published opening programme.

title: Climb the spiral stairs of the Great Laxey Wheel
description: The 22-metre Victorian waterwheel still turns above the former mine. Continue beyond the wheel along the mine trail to understand what its pumping power served.

title: Ride the mountain railway from Laxey to Snaefell
description: The electric railway climbs about 600 metres from Laxey to the island summit. Cloud can erase the celebrated views, so check conditions before boarding.

title: Walk the curtain walls of Peel Castle
description: The fortress occupies St Patrick's Isle beside Peel harbour and layers Viking and later Manx history. The exposed walls can be windy even when the town is calm.

title: Step through the rooms of Castle Rushen
description: The compact medieval castle preserves chambers, stairs and defensive works in the old capital. Seasonal opening means winter visitors should verify access first.

title: Take the steam railway from Douglas to Port Erin
description: The heritage line links the capital with the island's south using original-style steam operations. Check the seasonal timetable before building connections around it.

title: Walk a stage of the Raad ny Foillan coastal path
description: The complete Way of the Gull circles the island for roughly 160 kilometres. Choose a single stage around transport and tide rather than assuming every section is an easy coast stroll.

title: Boat to the seabird colonies of the Calf of Man
description: Small boats leave Port St Mary or Port Erin for the offshore bird observatory. Every sailing depends on tide, weather and boatman availability and must be booked ahead.

title: Watch the TT racers from an official viewing point
place: Isle of Man TT Mountain Course
description: Road closures divide the island and can leave spectators in place for hours. Use an official viewing area and plan food, shelter and the return journey before racing starts.

title: Descend through Dhoon Glen to its hidden cove
description: The short circuit passes a two-drop waterfall before reaching a secluded pebble cove. Steep inclines, wet paving and rugged paths make it more serious than the distance suggests.

title: Read the miners' story at Snaefell's washing floors
description: Free interpretation boards explain how women, children and men separated ore from waste on the 1848 floors. It is an easy add-on below the better-known Great Wheel.

title: Watch Raggiana birds-of-paradise at Varirata
description: Follow the signed forest tracks with a birding guide for a chance to see Raggiana birds-of-paradise, then pause at lookouts over the Sogeri escarpment. Confirm park and guide arrangements before leaving Port Moresby.

title: Surf the off-grid breaks near Namatanai
description: Base at a specialist coastal retreat to reach uncrowded surf around Namatanai. Travel with local arrangements and check swell, transport and current conditions before committing to this remote coast.

title: Meet makers at a POM City Market
description: Browse a scheduled city market for locally made Papua New Guinean craft and talk with the artisans behind it. Check the current monthly venue and use trusted transport.

title: Dive the quiet reefs of Natewa Bay
description: Travel beyond Savusavu for a small-scale dive or snorkel in the shallow reefs of the South Pacific's largest bay. Book a qualified local operator and confirm weather and reef conditions.

title: Walk into the Nausori Highlands
description: Leave Nadi's beach corridor for a guided walk among volcanic peaks, valleys and small highland villages. Arrange access through a recognised tour and follow village protocol.

title: Beachcomb with local life at Nasilai
description: Spend a quiet coastal pause near Nausori watching fishing and everyday village life rather than resort activity. Ask locally about access and conditions before settling in.

title: Walk among aircraft at Vilu War Museum
description: Visit the open-air collection of American and Japanese aircraft and artillery left from the Guadalcanal campaign. Confirm opening and transport with Tourism Solomons before the drive from Honiara.

title: Trek inland to Mataniko Cascade
description: Take a locally guided inland trek from the Honiara area to the Mataniko cascade. River and trail conditions change quickly, so arrange the outing through a trusted guide rather than attempting it independently.

title: Follow the cascades to Losinwei Waterfall
description: Take a locally guided riverside walk beneath coastal jungle to limestone swimming holes, hidden crevices and Losinwei Waterfall. The route includes rock pools and a steep rock face, so confirm conditions and arrange the guide before travelling to Malekula.

title: Climb Nguna's extinct Mount Taputoara
description: Walk with a community guide through villages and gardens to the rim of Nguna's extinct volcano. The sustained climb ends with views across the Shepherd Islands and the Nguna-Pele marine area.

title: Read penal and Kanak history at Fort Teremba
description: Walk the restored fort and museum to confront New Caledonia's penal-colony history and the Kanak revolts. Check current opening arrangements before detouring to Moindou.

title: Ride the dry-forest trails of Domaine de Deva
description: Explore marked routes on foot or mountain bike from dry forest and mangrove to ridgelines above the Bourail lagoon. Choose a route for your ability and check trail conditions locally.

title: Climb Mount Teurafaatiu above Maupiti lagoon
description: Climb from the small guesthouse island of Maupiti to a summit view over its lagoon, reef and neighbouring islands. Ask your host about the route and conditions before setting out.

title: Explore Ana A'eo cave with a local host
description: Enter Rurutu's limestone Ana A'eo cave to see openings that illuminate its stalagmites and stalactites. Arrange the visit with a local host and respect the cave's former religious significance.

title: Cycle Tikehau's few quiet roads
description: Borrow or hire a bicycle to explore the short roads around Tikehau's main village at an atoll pace. Ask your guesthouse about access, heat and any lagoon transfer needed.

title: Hike the forest track to Lake Lanoto'o
description: Follow a rough highland approach and rainforest trail to Samoa's Ramsar-listed volcanic crater lake. Arrange suitable transport to the trailhead and expect mud after rain.

title: Detour inland to Sauniatu Waterfall
description: Seek local directions and permission for this inland waterfall near Falefa, explicitly identified by Samoa Tourism as a hidden gem. Check current access and conditions locally, and never assume that swimming is safe.

title: Walk with a botanist through 'Ene'io Garden
description: Book a guided walk through Tonga's specialist collection of native, medicinal and introduced plants, built over decades by a local agronomist. Confirm tour days directly before travelling from Neiafu.

title: Descend between cliffs to Fangatave Beach
description: Reach a remote 'Eua beach enclosed by tall limestone cliffs on a guided land adventure. Confirm the route, land access and weather with a local guide before attempting the descent.

title: Wander the lily ponds at Maire Nui Gardens
description: Slow down among seven acres of tropical planting, lily ponds and mountain views at a family-established organic garden. Check current garden and cafe hours before visiting.

title: Look for kakerori in Takitumu forest
description: Join a very small guided walk through protected inland forest to learn about the endemic kakerori and its recovery. Book ahead because published tours run only on selected days with limited group size.

title: Cycle the Vinivini Track through Huvalu
description: Walk or ride a long bush track through mature forest and managed land in the Huvalu conservation area. Collect the current island guide and check track conditions at the visitor centre first.

title: Descend to Down Rope's Polynesian petroglyphs
description: Descend with a local guide beneath a roughly 700-foot cliff to Pitcairn's sandy beach and ancient Polynesian petroglyphs. The official tourism office calls the route difficult and potentially dangerous, so never attempt it independently and confirm weather access.

title: Follow the forest tracks through One Hundred Acres
description: Walk through a public reserve of rainforest, grass clearings and clifftop outlooks while watching for island birdlife. Check signs and current track conditions on arrival.

title: Ask permission to walk to Sipyen Waterfall
description: With the nearby landowner's permission, follow the short creek-side path to a small cascade and bathing pool in Utwe. Rocks can be slippery, so move carefully and leave the site as found.

title: Learn navigation and weaving at Alele Museum
description: Visit Majuro's cultural museum to connect traditional navigation, weaving and island history before travelling farther through the atolls. Confirm opening times locally.

title: Stay with an I-Kiribati community host
description: Arrange a community homestay to learn everyday skills and customs directly with an I-Kiribati family. Book through current tourism contacts, agree expectations in advance and ask before photographing people or places.

title: Join Funafuti's late-afternoon runway games
description: After the runway has been cleared for community use, join local games or walk the strip in the late afternoon. Enter only when locals do, obey every airport instruction and leave immediately whenever the runway returns to aviation use.

title: Step inside the small Naoero Museum
description: Visit Nauru's compact national museum for an indoor counterpoint to the island's mining, lagoon and wartime landscapes. The government page lists limited weekday hours and free entry, but confirm both before setting out.

title: Hike to Ngardmau Waterfall
description: Head inland on Babeldaob for a forest walk to Ngardmau Waterfall, a counterpoint to Palau's famous dive circuit. Confirm local access, fees and trail conditions before setting out.

title: See discarded glass remade at Belau Eco Glass
description: Visit the small recycling workshop where waste glass becomes usable objects and ornaments. Check whether demonstrations or retail access are available before visiting the waste-management complex.

title: Hike down to Pågat's freshwater cave pool
description: Descend a jungle trail to a dark freshwater cave pool, then continue toward the coastal point if conditions allow. Take a knowledgeable guide, carry lights and avoid the route after heavy rain.

title: Walk the Spanish-era lanes of historic Inalåhan
description: Explore the old village on foot for a quieter view of Guam's Spanish-period streets and registered historic sites, then stop at the coastal pools only if sea conditions are safe.

title: Walk to the star mound on Lower Sauma Ridge
description: Take the short interpretive trail to ancient grinding stones and views across the northeast coast and Vai'ava Strait. Go in the cooler morning and remain on the marked route.

title: Trace Wallis's American wartime trail
description: Look for surviving bunkers and buildings from the roughly 6,000 US troops once based on Wallis, ideally with the Uvea Museum Association. Most sites are described as accessible, but arrange guidance and confirm present access locally.

title: Arrange a village-hosted stay on Nukunonu
description: With advance village approval, stay in the small government hotel or privately arranged accommodation and experience an atoll with no established tourist industry. Sea transport and permits must be confirmed well ahead and can change.

title: Scan the forest canopy at Chenchun sanctuary
description: Use the overlook above an undisturbed limestone forest to watch seabirds roost and nest along Rota's rugged southeast coast. Keep noise low and follow sanctuary restrictions.

title: Walk Childers Cove at low tide
description: Limestone stacks rise behind a small white-sand cove west of the busier Twelve Apostles. Time the visit for low tide and treat the exposed coast cautiously.

title: Camp beside the Pink Lakes in Murray-Sunset
description: The remote salt lakes shift between pink and white with water, cloud and salinity. Stay overnight for the dark sky and carry supplies for an isolated national park.

title: Swim the Motueka Saltwater Baths at high tide
description: The 1930 tidal pool feels most complete around high tide and is quietest early or near sunset. Check water quality and tide before relying on a swim.

title: Walk beneath the Ōpārara limestone arches
description: Rainforest tracks lead to tannin-coloured water and vast limestone spans north of Karamea. Road and track conditions should be checked after heavy rain.

title: Follow the streambed into Putangirua Pinnacles
description: The easy lower route reaches the base of the eroded pillars, while a longer continuation climbs to a lookout. Flash flooding can make the streambed unsafe.

title: Take the forest track to Marokopa Falls
description: The short track reaches a broad waterfall a few kilometres beyond Waitomo's commercial caves. Spray and rain make the viewing approach slippery.

title: Book an open day among Gibbs Farm's giant sculptures
description: The private sculpture landscape opens only on selected pre-booked dates. Reserve well ahead and expect long outdoor walking between large-scale works.

title: Cycle the remote Pakihi section of the Motu Trails
description: The narrow backcountry section descends through forest far from road support. Use an appropriate bike, carry repair gear and arrange transport around the one-way ride.

title: Ride the Old Ghost Road through abandoned gold country
description: The remote Great Ride links old mining routes across exposed tops and dense forest. Hut bookings, weather margins and self-sufficient repair skills are essential.

title: Ride the mineral belt of the Coppermine Trail
description: The loop climbs from Nelson into exposed mineral country before a technical descent. Weather changes quickly above the bush line and the full circuit requires solid fitness.

title: Cycle the suspension bridges of the Timber Trail
description: The forest ride combines old tramways with long suspension bridges through Pureora. Arrange shuttles and accommodation because trail ends are far apart.

title: Trace the hillside rock carvings at Unakoti
description: Follow the forested hillside past Shaivite reliefs cut between the seventh and ninth centuries. Allow time for the stairs and smaller carvings beyond the main faces.

title: Watch masks take shape at Samaguri Satra
description: See monks and artisans build expressive performance masks from bamboo, clay and cloth in a satra that has carried the craft since the seventeenth century.

title: Hear prayer and Sattriya traditions at Auniati Satra
description: Enter a living Vaishnavite community where prayer, song, dance and theatre continue around the central namghar. Dress modestly and ask before photographing residents.

title: Read Dholavira through its ancient waterworks
description: Walk the Harappan city's reservoirs, drains and fortified sectors to see how an arid settlement managed water. Carry sun protection and confirm current site hours.

title: Learn Rogan painting from Nirona artisans
description: Visit a village workshop where a small artisan lineage draws castor-oil pigment onto fabric with a metal stylus. Arrange the demonstration directly and buy only if the work suits you.

title: Walk the Betwa beside Orchha's royal chhatris
description: Follow the river edge beneath a line of Bundela cenotaphs, including the unusually palace-like memorial to Bir Singh Deo. Visit in softer morning or late-afternoon light.

title: Find Orchha's Sawan Bhado cooling pillars
description: Look for the carved sandstone pillars associated with channels that created a cooling effect during the monsoon months. They reward a close detour within the larger fort complex.

title: Explore the rock-cut monastic rooms of Dhamnar
description: Move through a little-visited hill ensemble of 51 rock-cut caves, with monastic rooms, halls and stupas alongside the Dharmarajeshwara temple complex.

title: Walk the courtyard mansions of Kanadukathan
description: Read global trading histories in the tiled courtyards and long axes of Chettiar houses. Arrange access respectfully because many buildings remain private or have limited entry.

title: Cycle Bishnupur's terracotta temple circuit
description: Link the brick and laterite temples by bicycle, pausing at the double-roofed Jor Bangla and the gallery-ringed Rasmancha to compare distinct local forms.

title: Descend the shrine-lined Surya Kund at Modhera
description: Study the geometric steps and 108 small shrines of the temple tank before entering the carved assembly hall. Early light reveals the stonework without the midday heat.

title: Trek into Khaptad's high grasslands and lakes
description: Reach a remote plateau of forest, grassland and small lakes by a long overland approach and a final walk. Camp self-sufficiently and confirm permits and local conditions.

title: Bird the river grasslands of Koshi Tappu
description: Scan wetlands and riverine grasslands for wild water buffalo and migratory birds from a quieter Terai reserve reached via Biratnagar.

title: Walk Tansen's Newari lanes to Srinagar Hill
place: Tansen old town and Srinagar Hill
description: Climb from Tansen Bazaar past Newari houses and brass and Dhaka-cloth shops to the broad Himalayan views from Srinagar Hill.

title: Walk the Tinjure rhododendron ridge
description: Follow a high ridge through rhododendron forest toward Gupha Pokhari, with views toward Kanchenjunga and Makalu. Arrange local guidance for the longer remote sections.

title: Trek between the highland villages of Merak and Sakteng
description: Spend seven days crossing eastern highlands between distinctive pastoral communities, reaching roughly 4,100 metres. Book through a licensed Bhutanese provider.

title: Walk the low-altitude Nabji Korphu circuit
description: Take a six-day village and forest route at lower elevations than Bhutan's famous alpine treks. Confirm the seasonal itinerary with a licensed provider.

title: Cross the Far-Out East Bhutan trail
description: Follow a six-day eastern route through forest and isolated settlements, topping out near 3,000 metres. This is a specialist itinerary requiring licensed local arrangements.

title: Link the Buddhist mounds of Lalmai-Mainamati
description: Explore an elongated hill ridge holding temple and vihara remains from sites such as Kutila Mura, Ananda Vihara and Itakhola Mura.

title: Walk Mahasthan from citadel to Karatoya River
description: Read more than two millennia of settlement and living pilgrimage across the citadel, surrounding mounds and the seasonally active Karatoya channel.

title: Read terracotta stories at Kantanagar Temple
description: Circle the brick temple slowly to follow dense terracotta panels across its walls. Treat it as an active religious place and check local visiting arrangements.

title: Walk Ritigala's forest monastery paths
description: Climb stone-paved paths past bridges, bathing structures and austere meditation buildings in a forest-clad monastic landscape.

title: Take the ferry and tractor road around Delft Island
description: Cross from Kurikattuwan, then link coral-stone walls, fort ruins, baobab and pony country by the island's limited transport. Confirm ferry times before departure.

title: Pause at the hybrid stone shrine of Nalanda Gedige
description: Examine a compact all-stone shrine where Buddhist elements meet South Indian Hindu architectural forms, set away from the larger cultural-triangle monuments.

title: Circle the stone columns of Medirigiriya Vatadage
description: Climb the low rock to an elegant circular relic house whose concentric stone columns stand apart from Polonnaruwa's busier core.

title: Ferry to Nainativu's two pilgrimage traditions
description: Cross by short passenger ferry and walk between Nagadeepa Buddhist temple and Nagapooshani Amman Kovil, respecting dress and photography rules at both.

title: Canoe the red mangroves of Addu Nature Park
description: Paddle the sheltered Bedhi bay beside red mangroves, then use the wetland piers or cycling paths around Eydhigali Kilhi and Koattey.

title: Study the blue-tiled tombs of Uch Sharif
description: Walk among fourteenth- and fifteenth-century Sufi tombs decorated with moulded brick, carved timber and blue-and-white tilework. Reconsider travel and verify local security before any visit.

title: Trace Taxila's first street plan at Bhir Mound
description: Follow the irregular lanes among exposed houses at Taxila's earliest city, contrasting their organic plan with later Sirkap. Reconsider travel and confirm site access and local security conditions.

title: Enter Rohtas Fort through its quieter gates
place: Rohtas Fort outer gates and village
description: Explore the less-visited gates and surviving village within Sher Shah Suri's vast defensive circuit rather than stopping only at the main approach. Reconsider travel and verify conditions.

title: Walk the coloured badlands of Aktau and Katutau
description: Travel beyond the Singing Dune into Altyn-Emel's pale Aktau sediments and dark volcanic Katutau forms. Register the route with the park and carry desert supplies.

title: Read Bronze Age scenes at Tanbaly Reserve-Museum
description: Follow the reserve trail through a landscape holding roughly 5,000 rock carvings from the Bronze Age and later periods.

title: Descend toward Aksu Canyon with reserve permission
description: Enter only the visitor-open portion of Aksu-Zhabagly after reserve approval, then tackle the steep canyon approach with a locally authorised guide.

title: Meet potters at the Rishtan Craftsmen's Center
description: Visit workshops using the local red clay and distinctive blue-green glaze, with the master-apprentice tradition interpreted by working potters.

title: Walk the hilltop necropolis of Mizdakhan
description: Explore mausoleums, mounds and the remains of Giaur-Kala across a vast cemetery landscape outside Nukus. Respect active graves and pilgrimage practices.

title: Trace the petroglyphs through Sarmyshsay Gorge
description: Walk among thousands of carvings showing people, hunting scenes and now-vanished fauna. Use the managed route and never touch or chalk the rock art.

title: Find rescued avant-garde art at the Savitsky Museum
description: Spend an afternoon with Russian and Central Asian avant-garde works far from the standard Silk Road circuit. Check which galleries are open before travelling.

title: Read the coloured strata of Yangykala
description: Travel with pre-arranged permission and transport to layered red, white and ochre escarpments in the Balkan interior. Keep well back from the unprotected cliff edges.

title: Walk from Nohur village toward Khur-Khuri waterfall
description: Arrange a permitted local visit to the stone-built mountain village and its orchard landscape, adding a guided walk toward Khur-Khuri waterfall if conditions allow.

title: Walk the nut-fruit forests around Sary-Chelek
description: Follow a reserve-approved trail from walnut, apple and pear forest toward the high-basin lake. Use local guidance and respect the biosphere reserve's access controls.

title: Trek to the high petroglyph fields of Saimaluu-Tash
description: Reach a high Ferghana Range sanctuary containing thousands of engraved stones spanning the Bronze Age to medieval times. Go with specialist local support and leave every surface untouched.

title: Ride from Kochkor toward remote Kol-Ukok
description: Join a small guided horseback route into high pastures and camp near Kol-Ukok, using a named local operator able to manage horses and remote logistics.

title: Visit the springs and shrine of Chiluchor Chashma
description: Walk around a cluster of freshwater springs and the adjoining pilgrimage landscape in the Beshkent Valley. Treat healing claims as tradition, not medical advice.

title: Pair Hulbuk Fortress with its archaeology museum
description: Stop between Danghara and Kulob to compare the reconstructed fortress with carved plaster, pottery, coins and other finds in the museum opposite.

title: Hear plantation family histories at Museum Bakkie
description: Arrange a bus-and-boat journey to this small museum on the former Reynsdorp plantation. A personal tour connects original maps, objects and family histories, followed by a garden walk on the organised day trip. Reserve transport, guiding and lunch ahead; confirm the current route and accessibility.

title: Enter the Necropolis of the Via Triumphalis
description: Take the official guided route through a terraced Roman cemetery, with tomb inscriptions recalling people beyond the imperial elite. Book the chosen tour through the Vatican Museums and confirm its entrance, fee and current dates; the standalone route uses Porta di Santa Rosa.

title: Visit the Teutonic Cemetery in its morning access window
description: Ask the Swiss Guard for access to the small historic cemetery during its stated morning window. Wednesday entry may be unavailable when a papal audience is held.

title: Send a postcard through Vatican Post
description: Write a memory of your visit and send it through the Vatican postal service near Bernini's colonnade. Allow for postcard and postage costs, and check current counter hours before relying on a particular branch.

title: Graze your way through Adelaide Central Market
description: Open Tuesday to Saturday. One of the largest undercover produce markets in the Southern Hemisphere - cheese, smallgoods, doughnuts and a coffee crawl in one building.

title: Find the Mall's Balls and the bronze pigs on Rundle Mall
description: Adelaide's pedestrian shopping street, worth it for the buskers and the four bronze pigs rummaging in a bin.

title: Walk the Bicentennial Conservatory at Adelaide Botanic Garden
description: Free 51-hectare garden in the middle of the city, with a giant glasshouse of lowland rainforest and the Museum of Economic Botany.

title: Spend a rainy afternoon in the Art Gallery of South Australia
description: Free entry to a serious collection of Australian, Aboriginal and European art on North Terrace.

title: See the Australian Aboriginal Cultures Gallery at the SA Museum
description: Home to the world's most comprehensive collection of Australian Aboriginal cultural material, plus the opal and megafauna halls.

title: Climb the Adelaide Oval roof at sunset
description: A harnessed walk along the stadium roofline, 50m above the pitch, with the city and the Adelaide Hills laid out around you.

title: Visit the giant pandas at Adelaide Zoo
description: Australia's second-oldest zoo and the only one in the country to host giant pandas.

title: Ride the tram to Glenelg for fish and chips on the jetty
description: The historic tram runs from the city centre straight to Jetty Road and a wide swimming beach - the classic Adelaide afternoon.

title: Watch the sun drop into the sea at Henley Beach Square
description: West-facing beach where the whole square turns out for sunset - grab a table and watch it go down over the Gulf.

title: Ride the Semaphore miniature steam railway
description: An old-fashioned seaside strip with a working miniature railway along the foreshore and a long, calm swimming beach.

title: Spot dolphins on a Port River cruise
description: A resident population of bottlenose dolphins lives in the Port River, alongside the ship graveyard and the old maritime warehouses.

title: Climb inside a Bluebird railcar at the National Railway Museum
description: The largest railway museum in Australia, in Port Adelaide - huge steam locomotives you can walk through.

title: Hike to all three waterfalls in Morialta
description: The falls only run after winter rain. A steep gorge 20 minutes from the CBD with three waterfalls and a good chance of koalas in the gums.

title: Hold a koala at Cleland Wildlife Park
description: One of the few places in Australia where you can legally hold a koala, plus walk-through kangaroo and emu enclosures.

title: See all of Adelaide from the Mount Lofty Summit
description: 727m lookout taking in the entire city, the Gulf and the Hills - best an hour before sunset.

title: Eat pork knuckle in Hahndorf, Australia's oldest German town
description: Settled by Prussian Lutherans in 1839 - a main street of German bakeries, beer halls and the Hahndorf Academy.

title: See the autumn colour in Stirling
description: A Hills village planted with European deciduous trees - in April and May the whole main street turns red and gold.

title: Drive your car onto the sand at Aldinga Beach
description: One of the few beaches in SA where you can legally drive onto the sand and park facing the water.

title: Photograph the old jetty ruins at Port Willunga
description: Weathered jetty pylons standing in the shallows below limestone cliffs and the cave-cut boat sheds - the best sunset on the Fleurieu.

title: Do a Shiraz tasting flight in McLaren Vale
description: Old-vine Shiraz and Grenache country 45 minutes from Adelaide, with cellar doors between the vines and the sea.

title: Get lost in the Alternate Realities Museum at the d'Arenberg Cube
description: A five-storey Rubik's-cube building dropped into a McLaren Vale vineyard, part cellar door, part surrealist art museum.

title: Walk beneath the red cliffs at Maslin Beach
description: Dramatic banded ochre cliffs above a long beach - Australia's first legal nude beach occupies the southern end.

title: Take the horse-drawn tram to Granite Island at Victor Harbor
description: A Clydesdale still pulls a double-decker tram across the causeway - the last horse-drawn tram of its kind in the world.

title: Walk the Kaiki Trail around Granite Island
description: A 1.5km loop over pink granite boulders with fur seals on the rocks and whales offshore in winter.

title: Watch southern right whales calving in Encounter Bay
description: Southern right whales come into the bay to calve every winter - the Bluff and Rosetta Head are the free viewing spots.

title: Hike down to Deep Creek Waterfall
description: The wildest corner of the Fleurieu - steep gullies down to hidden beaches, with a serious climb back out.

title: Catch the ferry from Cape Jervis to Kangaroo Island
description: The 45-minute crossing of Backstairs Passage - book the car on early, it fills up over summer.

title: Spend three days circling Kangaroo Island
description: Australia's third-largest island - sea lions, koalas, wild coastline and dark skies, an hour off the mainland.

title: Walk the beach among wild sea lions at Seal Bay
description: A guided walk onto the sand of a working Australian sea lion colony - one of the only places on earth you can do this.

title: Watch first light hit the Remarkable Rocks
description: Wind-carved granite boulders balanced on a dome 75m above the Southern Ocean, orange with lichen at sunrise.

title: Count the fur seals under Admirals Arch
description: A collapsed sea cave hung with stalactites at Cape du Couedic, with hundreds of long-nosed fur seals on the rocks below.

title: See the regrowth after the fires in Flinders Chase
description: The wild western end of Kangaroo Island - badly burnt in 2019-20 and now a remarkable study in how mallee country comes back.

title: Watch the evening pelican feed at Kingscote wharf
description: Kangaroo Island's main town, with a long-running pelican feed on the town jetty.

title: Swim off the jetty at Emu Bay
description: A 5km north-facing white sand beach with calm water - one of the few KI beaches you can drive onto.

title: Watch little penguins come ashore at Penneshaw
description: The ferry town, with a little penguin colony that comes up the rocks after dark.

title: Ride the shuttle past the lions at Monarto Safari Park
description: The largest open-range zoo outside Africa - 1,500 hectares of white rhino, giraffe, cheetah and lions an hour from Adelaide.

title: Taste 100-year-old vine Shiraz in the Barossa
description: Australia's most famous wine region, with some of the oldest continuously producing Shiraz vines on the planet.

title: Buy mettwurst from a Tanunda butcher
description: The most German of the Barossa towns - Lutheran churches, bakeries and butchers still making mettwurst the old way.

title: Stand in the original Grange cellar at Penfolds Magill Estate
description: The birthplace of Penfolds Grange, still a working vineyard inside Adelaide's suburbs - 20 minutes from the CBD.

title: Drink Riesling where it grows best in the Clare Valley
description: Two hours north of Adelaide and Australia's benchmark Riesling country, quieter and greener than the Barossa.

title: Cycle the Riesling Trail between cellar doors
description: 35km of old railway line converted to a flat gravel path, with cellar doors the whole way along it.

title: Buy the Burra Passport key and let yourself into the historic sites
description: A 19th-century copper town where a single key unlocks eight heritage sites, including the dugouts miners lived in on the creek bank.

title: Tour the Georgian rooms of Martindale Hall at Mintaro
description: An 1880 mansion used as the school in Picnic at Hanging Rock, in a slate-quarry village of about 80 people.

title: Stay a night in the Clare township
description: The valley's main town and the practical base for a weekend of Riesling and the Trail.

title: Follow the Copper Coast trail through Cornish mining country
description: Wallaroo, Moonta and Kadina - the Little Cornwall triangle, built on 19th-century copper and still holding the Kernewek Lowender festival.

title: Eat a Cornish pasty on the Wallaroo foreshore
description: A working grain port with a long jetty, a swimming beach and bakeries that still take the pasty seriously.

title: Ride the Moonta Mines tourist railway through the ruins
description: Once the richest copper mine in Australia - a small train runs through the ruins, tailings and Miners' Cottage.

title: Find the Ethel shipwreck on the beach at Innes National Park
description: The wild toe of Yorke Peninsula - surf breaks, the ghost town of Inneston and the rusted ribs of a wreck in the sand.

title: Watch the sun set over the Southern Ocean at Marion Bay
description: The last town before Innes, with a beach that faces straight into the Southern Ocean swell.

title: Drive the full loop of the Yorke Peninsula
description: A boot-shaped peninsula of crayfish, jetties and empty beaches that most interstate visitors drive straight past.

title: Shuck Coffin Bay oysters standing in the water they grew in
description: Wader-deep oyster tours where you stand at a table in the lease and eat them straight out of the bay.

title: Four-wheel-drive out to Point Sir Isaac
description: Soft-sand tracks out along a remote peninsula of dunes and emerald bays - genuine 4WD country, not a soft-roader run.

title: Cage-dive with great white sharks out of Port Lincoln
description: The only place in Australia licensed for great white cage diving, out at the Neptune Islands.

title: Swim with wild sea lions at Baird Bay
description: A tiny fishing settlement where one family-run operation takes you into the water with a wild sea lion colony that comes to play.

title: Drive the Seafood Frontier around the Eyre Peninsula
description: Oysters at Coffin Bay, tuna at Port Lincoln, whiting all the way up the west coast - Australia's best-value seafood drive.

title: Look down on whales from the cliffs at Head of Bight
description: Southern right whales calve directly below the Bunda Cliffs here - the best land-based whale watching in Australia.

title: Stand on the salt crust of Lake Gairdner
description: A 160km salt lake used for land speed record attempts - blinding white to the horizon and almost nobody there.

title: Sleep under the stars in the Flinders Ranges
description: 800-million-year-old ranges of red rock, river red gums and yellow-footed rock wallabies, five hours north of Adelaide.

title: Climb toward St Mary Peak on the rim of Wilpena Pound
description: A 21km circuit around a natural amphitheatre 17km long. Adnyamathanha Traditional Owners ask that walkers stop below the actual summit.

title: Go underground at Blinman, the highest town in South Australia
description: Population about 20, elevation 610m - a guided underground tour of a copper mine that closed in 1907.

title: Look through the telescopes at Arkaroola's observatories
description: A private wilderness sanctuary in the northern Flinders with three observatories and some of the darkest skies in Australia.

title: Eat feral food at the Prairie Hotel in Parachilna
description: A pub in a town of almost nobody, famous for a mixed grill of camel, kangaroo and emu.

title: Ride the Pichi Richi steam train out of Quorn
description: Original Ghan locomotives running the 1879 line through the Pichi Richi Pass, restored and operated by volunteers.

title: Ride the mountain bike trails at Melrose
description: The oldest town in the Flinders and now the state's mountain biking capital, with trails starting off the main street.

title: Walk the floor of Alligator Gorge
description: A narrow red quartzite gorge where the walls close in to a few metres apart - you walk along the creek bed between them.

title: See megafauna fossils at the Naracoorte Caves
description: South Australia's only World Heritage site - pitfall caves that trapped and preserved 500,000 years of Australian megafauna.

title: Walk the Obelisk track at Robe
description: A red-and-white striped obelisk on eroding limestone cliffs, above a town of crayfish boats and long beaches.

title: Float in the Pool of Siloam at Beachport
description: A saltwater lake around seven times saltier than the sea - you physically cannot sink in it.

title: See the Blue Lake turn cobalt at Mount Gambier
description: A crater lake that shifts from steel grey to brilliant cobalt every November and back again in March, for reasons still debated.

title: Canoe the Coorong lagoons
description: A 130km saltwater lagoon behind the Younghusband Peninsula dunes, Ngarrindjeri country and the setting for Storm Boy.

title: Take a paddle steamer out of Mannum
description: The birthplace of the Murray River paddle steamer trade, an hour from Adelaide, with houseboats and limestone cliffs.

title: Watch sunrise light hit Machu Picchu from the Sun Gate
description: Entry tickets sell out months ahead in high season, and only a few hundred Sun Gate arrivals catch the light before the cloud rolls in. Book the first entry slot if you want the postcard shot without the rope-line crowd.

title: Climb Huayna Picchu for the aerial view over Machu Picchu
description: Only 400 permits are issued per day, split into two entry times, and they attach to a specific Machu Picchu ticket booked weeks in advance. The final stretch is a near-vertical scramble on Inca-cut steps with a chain handrail.

title: Trek the classic four-day Inca Trail to Machu Picchu
description: The trail closes every February for maintenance and permits, 500 a day including guides and porters, sell out four to six months ahead in peak season. Dead Woman's Pass at 4,215m is the point most people question their choices.

title: Trace the zigzag stone walls of Sacsayhuaman above Cusco
description: Some of the fitted andesite blocks weigh over 100 tonnes and were cut with no mortar, gaps too tight for a blade. It's a 20-minute uphill walk from the Plaza de Armas, useful for acclimatising before the Inca Trail.

title: Watch evening light hit the cathedral from Cusco's Plaza de Armas
description: The cathedral was built directly over the demolished palace of Inca Wiracocha using stones looted from Sacsayhuaman. Inside, a Cusco-school painting reworks the Last Supper with a plate of roast guinea pig as the main course.

title: Climb the terraces of Ollantaytambo, a still-living Inca town
description: Unlike most Inca sites, Ollantaytambo's original street grid and water channels are still in daily use by the families living in them. The unfinished Temple of the Sun shows exactly how the enormous stone blocks were dragged and stacked.

title: Walk the Pisac ruins terraces and browse the Sunday market
description: The ruins above town see a fraction of Machu Picchu's crowds despite equally dramatic terracing and an intact Inca cemetery pocked with looted tombs. The market is best on Sunday, when villages from the surrounding valley bring produce and textiles down.

title: See Moray's farming terraces and the salt pans of Maras
description: Moray's terraced bowl creates a 15C temperature gradient between top and bottom, thought to be an Inca crop laboratory. Ten minutes away, over 3,000 salt pools fed by a subterranean spring have been worked by the same families since Inca times.

title: Hike to Rainbow Mountain before the afternoon cloud rolls in
description: The mineral stripes were only exposed by melting snow around 2015, and the trailhead sits at 4,600m before an already steep climb - altitude, not distance, is what wrecks people. Start at 3am with the first tour buses if you want the ridge to yourself.

title: Hike up to the turquoise water of Laguna Humantay
description: The glacial lake sits at 4,200m and its colour comes from suspended rock flour, brightest around midday sun. It's now a common detour on the Salkantay trek, but also works as a standalone day trip from Cusco.

title: Trek two days in to reach Choquequirao before the crowds do
description: Larger than Machu Picchu but reachable only by a two-day descent-and-climb trek, it gets a few dozen visitors a day instead of thousands. A cable car has been proposed for years but hasn't been built, so the walk is still the only way in.

title: Step onto a hand-built reed island on Lake Titicaca
description: The islands are woven from totora reed and re-layered every few weeks as the base rots from below, so walking on one feels like walking on a mattress. Go early, before the tour boats from Puno arrive in convoy.

title: Watch Taquile islanders knit their own social status into their hats
description: Men on Taquile knit, not weave, a skill passed down as a rite of passage, and the caps they wear signal marital status at a glance. There are no cars or hotels on the island, just a steep staircase up from the dock.

title: Spend the night with a host family on Amantani Island
description: Homestays are rotated between families by the community so tourism income is shared evenly. The climb to the twin hilltop temples of Pachatata and Pachamama for sunset over the lake is the reason to stay rather than day-trip.

title: See the Colla funeral towers of Sillustani at sunset
description: The tallest chullpa burial towers stand 12m high, built with a stonework precision the Inca later adopted, some predating Cusco's empire. Grave robbers left most of them cracked open, but the site on a peninsula over Lake Umayo is close to empty most afternoons.

title: Watch condors ride the thermals at Cruz del Condor
description: Andean condors use the canyon's morning thermals to launch, so arrive by 8am - by 10am most have soared off to feed. Colca is nearly twice the depth of the Grand Canyon, though the viewpoint doesn't advertise that.

title: Get lost in the painted streets of Santa Catalina Monastery
description: A walled citadel-within-a-city that housed cloistered nuns for over 400 years and wasn't opened to the public until 1970. The ochre, blue and terracotta streets inside are named after Spanish cities and were only ever meant to be seen by the sisters who lived there.

title: Summit the perfect cone of El Misti volcano overnight
description: The two-day climb tops out at 5,822m, and most operators push for the summit at 2am to catch sunrise and descend before the afternoon wind picks up. Acclimatise in Arequipa (2,335m) for at least two days first or the altitude will end the trip for you.

title: Trek down into Colca Canyon to the Sangalle oasis
description: The descent from Cabanaconde to the palm-fringed 'Oasis' at the canyon floor drops over 1,000m on a dusty switchback trail, and the climb back out the next morning is the part nobody mentions in advance. Bring more water than feels necessary.

title: Fly over the Nazca Lines to see the hummingbird and the monkey
description: The geoglyphs are only legible from the air, and the small planes bank hard and repeatedly so both sides get a view - motion sickness tablets are worth taking beforehand. Morning flights avoid the thermal turbulence that grounds afternoon slots.

title: Climb the roadside mirador for a free look at the Nazca Lines
description: The metal tower beside the Pan-American Highway shows only two figures, the hands and the tree, at an angle, nothing like the flight - but it costs a few soles instead of over a hundred dollars. A reasonable stop if a flight isn't in the budget.

title: Sandboard the dunes around the Huacachina oasis at golden hour
description: Dune buggies haul you to the top of dunes over 100m high for a stomach-drop descent before the sunset run, which is the timing worth booking for. The oasis lagoon itself has shrunk over the decades and is now partly topped up artificially.

title: Cruise past sea lions and penguins at the Ballestas Islands
description: Nicknamed the 'poor man's Galapagos', the boat doesn't land but gets close enough for Humboldt penguins, sea lion colonies and the occasional condor overhead. Boats leave early to beat the wind that picks up by mid-morning.

title: Taste pisco straight from the still at an Ica bodega
description: Ica is Peru's pisco heartland, and small family bodegas still press grapes the traditional way in stone troughs. Harvest and distillation run March to May, so that window is when the bodegas are actually working rather than just pouring for tours.

title: Find the ochre sand of Playa Roja in Paracas National Reserve
description: The reddish sand comes from eroded granite cliffs mixing with black volcanic rock, and it's a detour most Ballestas Islands day-trippers skip entirely. There's no shade and no facilities, so treat it as a lookout stop rather than a swim.

title: Descend into the bone-lined catacombs under San Francisco Church
description: An estimated 25,000 people are buried in the tunnels beneath the monastery, and some chambers arrange femurs and skulls into geometric patterns rather than piles. It was Lima's main cemetery until the early 1800s and stayed sealed and forgotten until 1943.

title: Eat ceviche for lunch in Miraflores, the way locals actually do
description: Ceviche is a lunch dish in Peru, not a dinner one - the fish is cut to order and most serious cevicherias close by 5pm. The leftover citrus-chilli marinade, leche de tigre, is often served as a shot before the plate arrives.

title: Cross the Bridge of Sighs in Barranco holding your breath
description: Local legend says if you cross while holding your breath your wish comes true - a short enough bridge that most people manage it. The surrounding streets carry some of Lima's best street art and turn into an open-air party most weekend nights.

title: Tour the adobe pyramid of Huaca Pucllana lit up after dark
description: A pre-Inca Lima-culture pyramid built from adobe bricks stacked on edge, like a bookshelf rather than flat, to survive earthquakes, standing in the middle of a modern Miraflores neighbourhood. The night tour lights the ramps and excavated tombs differently to the daytime visit.

title: Walk the pyramid complex of Pachacamac outside Lima
description: A pilgrimage site and oracle temple that predates the Inca by centuries and was still functioning when the Spanish arrived, who later built a convent on top of it. It's 40 minutes from Miraflores and gets a fraction of the visitors of sites in Cusco.

title: Walk the adobe walls of Chan Chan, the world's largest mud-brick city
description: The Chimu capital once housed an estimated 30,000 people across ten walled royal compounds, its walls carved with friezes of fish and pelicans repeated across entire courtyards. El Nino rains have eroded whole sections over the last century, so the restored Tschudi complex is the part still worth the entry fee.

title: Watch fishermen paddle centuries-old caballito reed boats at Huanchaco
description: Local fishermen still ride the same reed-boat design depicted on 3,000-year-old Moche pottery, straddling them like a horse (caballito) to paddle out past the break. The town also has a legitimate, mellow point break beginners can handle.

title: Spend a night in an Amazon jungle lodge reachable only by boat from Iquitos
description: Iquitos is the largest city in the world unreachable by road - everyone arrives by plane or boat. Lodges an hour or more downriver run night caiman-spotting trips and canopy walkways that day-trippers from the city dock never reach.

title: Spot pink river dolphins in the Pacaya-Samiria reserve
description: Peru's largest protected wetland is nicknamed the 'mirror of the jungle' for its flooded-forest reflections, and boat access changes completely between high water (roughly December to May) and low water months. A multi-day river trip is the only way in - there's no road or day-trip version.

title: Walk the floating stilt-house market of Belen
description: Known locally as the 'Venice of the Amazon', the neighbourhood floats or stands on stilts depending on the river level, and the market sells jungle produce found nowhere else, including bark, grubs and fruit with no English name. Go with a guide; it's a real neighbourhood, not a tourist set.

title: Hike to the glacial-blue water of Laguna 69
description: The trailhead alone sits at 3,850m and the lake at 4,600m, so the altitude gain hurts more than the 9km distance suggests. It's the single most-hiked trail out of Huaraz for a reason - meltwater off Nevado Chacraraju turns the lake an almost unreal blue.

title: Explore the underground galleries of Chavin de Huantar
description: This temple complex predates the Inca by over 2,000 years, and its stone tenon heads and underground acoustic passages were built to disorient pilgrims during hallucinogenic rituals. A network of stone ducts still channels water through the galleries the way it did 3,000 years ago.

title: Ride the cable car up to the fortress of Kuelap
description: Called the 'Machu Picchu of the north', this Chachapoya cloud-fortress predates the Inca and once held around 400 circular stone houses inside walls up to 19m tall. A cable car opened in 2017 cut what used to be a multi-hour climb down to 20 minutes.

title: Hike through cloud forest to the base of Gocta waterfall
description: At around 770m it's one of the tallest waterfalls in the world, yet it wasn't formally measured and mapped for outsiders until 2005 - locals had kept it quiet, believing a mermaid and a serpent guarded it. The hike in is humid and muddy regardless of season; proper boots matter more than timing.

title: Learn to surf the point break at Mancora
description: Mancora's wave is forgiving enough for first-timers, which is why the town doubles as Peru's party-beach destination, loudest December through February. For the serious break, surfers head an hour south to Cabo Blanco or Puerto Chicama instead.

title: See the untouched royal tomb of the Lord of Sipan
description: Discovered in 1987, this Moche tomb was the richest unlooted burial ever found in the Americas, and the museum reconstructs the burial chamber exactly as archaeologists found it, gold mask and all. It gets a fraction of Cusco's visitor numbers despite the find being compared to Tutankhamun's tomb.

title: Watch dozens of macaws feed at a Tambopata clay lick at dawn
description: Macaws and parrots gather at exposed riverbank clay to neutralise toxins in the seeds they eat, and dawn is the only reliable window before they scatter for the day. Reaching the reserve means a flight to Puerto Maldonado followed by hours upriver by boat.

title: Ride the cog train up to Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado
description: The 38m Art Deco statue took nine years to build and stands on a peak inside Tijuca National Park, the largest urban rainforest in the world. Clear-sky slots fill first online - go early morning before the cloud that regularly swallows the summit by midday.

title: Take the two-stage cable car up Sugarloaf Mountain for sunset
description: The original 1912 cable car system still runs, now updated to glass-sided cars that swap between two peaks. Sunset is the busiest slot for a reason: the whole bay, Christ the Redeemer and Copacabana line up in one 360-degree view.

title: Walk the wave-pattern promenade along Copacabana Beach at dawn
description: The black-and-white Portuguese stone mosaic underfoot was laid in 1970 and copies a Lisbon pavement pattern. Locals do their exercise laps before 7am, before the beach fills and the afternoon sun gets fierce.

title: Watch the sunset crowd applaud from Ipanema's Arpoador rocks
description: Arpoador, the rocky point between Ipanema and Copacabana, is the one spot in Rio where the sun sets directly into the ocean, and regulars genuinely clap when it drops below the horizon. The beach itself is informally zoned by numbered lifeguard posts, each with its own crowd.

title: Climb the mosaic-tiled Selaron Steps in Lapa
description: Chilean artist Jorge Selaron covered these 215 steps in tiles from over 60 countries, sent to him by visitors after his work gained a following, and kept adding to it until his death in 2013. It sits a block from Lapa's arches, best combined with an evening out in the neighbourhood's samba bars.

title: Hike through Tijuca National Park to the Pedra Bonita viewpoint
description: The forest covering Rio's hills is entirely replanted - it was cleared for coffee plantations in the 1800s and replanted by hand starting in 1861 to protect the city's water supply. Pedra Bonita is also the hang-gliding launch point, so expect company circling overhead.

title: Tour the Maracana, Brazil's cathedral of football
description: Built for the 1950 World Cup final, it once held an official crowd of nearly 200,000 - modern safety rules cap it at a still-enormous 78,000. Match-day tickets are far cheaper and easier to get than European football, so catch a Flamengo game if the calendar lines up.

title: Watch samba schools parade the Sambodromo at Carnival
description: Each samba school gets exactly 65 to 75 minutes to parade with up to 3,000 dancers and a purpose-built float, and judges dock points for going over. Grandstand tickets for the top two nights sell out by December; the practical alternative is watching a rehearsal parade earlier in the season.

title: Wander the car-free cobblestones of colonial Paraty
description: Portuguese gold-route traders built Paraty's streets to flood deliberately at high tide, flushing the sewage into the bay - they still do. The historic centre bans cars entirely, and cachaca distilleries around town offer tastings of the spirit Paraty has made since the 1600s.

title: Hike between hidden beaches on car-free Ilha Grande
description: No cars are allowed on the island, so every beach, including Lopes Mendes, regularly ranked among Brazil's best, is reached on foot or by boat. It's two hours from Rio by bus and ferry, yet gets a fraction of Ilhabela or Buzios' crowds.

title: Cycle Ibirapuera Park past Sao Paulo's modernist museums
description: Oscar Niemeyer designed the park's curved concrete marquee, the Marquise, and several of the museum buildings inside it. Sunday mornings close it to cars entirely for cyclists and rollerbladers, the liveliest time to visit.

title: Eat a mortadella sandwich the size of your head at Mercado Municipal
description: The market's Bar do Mane mortadella sandwich, stacked with a quarter-kilo of meat, has been the signature order for decades and draws a queue by 11am. The stained-glass windows upstairs depicting rural harvest scenes are worth the neck ache.

title: Sail between waterfalls and beaches around Ilhabela
description: Ilhabela is almost entirely covered by Atlantic Forest reserve, with over 30 waterfalls tumbling down to its beaches, several reachable only by boat. It's also Brazil's sailing capital, hosting national regattas most of the summer.

title: Walk the colonial cobblestones of Salvador's Pelourinho
description: The pastel-coloured colonial core takes its name from the whipping post that once stood in its main square, a brutal reminder that Salvador was the largest slave port in the Americas. That same history built Bahia's Afro-Brazilian culture, which is now what the neighbourhood is loudest about celebrating.

title: Watch a capoeira roda play out in a Pelourinho square
description: Developed by enslaved Africans and disguised as dance to evade a ban on martial arts, capoeira is still practised in informal street circles most evenings around Pelourinho. Drop a few reais in the hat if you stop to watch - most circles are semi-professional and this is their income.

title: Trek to the blue grotto pools of Chapada Diamantina
description: The park's Poco Encantado cave has a beam of midday sunlight hitting crystal-clear water so precisely that it only lights up the full 60m depth for part of the year. Cachoeira da Fumaca, one of Brazil's tallest waterfalls, disperses into mist before it hits the ground.

title: Island-hop by boat to the car-free village of Morro de Sao Paulo
description: No cars or paved roads reach the village - everything moves by wheelbarrow cart from the pier. Its five numbered beaches get progressively quieter the further you walk from the lighthouse, with the fourth and fifth practically empty on weekdays.

title: Visit rescued sea turtles at the Praia do Forte conservation project
description: Projeto Tamar started here in 1982 and is credited with pulling several Brazilian sea turtle species back from the edge of extinction; the on-site pools let you see species you won't spot snorkelling. Nesting season runs September to March if you want a chance at hatchlings.

title: Base yourself in the hillside village of Vale do Capao
description: A dirt-road village of artisans and trekking guides at the edge of Chapada Diamantina, popular with Brazilians long before international tourists found the park's waterfalls. It's the quieter, cheaper base camp compared to Lencois, the town most tours default to.

title: Get soaked at the Devil's Throat walkway on the Brazilian side
description: Brazil's side of the falls has only about 20% of the total drop but the best panoramic view, a single trail ending on a walkway that puts you directly above the Devil's Throat's spray. Bring a dry bag - the mist here is heavier than a light rain.

title: Walk through free-flying toucan aviaries at Parque das Aves
description: Unlike most bird parks, several enclosures here are walk-through, so toucans, macaws and hummingbirds fly at head height around visitors. It sits right across from the falls entrance, easy to pair with the same morning.

title: Tour the turbine hall of the Itaipu hydroelectric dam
description: For decades Itaipu was the largest hydroelectric plant on earth and still supplies close to 90% of Paraguay's electricity from a dam shared between the two countries. The special technical tour goes inside the turbine floor, well beyond what the standard panoramic visit shows.

title: Boat the rivers of Porto Jofre for the best jaguar odds in the Pantanal
description: This stretch of the Cuiaba and Piquiri rivers has one of the highest densities of wild jaguars on the planet, with sightings odds during dry season running well above 90% for a multi-day stay. Boats are the only way in - there's no road once the Transpantaneira ends.

title: Drive the wildlife-lined dirt of the Transpantaneira Highway
description: A raised dirt road built over more than 120 wooden bridges, many left unrepaired for years, so punctures and washouts are part of the trip. Caimans sun themselves on the verges in such numbers that after the first hour you stop stopping the car for them.

title: Snorkel the transparent rivers of Bonito
description: Limestone filters the rivers here to near-swimming-pool clarity, and the Rio da Prata float lets you drift face-down over fish for over a kilometre without swimming a stroke. Access to every river is by permit through a licensed operator; there's no independent version of this.

title: Descend into the electric-blue cave lake of Gruta do Lago Azul
description: The underground lake's blue is most intense between roughly November and February, when sunlight hits the water at the right angle through the cave mouth. Access is capped by timed groups to protect the formations, so book the slot rather than showing up.

title: Swim in a rain-fed lagoon among the white dunes of Lencois Maranhenses
description: The 'sheets' are pure white sand dunes with no vegetation, and the turquoise lagoons only fill between roughly June and September - visit in November and the same view is just dry sand. Locals will tell you which lagoon is deepest that week; it changes.

title: Reach the remote Lagoa Bonita by 4x4 deep inside the dune field
description: Getting past the easy-access lagoons near Barreirinhas to Lagoa Bonita means a rough multi-hour 4x4 crossing or a multi-day trekking traverse from Atins. The reward is a lagoon most day-trippers never reach, without the crowds of the postcard viewpoint.

title: Watch the Rio Negro and Amazon run side by side, unmixed, at the Meeting of the Waters
description: The black, acidic Rio Negro and the pale, sediment-heavy Solimoes run side by side for several kilometres without blending, a difference in temperature, speed and density that's visible as a sharp line straight off the boat. Boats idle right on the seam so you can put one hand in each colour.

title: See an opera inside the jungle-bound Teatro Amazonas
description: Rubber barons shipped Italian marble, French ironwork and Murano glass upriver to build this opera house in 1896, at a time when Manaus had no road link to the rest of Brazil. It still hosts a real season, not just a tourist facade - check the calendar before assuming it's a daytime-only visit.

title: Spend a night in a jungle lodge upriver from Manaus
description: Lodges here run night caiman-spotting trips and canopy tower sunrises, and high-water season (roughly May to July) lets boats push directly into the flooded forest between tree trunks. Low water months instead open up beach camping on exposed river sandbars.

title: Join Manaus locals on the river beach at Ponta Negra in dry season
description: The Rio Negro drops enough between roughly August and November to expose a genuine sand beach right in the city, packed with locals rather than tourists. In high water months the same spot disappears entirely underwater.

title: Snorkel Baia dos Porcos on Fernando de Noronha
description: A daily environmental fee plus a visitor cap keep the island's waters some of the clearest in Brazil, with sea turtles visible from the shoreline most days. August to December brings the calmest, clearest water for snorkelling before the swell picks up.

title: Climb down the cliff staircase to Praia do Sancho
description: Repeatedly voted Brazil's best beach, it's reached by a steep staircase through a crack in the cliff face, not a road. Numbers are capped daily by the park, so arriving right at opening avoids the wait to descend.

title: Watch the sunset from Recife's Marco Zero square
description: Built on reclaimed land at the mouth of the Capibaribe river, the square marks the point the Portuguese first landed in 1535. The Instituto Ricardo Brennand nearby holds one of the largest collections of medieval armour and Dutch colonial art outside Europe, an odd but genuine detour.

title: Wander Olinda's hillside cobblestones during frevo carnival
description: Olinda's carnival runs on frevo, a frenetic brass-band style that requires no couple or samba steps, and giant papier-mache figures parade through streets too narrow and steep for floats. Outside carnival, the same hillside gives the best photo of Recife's skyline across the bay.

title: Climb Ouro Preto's baroque church steps built on gold-rush wealth
description: The town funded some of Brazil's finest baroque architecture, much of it carved by the sculptor Aleijadinho, on wealth from a gold rush so intense an estimated sixth of the world's gold passed through here in the 1700s. The steep streets are cobbled in the original stone; heels are a mistake.

title: Walk contemporary art pavilions set inside a botanical garden at Inhotim
description: Each major artwork gets its own purpose-built pavilion scattered through 140 hectares of landscaped gardens, so seeing it properly means a full day of walking or a golf-cart shuttle. It's one of the largest open-air contemporary art centres in the world, and most international visitors have never heard of it.

title: Tour Niemeyer's modernist Cathedral and Congress in Brasilia
description: The entire city was built from scratch in under four years and opened in 1960, laid out in the shape of an airplane or a bow depending who you ask at the viewing platform. The Cathedral's crown of concrete columns looks crushed by weight until you're standing directly underneath, where it suddenly opens into light.

title: Watch sunset from the dune at Jericoacoara
description: Locals gather on Duna do Por do Sol every clear evening and applaud when the sun drops, a ritual as reliable as the one on Ipanema's rocks. Jericoacoara only got paved road access in 2015; before that the whole town existed at the end of a sand track.

title: Ride a buggy over the red-and-white cliffs of Canoa Quebrada
description: The cliffs here are streaked red, white and ochre from mineral bands, and buggy drivers use them as a launch point for the labirinto dune trails further along the coast. Kitesurfers take over the same stretch of coastline once the trade winds pick up around August.

title: Surf the sandboard dunes and swell of Joaquina Beach
description: Joaquina hosts Brazil's national surf championship most years, and the dunes right behind the beach double as a sandboarding spot on flat days. The island of Florianopolis has over 40 beaches, each with a different personality, from this surf break to family-calm coves on the other coast.

title: Paddleboard the lagoon at Lagoa da Conceicao at sunset
description: The lagoon splits Florianopolis island in two and turns into the social centre of town after dark, ringed by bars that spill onto the sand. Stand-up paddleboard rental stands line the shore and stay open well past sunset in high summer.

title: Watch a tango unfold at a San Telmo milonga
description: San Telmo is where tango is generally agreed to have started, in the brothels and docks of the late 1800s, and the neighbourhood still runs open milongas where anyone can dance, not just paid performers. Sunday's antiques street fair on Defensa is the daytime version of the same neighbourhood energy.

title: Get lost among the marble mausoleums of Recoleta Cemetery
description: Laid out like a miniature city of streets and avenues, it holds over 6,400 elaborate tombs including Eva Peron's, tucked in a modest family vault rather than the grand monument most visitors expect. A resident cat colony has lived among the graves for decades and has its own informal caretakers.

title: Stand where Argentina's history keeps happening, Plaza de Mayo
description: The Madres de Plaza de Mayo still circle the square every Thursday afternoon, a protest tradition started in 1977 demanding answers about children disappeared under the military dictatorship. The pink Casa Rosada behind them gets its colour, by one account, from a 19th-century mix of whitewash and bull's blood.

title: Photograph the corrugated-tin colour of Caminito in La Boca
description: Dock workers originally painted their houses in leftover ship paint, whatever colour was on hand, which is how the clashing rainbow look started. Stick to the pedestrian street itself and the few blocks around La Bombonera stadium; the surrounding barrio has a rougher reputation after dark.

title: Order a full parrillada at a Buenos Aires steakhouse
description: Argentina eats more beef per capita than almost anywhere on earth, and a parrillada mixta brings a share plate of cuts most visitors have never tried, chinchulines and morcilla included. Order it medium-rare (a punto) or the kitchen will assume you want it well done, the local default.

title: Tour the gold-leaf interior of Teatro Colon opera house
description: Acoustically it's ranked among the five best opera houses on earth, a reputation built on marble shipped from Europe and decades of construction that ran from 1889 to 1908. Same-day cheap standing tickets (tertulia) are sold for evening performances if the guided day tour isn't enough.

title: Browse shelves stacked on a converted theatre's stage at El Ateneo
description: The building opened as a 1919 theatre and cinema before being converted into a bookstore in 2000, keeping its frescoed ceiling, opera boxes and red stage curtain intact. The old stage is now a cafe, worth the coffee just to sit under the dome.

title: Watch gauchos race horses at the Feria de Mataderos folk fair
description: Out past the western edge of the city where the old cattle yards used to be, this weekend fair pulls in folk dancers, gaucho horsemanship displays and regional food stalls almost entirely for a local crowd. It's a 40-minute bus or taxi from downtown and worlds away from anything San Telmo sells tourists.

title: Watch chunks calve off Perito Moreno Glacier from the boardwalks
description: It's one of the few glaciers on earth still advancing rather than retreating, and the ice face regularly cracks and drops slabs the size of buildings into the lake with a boom you feel before you hear it. The metal walkway system gives multiple viewing levels without a hike required.

title: Strap on crampons and walk the blue ice of Perito Moreno
description: A short boat crossing gets you onto the glacier itself for a guided walk between crevasses, finishing most tours with a whisky poured over glacier ice. Bigger 'ice trekking' routes go further onto the surface than the standard 'mini trekking' option, at extra cost and fitness required.

title: Hike to Laguna de los Tres beneath Mount Fitz Roy
description: The final kilometre is a steep, exposed scramble that regularly turns hikers back in high wind, but it opens onto the postcard view of Fitz Roy's granite spires reflected in a turquoise glacial lake. The trailhead starts directly from El Chalten, no transport needed and no entry fee, unusual for a park this famous.

title: Trek to the Cerro Torre lookout over Laguna Torre
description: Cerro Torre's near-vertical granite spire, often capped by a mushroom of rime ice, was one of the last major peaks in the world to be climbed, and disputed claims over the first ascent ran for decades. The trail is gentler than the Fitz Roy hike, making it the better call on a low-visibility day.

title: Base yourself in Argentina's trekking capital, El Chalten
description: Founded only in 1985, largely to help Argentina's territorial claim against Chile in the area, the town exists almost entirely to service trekkers heading into Los Glaciares National Park. Every trail starts free and unguided right from town, a rarity worth building a multi-day stay around.

title: Get your passport stamped at the end of the world in Ushuaia
description: Ushuaia markets itself hard as 'Fin del Mundo', and the tourist office sells a novelty passport stamp to prove you made it. It's also the main departure point for Antarctica cruises, so the harbour often has a genuine icebreaker or expedition ship docked alongside the fishing boats.

title: Ride the End of the World Train into Tierra del Fuego National Park
description: The narrow-gauge steam train was built in 1902 to haul timber cut by convict labour from the nearby prison, and it now runs a short scenic stretch purely for tourists. Get off partway and hike the rest of the park's coastal trail instead of riding the full loop back.

title: Cruise the Beagle Channel past sea lions and the Lighthouse at the End of the World
description: Named after Darwin's ship, the channel splits Argentina and Chile and its small rocky islands are packed with sea lion colonies and cormorant nests. Full-day versions add a landing on Bridges Island for a short walk and hot chocolate rather than just a photo pass of the lighthouse.

title: Hike up to Martial Glacier for the view back down over Ushuaia
description: A chairlift cuts out the first stretch of the climb, leaving a rougher scramble up scree to the glacier face itself. In winter the same slope becomes Ushuaia's small in-town ski area, unusual for a glacier hike anywhere else in the world.

title: Walk the catwalk over the Devil's Throat on the Argentine side
description: A long metal walkway crosses the Iguazu River directly above the point where 14 separate falls converge, putting you at the rim looking straight down rather than across at it like the Brazilian viewpoint. The park's little train saves the twenty-minute walk to the trailhead if you're short on time.

title: Take the boat under the base of the falls on the Gran Aventura
description: The boat drives directly into the spray at the base of the San Martin falls, close enough that ponchos are handed out but everyone gets soaked regardless. It's a separate ticket and trail system, the Lower and Upper Circuits, from the Devil's Throat walkway, so budget a full day to do both properly.

title: Walk the red sandstone ruins of the San Ignacio Mini Jesuit mission
description: Founded in 1610, this was one of over 30 Jesuit reductions built to convert and protect Guarani communities before the order was expelled in 1767 and the jungle reclaimed most of them. An evening light-and-sound show projected onto the ruins runs most nights, telling the mission's history across the stonework itself.

title: Cycle between Malbec wineries in Mendoza's Lujan de Cuyo
description: Mendoza's high-altitude desert vineyards, most over 900m, are what give Argentine Malbec its intensity, and Lujan de Cuyo and the Uco Valley are dense enough with bodegas to cycle between tastings. Harvest season, roughly late February to April, adds grape-stomping festivals on top of the usual tastings.

title: Look up at Aconcagua, the tallest peak outside the Himalayas
description: At 6,961m it's the highest mountain in both the western and southern hemispheres, and the Confluencia viewpoint trail gets you a proper look at it without needing the multi-week expedition permit serious climbers require. Around 3,000 people attempt the summit each season; roughly a third make it.

title: Rent a bike and wobble between Maipu's family wineries
description: Maipu is close enough to Mendoza city for a bike-and-wine day trip without a driver, with small family bodegas, an olive oil mill and an absinthe distillery all within pedalling distance of each other. Pace the tastings; several visitors a year genuinely do fall off on the ride back.

title: See the sulphur-stained natural bridge at Puente del Inca
